Mirena IUD insertion performed. Patient tolerated procedure well with mild cramping. Ibuprofen 600mg given 1 hour prior. Strings visualized at cervical os, trimmed to 3cm. Post-insertion ultrasound confirms proper fundal placement. Counseled on expected irregular bleeding/spotting for first 3-6 months with likely significant reduction in menstrual flow thereafter. Combined OCP discontinued. Return in 6 weeks for string check.

Follow-up iron deficiency anemia. Patient on ferrous sulfate 325mg BID for 8 weeks now and Mirena placed November. Reports improved energy. Hgb 12.1 g/dL (up from 10.2), MCV 78 fL, ferritin 22 ng/mL (improving). Continue iron supplementation for additional 3 months to replete stores (target ferritin >50). Menstrual flow already lighter per patient.

Follow-up. Hgb 13.4 g/dL, ferritin 56 ng/mL. Iron stores repleted. Discontinue ferrous sulfate. Menstrual periods now very light with Mirena. Atopic dermatitis controlled with tacrolimus maintenance. No other concerns. BMI 21.8, BP 112/70. All well.

Self-referred for evaluation of anxiety and low mood following a difficult breakup 2 months ago. Reports poor sleep (initial insomnia), decreased appetite, loss of interest in hobbies, difficulty concentrating at work. No SI/HI. No prior psychiatric history. PHQ-9 score 12 (moderate depression), GAD-7 score 10 (moderate anxiety). Diagnosis: adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood. Recommended psychotherapy (CBT) as first line. Patient prefers to try therapy before medication. Referral to psychologist placed. Follow up in 6 weeks.

Follow-up adjustment disorder. Patient has been attending CBT weekly for 3 months. Reports significant improvement: sleeping better, appetite normalized, re-engaging with friends and activities. PHQ-9 score 5, GAD-7 score 4. Continue therapy, plan to taper to biweekly sessions. No medication needed at this time. Good prognosis.

Annual visit. Mirena IUD in place, strings palpable. Minimal menstrual spotting only. No pelvic pain. Breast exam normal. Pap not due until 2022. Patient reports she and new partner considering pregnancy in next 1-2 years. Discussed timeline: IUD removal when ready to conceive, start prenatal vitamins with folic acid 800mcg 3 months prior to planned conception. Reviewed preconception counseling including avoidance of alcohol, smoking (patient is nonsmoker/nondrinker).

Follow-up atopic dermatitis. Flare on bilateral hands, dorsal surfaces, likely triggered by cold weather and frequent handwashing. Fissuring noted on several fingertips. Prescribed triamcinolone 0.1% ointment to hands BID x 2 weeks, then tacrolimus maintenance. Cotton glove occlusion at night recommended. Discussed barrier repair strategy. Patch testing not indicated at this time as distribution consistent with AD rather than contact dermatitis.

Patient presents for IUD removal and preconception visit. Mirena removed without difficulty. Started prenatal vitamin with folic acid 800mcg daily 2 months ago. Rubella immune per prior records. Varicella immune. Pap smear performed (due 2022, slightly overdue). TSH ordered. No chronic medications. Atopic dermatitis — counseled on pregnancy-safe moisturizers and limited topical steroid use. Expect return of menses within 1-3 months. Advised to begin attempting conception after first normal cycle.

Patient presents with positive home pregnancy test. LMP 6/5/2023. Transvaginal ultrasound shows intrauterine gestational sac with yolk sac, CRL 5mm consistent with 6w2d. Fetal cardiac activity present at 118 bpm. Estimated due date 3/11/2024. Initial prenatal labs ordered: CBC, blood type/Rh/antibody screen, rubella, hepatitis B, HIV, RPR, UA/culture, GC/chlamydia. Patient elated. Prenatal vitamins continued. First trimester screening discussed and scheduled. Return in 4 weeks.

10-week prenatal visit. Prenatal labs all normal: blood type A+, antibody screen negative, rubella immune, HBsAg negative, HIV negative, RPR nonreactive. Hgb 12.8 g/dL, good given prior history of iron deficiency. Mild nausea managed with ginger and small frequent meals. BP 108/66. Weight gain 1 lb, appropriate. NT scan and first trimester screening scheduled for 12 weeks. Discussed NIPT as optional; patient elects NIPT.

12-week visit. NT scan: 1.2mm (normal). NIPT results: low risk for trisomy 21, 18, 13. Fetal sex: female. Patient and partner very happy. Nausea improving. BP 110/68. Fundal height not yet measurable. Fetal heart tones 156 bpm by Doppler. Atopic dermatitis flare on arms — advised CeraVe moisturizer and limited low-potency hydrocortisone. Next visit at 16 weeks. Anatomy scan scheduled for 20 weeks.

20-week anatomy scan. All fetal structures within normal limits. EFW 368g, 45th percentile. Normal amniotic fluid volume. Anterior placenta, not previa. Cervical length 3.8cm (normal). Patient feeling fetal movement. BP 112/70. Weight gain 10 lbs total, appropriate. Hgb 11.9, monitoring closely given iron deficiency history. Started prophylactic low-dose iron supplementation (ferrous sulfate 325mg daily). Glucose challenge test scheduled at 24-28 weeks.

28-week visit. 1-hour GCT: 118 mg/dL (normal, cutoff 140). Hgb 11.6 on iron supplementation. Rh positive, so RhoGAM not indicated. BP 114/72. Fundal height 28cm, appropriate. Fetal heart tones 148 bpm. Tdap vaccine administered. Patient reports mild low back pain and bilateral ankle swelling at end of day, both common in third trimester. Reviewed kick counts. Visits now every 2 weeks.

47 y/o male presenting for executive health physical. No significant PMH. Family history: father died of MI at age 58, mother alive with T2DM. No allergies. Social history: drinks 2-3 beers most nights, denies tobacco, exercises sporadically. BP 136/88, HR 78, BMI 28.9. Abdominal exam reveals mild hepatomegaly. Comprehensive labs ordered including CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c, hepatic panel, GGT. ECG: NSR, no abnormalities.

Lab results: A1c 5.6%, fasting glucose 104. Lipids: TC 238, LDL 156, HDL 39, TG 215. AST 52, ALT 68 (both elevated), GGT 98 (elevated), albumin 4.0. CBC and renal function normal. Lipid panel and LFTs concerning. Given strong family history of premature CAD, high LDL, low HDL, and elevated TG, 10-yr ASCVD risk calculated at 9.8%. Started atorvastatin 20mg daily. Strongly counseled on alcohol reduction — elevated LFTs likely related to alcohol and/or NAFLD. Abdominal ultrasound ordered. Return in 6 weeks.

Abdominal ultrasound results: hepatic steatosis (fatty liver), no focal lesions, normal biliary system. Consistent with NAFLD given BMI and alcohol use. Patient reports has reduced alcohol to 2-3 drinks per week. Repeat LFTs: AST 38, ALT 45, GGT 62, trending down. BP 132/84 — lifestyle modifications discussed before starting antihypertensive. Weight loss program recommended. Target: lose 15 lbs over next 6 months. Lipids to be rechecked at 3 months on statin.

3-month follow-up. Weight 206 lbs (down 5 from 211). BP 130/82. Lipids on atorvastatin 20mg: TC 192, LDL 112, HDL 43, TG 185. LDL improved but not at goal <100 given high risk. Increased atorvastatin to 40mg. LFTs normalizing: AST 32, ALT 38. Patient reports alcohol now limited to weekends only. Encouraged continued weight loss and exercise. Coronary artery calcium score discussed given family history; patient agrees. Ordered CAC scan.

Coronary artery calcium scoring requested by PCP given strong family history of premature CAD. CAC score: 85 Agatston units (75th percentile for age/sex/race). Moderate coronary calcification indicating subclinical atherosclerosis. This reclassifies patient to higher risk category. Recommend aggressive lipid management targeting LDL <70. Aspirin 81mg daily appropriate. Stress testing not indicated in asymptomatic patient at this time. Lifestyle modification critical. Results communicated to Dr. Lindstrom.

Follow-up to discuss CAC score results. CAC 85 places patient at elevated cardiovascular risk despite age 48. Given reclassification, increased atorvastatin to 80mg daily (max dose) targeting LDL <70. Added aspirin 81mg daily per cardiology recommendation. BP today 134/86 — given persistent borderline HTN and high CV risk, starting lisinopril 10mg daily. Comprehensive dietary counseling provided. Referred to dietitian. Patient highly motivated given family history.

Follow-up. Weight 198 lbs, down 13 lbs total. BP 122/76 on lisinopril 10mg. Lipids on atorvastatin 80mg: TC 158, LDL 74, HDL 46, TG 150. LDL near goal. LFTs now normal: AST 24, ALT 28. NAFLD likely improving with weight loss and alcohol reduction. Patient exercising 4x/week, mostly eliminated weekday alcohol. Excellent progress. Continue current regimen.

Annual visit. Weight 195 lbs, BMI 26.4. BP 118/74. A1c 5.3%, improved. Lipids: LDL 68, at goal. HDL 48, TG 138. LFTs normal. Patient has maintained lifestyle changes. Alcohol use minimal (1-2 drinks/week socially). Reports new bilateral shoulder stiffness in mornings, lasting 10-15 minutes. ROM slightly limited bilaterally on exam. Likely age-related periarthritis vs early OA. Recommend stretching, NSAIDs PRN. No imaging needed at this time.

Referred by PCP for evaluation of progressive bilateral hearing loss noticed over past year. Patient reports difficulty hearing conversations in noisy environments and frequently asks people to repeat themselves. Audiometry shows bilateral symmetric sensorineural hearing loss, mild-moderate, predominantly high-frequency (4-8kHz). Speech recognition scores 84% bilaterally. No tinnitus or vertigo. Consistent with age-related hearing loss (presbycusis), though onset somewhat early at age 49 — may be noise-related given history of concert attendance without hearing protection. Discussed hearing aid options. Patient prefers to monitor for now. Annual audiogram recommended.

Annual visit. Weight stable at 196 lbs. BP 120/76. All labs excellent: LDL 65, A1c 5.2%, LFTs normal. NAFLD likely resolved or significantly improved. Liver US repeat not urgently needed given normal LFTs and weight loss. Shoulder stiffness improved with stretching routine. Hearing loss stable per patient; declined hearing aids. Discussed age-appropriate cancer screening: colonoscopy due at 50 (next year given updated USPSTF guidelines recommending screening at 45); scheduled. PSA screening discussed; patient defers.

Screening colonoscopy at age 50. Prep excellent. Cecum reached, terminal ileum intubated. Colon entirely normal, no polyps or masses identified. Normal vascular pattern throughout. Recommend repeat in 10 years. Results communicated to PCP.

Annual visit. Weight 194 lbs, BMI 26.3. BP 116/72. Labs: LDL 62, HDL 50, TG 128, A1c 5.1%, CMP unremarkable. Patient maintaining excellent lifestyle changes for 3+ years now. Colonoscopy normal. Cardiovascular risk well managed. No new concerns. Discussion about stress testing given CAC score history and approaching age 52; cardiology follow-up recommended for reassessment.

Follow-up from 2019 CAC score of 85. Patient now 51, asymptomatic, excellent risk factor control: LDL 62, BP 116/72, nonsmoker, regular exercise. On atorvastatin 80mg, lisinopril 10mg, aspirin 81mg. Exercise stress test performed: achieved 12.1 METs, Bruce protocol stage 4. No chest pain, no ischemic ECG changes. Excellent functional capacity. Continue current medical therapy. No further imaging needed unless symptoms develop. Annual PCP follow-up sufficient.

Annual visit. Age 52. Weight 192 lbs. BP 118/72. All labs at goal. Stress test from October normal. Patient remains committed to exercise (runs 3x/week, strength training 2x/week). Hearing loss: now notices more difficulty, willing to consider hearing aids. Re-referred to ENT. No other concerns. Flu vaccine administered.

Follow-up audiometry: bilateral SNHL progressed slightly, now moderate at 4-8kHz. Speech recognition 78% right, 80% left. Patient now motivated for amplification given workplace difficulties. Fitted for bilateral receiver-in-canal hearing aids. Real-ear measurements performed with appropriate gain targets. Patient reports immediate improvement in clarity. Follow-up in 2 weeks for fine-tuning. Counseled on acclimatization period of 4-6 weeks.

53 y/o female referred for management of poorly controlled T2DM. Diagnosed 8 years ago. Currently on metformin 1000mg BID and glipizide 10mg BID. A1c 8.9%. BMI 34.6. Reports frequent hypoglycemic episodes in the afternoon, often skips lunch due to work schedule. Fasting glucose today 186 mg/dL. Allergy: penicillin (rash). Family history: both parents with T2DM. Microvascular screening: last eye exam 6 months ago showed no retinopathy. Urine microalbumin/creatinine ratio 45 (mildly elevated). Plan: discontinue glipizide given hypoglycemia risk. Start semaglutide 0.25mg SC weekly, titrate to 0.5mg after 4 weeks for glycemic control and weight loss benefit. Continue metformin. Reinforce meal regularity. Recheck A1c in 3 months.

Follow-up T2DM. On metformin 1000mg BID and semaglutide 0.5mg SC weekly (titrated up from 0.25mg). A1c 8.0%, down from 8.9%. FBG 148. Weight down 6 lbs to 208 lbs. No hypoglycemia since stopping glipizide. Mild nausea with semaglutide, improving. Tolerating well overall. Increase semaglutide to 1mg weekly. Repeat urine albumin: 38. Continue ACE inhibitor discussion with PCP for renal protection. Recheck A1c in 3 months.

Visit to coordinate care per endocrinology recommendation. Patient has T2DM with microalbuminuria. Currently on lisinopril 10mg for HTN (BP 132/82). Given microalbuminuria, increased lisinopril to 20mg for renal protection. BP goal <130/80. Also addressed: overdue mammogram and colon cancer screening. Referrals placed. Penicillin allergy noted. Continue metformin and semaglutide per endocrine.

A1c 7.3%, significant improvement from 8.9% at baseline. Weight 201 lbs, down 13 lbs total. No hypoglycemia. Nausea resolved on semaglutide 1mg weekly. FBG 128. Urine albumin/creatinine 32, improving on lisinopril 20mg. Excellent progress. Continue current regimen. Consider adding SGLT2 inhibitor if A1c does not reach <7% by next visit for additional cardiorenal benefit. Recheck in 3 months.

A1c 6.9%, at goal. Weight 196 lbs, BMI 32.0. Excellent response to semaglutide + metformin. Urine albumin 28, trending toward normal. eGFR 78, stable. Given continued microalbuminuria and CV risk, adding empagliflozin 10mg daily for additive renal and cardiac benefit. Penicillin allergy documented. Continue metformin and semaglutide. Return in 6 months if stable.

Presenting with chronic left knee pain for past 4 months, worsening with stairs and prolonged walking. BMI 31.5 contributing to mechanical stress. X-ray: moderate medial compartment joint space narrowing with osteophytes, consistent with OA. No effusion on exam. Started physical therapy referral, topical diclofenac gel BID, and weight-bearing activity modification. Weight loss will be critical for symptom management. Discussed potential for intra-articular injections if conservative measures fail. Avoid oral NSAIDs given renal considerations.

Annual wellness visit. BP 126/78 on lisinopril 20mg. Weight 192 lbs, continued slow loss. A1c 6.7% per recent endocrine visit. Mammogram performed: BI-RADS 2, benign findings. Colonoscopy completed last month: 2 hyperplastic polyps removed, repeat in 10 years. Knee OA managed conservatively. Mood good. PHQ-2 negative. Flu vaccine administered.

6-month follow-up. A1c 6.5%. Weight 188 lbs, BMI 30.7. Outstanding progress — 26 lbs total weight loss since starting semaglutide. Urine albumin/creatinine now 18, normalized. eGFR 80. Continue metformin 1000mg BID, semaglutide 1mg weekly, empagliflozin 10mg daily. No medication side effects. Eye exam up to date, no retinopathy. Foot exam: monofilament intact bilaterally, pulses palpable. Next visit 6 months.

Presenting with hyperpigmented, velvety plaques in axillae and posterior neck. Classic appearance of acanthosis nigricans associated with insulin resistance. Also noted small skin tags in axillae. Patient aware of association with diabetes. Reassured that these may improve with continued weight loss and improved insulin sensitivity. Removed 4 skin tags by snip excision. Ammonium lactate 12% lotion to affected areas BID for cosmetic improvement. No biopsy needed.

Annual visit. BP 124/76. Weight 184 lbs, BMI 30.1. Approaching normal BMI range. Labs: A1c 6.4%, CMP unremarkable, eGFR 82, lipids — LDL 94, HDL 54, TG 140. Not currently on statin. 10-yr ASCVD risk 8.2% with DM factored in. Per ACC/AHA guidelines, all DM patients 40-75 should be on moderate-intensity statin. Started atorvastatin 20mg daily. COVID-19 vaccine series completed (Pfizer). Flu shot given.

Routine DM follow-up. A1c 6.3%, stable. Weight 182 lbs. No hypoglycemia. All renal markers normal. Patient doing extremely well. Discussed potential for reducing medications if weight loss continues. However, semaglutide provides cardiorenal benefit beyond glycemic control, so recommend continuing. Empagliflozin also continued for cardiorenal benefit. Foot exam normal. Annual eye exam reminder sent. Return in 6 months.

Follow-up left knee OA. Patient reports significant improvement with 30+ lb weight loss, now only occasional discomfort after long walks. ROM improved. Crepitus present but less symptomatic. No longer using topical diclofenac regularly. Physical therapy completed, continues home exercise program. No indication for injection or surgical intervention at this time. Return PRN.

Annual visit. Age 58. BP 120/74. Weight 178 lbs, BMI 29.1. A1c 6.2%. Lipids on atorvastatin 20mg: LDL 72, HDL 58, TG 118. Renal function normal, microalbuminuria resolved. Knee OA improved. Acanthosis nigricans less prominent per patient. Comprehensive metabolic panel unremarkable. Truly remarkable turnaround in metabolic health over past 4 years. Continue all current medications. Mammogram scheduled.

Routine DM follow-up. 60 y/o female, T2DM diagnosed ~2011 (15 years). On metformin 1000mg BID, semaglutide 1mg weekly, empagliflozin 10mg daily (since Oct 2019). Lisinopril 20mg daily since May 2019. No MRA. BP 122/74. Weight 180 lbs. A1c 6.3%. Labs Jan 13: Cr 0.78, eGFR 87, K 4.2. Urine albumin/creatinine 14 mg/g — remains normal. No CKD: earlier microalbuminuria resolved (normal since 2021), no diabetic kidney disease at present. No hypoglycemia. Foot exam: monofilament intact, pulses palpable. Eye exam Nov 2025: no retinopathy. Continue all current medications including atorvastatin 20mg. Penicillin allergy documented. Return in 6 months.

40 y/o male presents to ED with acute onset severe headache, worst of his life, rated 10/10, with neck stiffness and photophobia. Onset 2 hours ago during exercise. No trauma. No prior headache history. BP 162/98, HR 88, temp 98.8F, neuro exam nonfocal. Stat CT head without contrast: negative for hemorrhage. Given high clinical suspicion for SAH despite negative CT, LP performed: opening pressure 18 cmH2O, RBC count tube 1: 12,000, tube 4: 11,500 (no clearing), xanthochromia positive. Diagnosis: subarachnoid hemorrhage. CTA head/neck ordered urgently. Neurosurgery consulted. Nimodipine 60mg q4h started for vasospasm prophylaxis. Admitted to neuro ICU.

Neuro ICU day 1. CTA reveals 4mm saccular aneurysm at left posterior communicating artery origin, likely source of SAH. Hunt-Hess grade 2, Fisher grade 3. Patient alert, oriented, GCS 15 but with headache and nuchal rigidity. Interventional neuroradiology consulted for endovascular coiling vs neurosurgical clipping. Given aneurysm location and size, endovascular coiling recommended. Procedure scheduled for tomorrow. Nimodipine continued. Strict BP control with IV nicardipine targeting SBP 120-140. Serial neuro checks q1h.

Post-coiling day 0. Endovascular coiling of left PComm aneurysm performed successfully via femoral artery approach. Complete occlusion achieved. No procedural complications. Patient neurologically intact post-procedure, GCS 15. Maintained in neuro ICU for vasospasm monitoring. Transcranial Dopplers initiated daily. Continue nimodipine x 21 days. IV fluids for euvolemia. Pain management with acetaminophen and low-dose hydromorphone PRN. Stool softeners to avoid straining.

Hospital day 8. Patient stable, headache gradually improving. Transcranial Dopplers day 7 show mildly elevated velocities in left MCA (130 cm/s) concerning for early vasospasm. Increased IV fluids. Repeat TCD tomorrow. Neurologically unchanged — no focal deficits, oriented x 3. Transitioned to ward from ICU on day 6. Nimodipine continued. Physical therapy initiated for deconditioning. Planning discharge in 2-3 days if vasospasm trend improves. Counseled patient on activity restrictions for 6 weeks.

Discharge summary. Hospital day 11 post-SAH. TCD velocities normalized. No clinical vasospasm occurred. Patient ambulating independently, headache controlled with acetaminophen. Discharge medications: nimodipine 60mg q4h (to complete 21-day course), acetaminophen 1g q6h PRN, docusate 100mg BID. Activity restrictions: no heavy lifting, strenuous exercise, or driving for 6 weeks. Follow-up: neurology 2 weeks, CTA 6 months to assess coil stability. Return to ED for thunderclap headache, new neurologic symptoms, or seizure.

2-week post-discharge follow-up. Headaches now mild and intermittent, no thunderclap recurrence. Completed nimodipine course. Neuro exam nonfocal. Mood slightly low — adjusting to activity restrictions, anxious about recurrence. PHQ-2 score 2. Reassured about low recurrence risk post-coiling. Cleared for light activity; full activity at 6 weeks. Cognitive testing intact. CTA scheduled for October. Return PRN or in 6 months.

6-month follow-up. CTA head: left PComm aneurysm coil mass stable, no residual filling or recurrence. No new aneurysms. Patient fully recovered, returned to work as an architect 3 months post-SAH. No headaches. Exercising regularly again (cleared at 6 weeks). BP 128/80 on no medications. Neuro exam normal. Recommend annual CTA for first 3 years then MRA surveillance. Next imaging October 2020.

40 y/o male, new patient visit post-SAH for primary care establishment. No other PMH. Medications: none currently. Family history: father with HTN. No allergies. BP 132/84, BMI 25.2. Comprehensive labs: CBC normal, CMP normal, lipids — TC 205, LDL 128, HDL 52, TG 125. A1c 5.4%. Given history of SAH and borderline HTN, recommend BP monitoring. If persistently >130/80, will initiate therapy. Lifestyle counseling for CV risk reduction. Annual physical planned.

Annual CTA surveillance: coil mass stable, no recurrence, no new aneurysms. Patient doing well. Occasional mild headaches managed with acetaminophen, likely tension-type. No neurologic symptoms. Continue annual surveillance imaging. Next CTA October 2021 (3-year mark), after which may transition to MRA.

Annual visit. BP 134/86 today, has been 130-138/82-88 on home readings over past 3 months. Meeting criteria for stage 1 HTN. Given SAH history and family history of HTN, starting lisinopril 10mg daily. Target BP <130/80. Lipids: LDL 132. 10-yr ASCVD risk 4.6% — does not meet statin threshold, but with SAH history, will monitor closely. Encouraged dietary sodium reduction and continued regular exercise.

3-year annual surveillance. CTA head: coil mass stable and well-packed, no residual aneurysm filling. No new aneurysms. Transition to MRA for future surveillance (less radiation, no contrast needed). Next MRA in 2 years (2023). Patient asymptomatic. BP now controlled on lisinopril per PCP.

Annual visit. BP 124/78 on lisinopril 10mg. Labs: LDL 118, improved with diet. A1c 5.3%. eGFR >90. Patient reports occasional low back pain from prolonged desk work. Exam: paraspinal muscle tenderness, no radiculopathy. Advised ergonomic workstation setup and core strengthening exercises. No imaging indicated. Otherwise well.

Annual visit. Age 44. BP 122/76. Weight stable. Labs all normal. LDL 112. Patient very health-conscious since SAH event. Exercises 5x/week, follows DASH diet. MRA scheduled for October per neurology surveillance plan. Colonoscopy recommended given age 45 screening guidelines; referral placed. No complaints.

MRA head: coil mass at left PComm stable. No new aneurysms. 4.5 years post-SAH, excellent outcome. Given stability across multiple imaging studies, recommend extending surveillance interval to every 3 years. Next MRA 2026. Patient in excellent health. Discharged from frequent follow-up; return PRN or per surveillance schedule.

60 y/o Vietnamese American female referred for joint pain, fatigue, and malar rash present intermittently for past 6 months. PMH: recurrent pleurisy episodes x 2. Family history: sister with Sjogren syndrome. Allergies: none. Exam: butterfly-shaped erythematous rash on cheeks sparing nasolabial folds, tender MCP joints bilaterally, no synovitis. Labs ordered: ANA, dsDNA, complement levels, CBC, CMP, UA, ESR, CRP, anti-Smith, anti-SSA/SSB.

Lab results: ANA 1:640 homogeneous pattern, anti-dsDNA 85 IU/mL (elevated), anti-Smith positive, C3 68 (low), C4 10 (low), ESR 42, CRP 1.2. CBC: WBC 3.2 (leukopenia), Hgb 11.4, platelets 138 (low normal). UA: trace protein. Meets ACR/EULAR criteria for systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) — malar rash, serositis history, leukopenia, positive ANA, anti-dsDNA, anti-Smith, low complements. SLEDAI score 10 (moderate activity). Started hydroxychloroquine 200mg BID as foundational therapy. Baseline eye exam referral for HCQ monitoring. Low-dose prednisone 10mg daily for acute symptom control. Spot urine protein/creatinine ratio ordered to evaluate for lupus nephritis.

Follow-up new SLE diagnosis. Spot urine protein/creatinine 0.3 (borderline). eGFR 82. Given proteinuria and active serology, nephrology referral placed for consideration of renal biopsy to evaluate for lupus nephritis. Malar rash improved on prednisone 10mg. Joint pain 60% better. Started calcium and vitamin D supplementation given steroid use. Discussed sun protection (SPF 50+, sun-avoidant clothing) given photosensitivity.

Evaluation for possible lupus nephritis. Spot urine P/C now 0.5, worsened. UA shows 2+ protein, 5-10 RBCs/hpf, RBC casts noted on sediment. eGFR 78. Strongly suggestive of active nephritis. Renal biopsy recommended and performed under ultrasound guidance. Tolerated well, 2-hour post-procedure monitoring normal. Pathology pending. Will communicate results in 1 week.

Renal biopsy results: Class III focal proliferative lupus nephritis (ISN/RPS classification) with activity index 6/24 and chronicity index 1/12. Immunofluorescence: full-house pattern. Electron microscopy: subendothelial and mesangial deposits. Given Class III with moderate activity, recommend induction therapy with mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) 1g BID in addition to hydroxychloroquine and low-dose prednisone. Discussed treatment plan with rheumatology. Patient counseled on importance of contraception while on MMF (teratogenic). BP 128/82; started lisinopril 10mg for renal protection and proteinuria reduction.

Coordinated SLE follow-up. On HCQ 200mg BID, MMF 1g BID, prednisone 7.5mg (tapering), lisinopril 10mg. Labs: anti-dsDNA 42 (down from 85), C3 82 (improving), C4 14, WBC 4.1, Hgb 11.8. Spot urine P/C 0.28, improved. SLEDAI 6, down from 10. Good serologic and clinical response. Continue prednisone taper to 5mg. Baseline ophthalmology exam completed for HCQ monitoring — normal. Flu and pneumococcal vaccines given (inactivated only given immunosuppression). Avoid live vaccines.

6-month post-induction follow-up. Spot urine P/C 0.15, near normal. eGFR 84, stable. UA: trace protein, no RBCs, no casts. Serologies improving per rheumatology. MMF 1g BID well tolerated, no GI side effects. Continue MMF as maintenance therapy for minimum 3-5 years for Class III nephritis. Prednisone now at 5mg daily. Renal function to be monitored every 3 months. Excellent response.

Routine SLE follow-up. Patient stable. SLEDAI 2 (low activity). On HCQ 200mg BID, MMF 1g BID, prednisone 5mg. Labs: dsDNA 28, C3 92, C4 16, CBC normal, CMP normal. No rash, no arthralgia. Prednisone taper to 2.5mg daily, goal to discontinue by next visit if stable. Discussed importance of sun protection with summer approaching. Bone density scan ordered given cumulative steroid exposure.

Follow-up. SLEDAI 0 — clinical and serologic remission on HCQ + MMF. Prednisone discontinued as of 1 month ago. No flare. Labs: dsDNA 18, complements normal, CBC normal, urine P/C 0.1. DEXA scan: T-score -1.3 lumbar spine, -0.9 hip. Osteopenia, likely steroid-related. Start calcium 1200mg + vitamin D3 2000 IU daily. Weight-bearing exercise recommended. Reassess bone density in 2 years. Continue HCQ and MMF maintenance.

Annual HCQ monitoring exam. On hydroxychloroquine 200mg BID (400mg/day) for 2 years. OCT macula: normal retinal thickness bilaterally, no bull's-eye pattern. Visual fields 10-2: no paracentral scotoma. Fundoscopy normal. No evidence of HCQ retinal toxicity. Continue current dose. Annual monitoring recommended given cumulative dose approaching higher risk threshold after 5 years.

Routine follow-up. SLE in sustained remission on HCQ + MMF for over 1 year off prednisone. All serologies normal. Renal function excellent, eGFR 86. Patient reports some fatigue but attributes to pandemic-related stress and poor sleep. PHQ-9 score 6. Discussed sleep hygiene. No evidence of flare. MMF to continue. Consider MMF dose reduction after 3 years of maintenance if remission sustained.

Annual wellness visit. Age 63. BP 124/76 on lisinopril 10mg. BMI 24.8. Labs: A1c 5.4%, lipids — TC 198, LDL 118, HDL 56, TG 120. SLE well controlled per rheumatology. Mammogram: BI-RADS 1, normal. Colonoscopy up to date. Flu vaccine administered (inactivated). COVID booster received last month. General health good despite SLE diagnosis.

SLE follow-up. Remission continues — 3+ years. Discussed MMF dose reduction. Reduced MMF from 1g BID to 750mg BID. Continue HCQ 200mg BID unchanged (cornerstone therapy). Monitor labs closely over next 3 months for any serologic reactivation during taper. dsDNA 15, complements normal, urine P/C 0.08. Counsel patient to report any new rash, joint pain, or fatigue promptly.

3-month check after MMF dose reduction. All serologies stable: dsDNA 16, C3 94, C4 18. CBC normal. Urine P/C 0.09. No clinical symptoms of flare. Continue MMF 750mg BID. Plan to further reduce to 500mg BID in 3 months if stable. HCQ unchanged. Ophthalmology monitoring up to date.

Reduced MMF to 500mg BID 3 months ago. Labs today: dsDNA 22 (slight rise from 16), C3 88 (still normal), C4 16, urine P/C 0.12 (minimal rise). No clinical symptoms. These minor lab fluctuations may represent subclinical activity. Hold MMF at 500mg BID, do not reduce further. Recheck in 6 weeks. If serologies worsen, will increase back to 750mg.

6-week recheck. dsDNA 20, stable. Complements normal. Urine P/C 0.10. No clinical flare. Lab fluctuations appear stable and clinically insignificant. Continue MMF 500mg BID. HCQ 200mg BID. Next routine visit in 3 months. Patient counseled to maintain sun protection with approaching spring/summer.

Annual HCQ monitoring, now on HCQ for 5 years. OCT: minimal parafoveal thinning OD noted, within normal limits but flagged for close monitoring. Visual fields 10-2 normal. Fundoscopy unremarkable. Diet: moderate protein restriction 0.8g/kg/day. Phosphorus and PTH levels normal. Bicarbonate 22 — borderline, monitor. Follow-up 6 months.

Annual visit. 80 y/o. HbA1c 7.2% — relaxed goal <7.5% appropriate given age, CKD, and hypoglycemia risk. eGFR 46. K+ 4.9. BNP 195. Weight stable. NYHA class II, no change. Medications: metformin 500mg BID, lisinopril 20mg, chlorthalidone 12.5mg, furosemide 20mg, spironolactone 12.5mg. DEXA ordered — given age, CKD, diuretic use. Influenza and pneumococcal vaccines given. Advance care planning discussed — patient has durable POA designated (daughter).

80 y/o female brought by daughter for increasing SOB over 3 days, orthopnea (now sleeping on 3 pillows), and bilateral ankle swelling. Weight up 8 lbs from baseline. Vitals: BP 158/82, HR 92, SpO2 88% RA. Exam: JVP elevated, bilateral crackles to mid-lung fields, 3+ pitting edema bilateral LE. BNP 890. CXR: bilateral pleural effusions, pulmonary congestion. Troponin negative. ECG: sinus tach, LVH pattern. Acute decompensated HF. IV furosemide 40mg bolus, O2 via NC. Admitted to telemetry. Nephrology and cardiology consulted.

Inpatient day 3 for acute decompensated HFpEF. Diuresed 6 liters with IV furosemide drip. SpO2 96% RA. Weight down to near baseline. Crackles cleared. Edema 1+. Cr rose to 1.5 (from 1.3 on admit) — expected cardiorenal interaction, acceptable given clinical improvement. Echo during admission: LVEF 60%, worsened diastolic dysfunction (grade III). Trigger identified: dietary indiscretion (holidays) and missed chlorthalidone doses. Discharge on oral furosemide 40mg daily (increased from 20mg). Continue spironolactone. Sodium restriction reinforced. Daughter enrolled in HF caregiver education. Daily weights mandatory. Follow-up 1 week.

Post-discharge follow-up. Weight stable. BP 132/70. SpO2 96% RA. No orthopnea, no edema. Cr recovered to 1.3, K+ 5.0. Continue furosemide 40mg daily. Daughter monitoring daily weights and sodium intake. Discussed medication adherence — set up pill organizer. Held chlorthalidone (now on higher dose furosemide). eGFR 44. Close follow-up in 2 weeks.

Annual visit. No HF exacerbation since March hospitalization. Weight stable. BNP 220 (improved). eGFR 42 (progressive CKD now stage 3b). K+ 5.1 — concerning trend. Reduced spironolactone to every other day. Metformin 500mg BID still appropriate but approaching threshold. HbA1c 7.3%. DEXA: T-score -2.8 hip — osteoporosis. Started denosumab 60mg SC q6months (bisphosphonates avoided given CKD). Cognitive screen: MMSE 26/30 — stable from last year. Flu vaccine given.

CKD follow-up. eGFR 40. Proteinuria: urine protein/Cr 340 (worsening). K+ 4.8 (improved since spironolactone dose reduction). Bicarb 20 — started sodium bicarbonate 650mg TID for metabolic acidosis of CKD. Phosphorus 4.8 (upper normal), PTH 78 (mildly elevated) — monitor, may need phosphate binder if worsens. Metformin continued with close eGFR monitoring — discussed stopping if <30. Anemia screen: Hgb 10.8, iron studies adequate, no EPO needed yet. Follow-up 6 months.

Annual diabetic eye exam. NPDR stable — no progression to moderate or severe. No macular edema. BCVA 20/40 OD, 20/50 OS — cataracts progressing, particularly OS. Patient reports difficulty reading and driving at dusk. Discussed cataract surgery for OS — referred to cataract surgeon. Continue annual diabetic screening.

L eye cataract surgery — phacoemulsification with posterior chamber IOL implant under topical anesthesia. Uncomplicated procedure. Post-op day 1: BCVA 20/25 OS, quiet anterior chamber, IOL centered. Started prednisolone acetate 1% QID taper and moxifloxacin drops TID x1 week. Follow-up 1 week then 1 month. Discussed R eye surgery when ready — patient prefers to wait 2-3 months.

Annual visit. 83 y/o. eGFR 36 (CKD stage 3b, progressing). Discontinued metformin per nephrology guidance at eGFR <30 threshold approaching — switched to linagliptin 5mg daily (renal-safe DPP-4 inhibitor). HbA1c 7.4%. K+ 4.7. BNP 240. HF stable, NYHA II. Cataract surgery successful bilaterally. MMSE 25/30 — slight decline, monitoring. Denosumab dose 2 given on schedule. Medication burden is high — discussed priorities and goals of care with patient and daughter. Patient wishes to continue active management.

Annual visit. 84 y/o. eGFR 32. HbA1c 7.5% on linagliptin — acceptable for age. BNP 260. NYHA class II-III — now dyspneic walking one block. Weight stable. Mild bilateral edema — increased furosemide to 60mg daily. K+ 4.5. Cognitive decline: MoCA 20/30. Referred to neurology for cognitive assessment. Daughter increasingly assisting with medication management and appointments. Updated code status discussion — patient wishes to remain full code but does not want prolonged ICU stay. Goals of care documented.

41 y/o male presenting for executive physical. No significant PMH. Medications: none. NKDA. FH: mother with breast cancer, father with HTN. Social: management consultant, high-stress job, travels frequently, exercises sporadically, non-smoker, drinks 4-5 alcoholic beverages/week. Vitals: BP 132/86, HR 78, BMI 27.8. Exam: mild central adiposity, otherwise unremarkable. Labs: CBC normal, CMP normal, fasting glucose 104, HbA1c 5.7%, TC 212, LDL 138, HDL 44, TG 152. Mildly elevated BP and pre-diabetic. Lifestyle counseling provided — DASH diet, exercise 150 min/week, reduce alcohol. Recheck BP in 3 months.

3-month BP recheck. Home readings averaging 134/84. In-office: 136/88. Repeat fasting glucose 108. Weight unchanged. Reports improved but inconsistent exercise. Given persistent stage 1 HTN, started lisinopril 10mg daily. Discussed 10-year ASCVD risk: 6.2% — below statin threshold but will optimize lifestyle first. Return 3 months.

Follow-up HTN. BP 124/78 on lisinopril 10mg. Home readings consistently <130/80. Well tolerated, no cough. Fasting glucose 102, HbA1c 5.6%. Weight down 4 lbs with dietary changes. LDL 128. Continue current management. Annual labs in 6 months.

Self-referred for worsening anxiety and insomnia over 4 months. Reports racing thoughts, difficulty unwinding, early morning wakening (4am), irritability, muscle tension. Decreased concentration affecting work performance. Denies depressed mood, anhedonia, SI. PHQ-9: 6 (mild). GAD-7: 16 (severe anxiety). No prior psychiatric history. Stressors: pandemic uncertainty, work demands, relationship strain. Diagnosis: generalized anxiety disorder. Started escitalopram 10mg daily. Sleep hygiene counseling. Offered CBT referral — patient interested. Follow-up 4 weeks.

4-week follow-up. Escitalopram 10mg — initial side effects (mild nausea, headache) resolved by week 2. Sleep improved, falling asleep easier but still early wakening. GAD-7: 12 (moderate — improving). Started CBT with therapist, weekly sessions. Discussed increasing escitalopram to 15mg — patient prefers to give more time. Continue current dose. Return 6 weeks.

10-week follow-up. Anxiety significantly improved. GAD-7: 8 (mild). Sleeping through to 5:30am. CBT has been very helpful — practicing cognitive restructuring and progressive muscle relaxation daily. Work performance improved. No medication side effects — mild decreased libido reported but not distressing. Continue escitalopram 10mg. Transition to q3 month psychiatric follow-up. Ongoing CBT.

Annual visit. BP 122/76 on lisinopril. HbA1c 5.5%. LDL 124. BMI 26.4 (down from 27.8). GAD managed on escitalopram, doing well. Exercising 3-4x/week consistently now. Alcohol reduced to 2/week. Labs all WNL. Discussed hepatitis screening — HBV/HCV negative. HIV screening negative. PSA: not indicated at age 43 per USPSTF. Continue current management.

Referred for bilateral progressive hearing loss over 2 years, worse in noisy environments. Reports difficulty hearing conversations in meetings and restaurants. No tinnitus, vertigo, or ear pain. Otoscopy: TMs intact bilaterally, no effusion. Audiogram: bilateral symmetric mild-to-moderate sensorineural hearing loss, predominantly high-frequency (4-8kHz). Speech discrimination 84% R, 80% L. Consistent with noise-induced hearing loss (history of concerts without ear protection in 20s). Discussed hearing aid options. Referred to audiology for fitting. No further workup needed given symmetric presentation.

Hearing aid follow-up. Patient fitted with bilateral receiver-in-canal hearing aids 3 months ago. Reports significant improvement in conversational hearing, especially in meetings. Comfortable wearing 10-12 hours daily. Audiologist fine-tuned programming. Discussed hearing protection for any future noise exposure. Annual audiogram recommended.

6-month follow-up. Anxiety well managed. GAD-7: 5 (minimal). Completed 20 CBT sessions, now using skills independently. Discussed tapering escitalopram — patient prefers to continue given stability and ongoing work stress. No side effects. Continue escitalopram 10mg. Follow-up 6 months.

Presenting with 6 weeks of loose stools (3-4/day), occasional cramping, no blood. No weight loss. No fever. No recent travel or antibiotics. Exam: mild LLQ tenderness, no rebound. Labs: CBC normal, CRP 0.4, celiac panel (tTG IgA) negative, stool calprotectin 28 (normal). Likely IBS-D given symptom pattern and negative workup. Started low-FODMAP diet trial. If no improvement in 6 weeks, consider loperamide PRN or trial of rifaximin. Return 6 weeks.

6-week follow-up. Low-FODMAP diet significantly improved symptoms — stools now 1-2/day, formed. Identified lactose and fructans as main triggers. Gradually reintroducing other FODMAP groups. No further testing needed. Patient to continue modified diet with selective avoidance. Return PRN.

Annual visit. 45 y/o. BP 120/74 on lisinopril. BMI 25.8. HbA1c 5.4% — no longer pre-diabetic. LDL 118. GAD stable on escitalopram. IBS-D controlled with dietary modification. Hearing aids working well. Flu vaccine given. Updated COVID booster. All preventive care current. Discussed screening colonoscopy — not yet due by standard guidelines (age 45 per ACS), but given family history and mild GI symptoms, GI to determine timing. Overall excellent health trajectory.

Screening colonoscopy at age 46. Prep excellent. Cecum reached. No polyps, no masses, no inflammation. Normal terminal ileum. Assessment: normal colonoscopy. Repeat in 10 years per standard guidelines. IBS-D remains well controlled on modified diet.

47 y/o female presenting with fatigue, weight gain (15 lbs over 6 months), constipation, and cold intolerance. PMH: depression (on bupropion 150mg XL daily), migraines (sumatriptan PRN). Allergies: sulfonamides (Stevens-Johnson syndrome — severe). FH: mother and sister with hypothyroidism. Vitals: BP 118/76, HR 58, BMI 29.2. Exam: dry skin, mildly puffy face, delayed DTRs. Labs: TSH 28.4 mIU/L (elevated), free T4 0.5 ng/dL (low). Diagnosis: primary hypothyroidism. Started levothyroxine 75mcg daily on empty stomach. Recheck TSH in 6 weeks.

6-week follow-up hypothyroidism. TSH 12.1 — improving but still elevated. Free T4 0.8. Patient reports some improvement in energy and constipation. Increased levothyroxine to 100mcg daily. Reminded to take on empty stomach, 30 min before breakfast, avoid calcium and iron supplements within 4 hours. Recheck TSH 6 weeks.

Repeat TSH: 4.2 mIU/L, free T4 1.1 — approaching euthyroid. Significant symptom improvement — energy much better, weight down 5 lbs, constipation resolved. HR 68. Continue levothyroxine 100mcg. Recheck in 3 months to confirm stable.

TSH 3.1 — normal and stable on levothyroxine 100mcg. Feeling well. Weight down another 4 lbs. Depression well managed on bupropion — PHQ-9: 4. Migraines occurring 1-2x/month, managed with sumatriptan. Annual labs: CBC, CMP, lipids all normal. BMI 27.8. Flu vaccine given. Annual TSH monitoring going forward.

Referred for increasing migraine frequency — now 4-5/month, impacting work productivity. Using sumatriptan 100mg at each episode. Neuro exam normal. No aura, no focal deficits. Reviewed headache diary — triggers include stress, poor sleep, menstruation. Given frequency, prophylactic therapy indicated. Options discussed: topiramate (risk of cognitive side effects), propranolol (low HR concern if hypothyroid), amitriptyline (weight gain risk). Selected topiramate 25mg nightly, titrating to 50mg over 2 weeks. Continue sumatriptan PRN. Follow-up 8 weeks.

8-week follow-up. On topiramate 50mg nightly. Migraine frequency reduced to 1-2/month. Mild paresthesias in fingers (known topiramate side effect) — tolerable. No cognitive complaints. Weight stable. Continue current dose. Patient pleased with improvement. Follow-up 6 months.

Annual gynecologic exam. Age 49. Reports irregular menses over past 8 months — cycles ranging 21-45 days, varying flow. Occasional hot flashes. LH 28, FSH 32, estradiol 38 — consistent with perimenopausal transition. Pap smear: NILM, HPV negative. Mammogram ordered (screening). Discussed perimenopause symptoms and management options — patient prefers to observe for now. Calcium and vitamin D supplementation recommended.

Mammogram result: BI-RADS 0 — incomplete, area of asymmetry R breast. Diagnostic mammogram with ultrasound recommended. Called patient to schedule. She reports no palpable mass, no discharge, no skin changes. Appointment scheduled for next week.

Diagnostic mammogram and ultrasound R breast: 8mm area of architectural distortion at 2 o'clock, 5cm from nipple. US shows a hypoechoic irregular mass. BI-RADS 4B — suspicious. Recommend tissue sampling. US-guided core needle biopsy scheduled. Patient counseled and understandably anxious. Family history: mother with breast cancer noted. Provided support resources.

US-guided core needle biopsy R breast 2 o'clock lesion performed. 4 cores obtained. Specimen sent to pathology. Post-procedure: small hematoma, pressure dressing applied. Instructions given for wound care and activity restrictions. Results expected in 5-7 business days. Patient accompanied by sister for support.

Pathology results: invasive ductal carcinoma, grade 2, ER+/PR+, HER2 negative. Ki-67 15%. Discussed diagnosis with patient. Referral to multidisciplinary breast cancer tumor board. Staging workup ordered: CT chest/abdomen/pelvis, bone scan. Genetic counseling recommended given mother's breast cancer history. Surgery consultation for lumpectomy vs. mastectomy. Patient processing diagnosis, supportive family present.

Multidisciplinary consultation for newly diagnosed R breast IDC. Staging workup: CT clear, bone scan negative — stage I (T1cN0M0, pending surgical staging). Discussed treatment plan: lumpectomy with sentinel lymph node biopsy, followed by adjuvant radiation. Oncotype DX to determine chemotherapy benefit. Endocrine therapy (aromatase inhibitor or tamoxifen) for 5+ years given ER+. Genetic testing sent: BRCA1/2 panel. Patient prefers breast conservation. Surgery scheduled with Dr. Webb.

R breast lumpectomy with sentinel lymph node biopsy performed. Specimen oriented and sent to pathology. SLN: 2 nodes identified by lymphoscintigraphy, both negative on frozen section. EBL 50 mL. No complications. Drain placed. Post-op instructions reviewed. Topiramate and levothyroxine continued perioperatively. Sulfonamide allergy prominently documented — cefazolin used for prophylaxis. Discharge same day.

Final pathology: 14mm IDC, grade 2, ER 95%/PR 80%, HER2 negative. Margins clear (>2mm all directions). 0/2 sentinel nodes positive. Stage IA (pT1cN0). Oncotype DX recurrence score: 12 (low risk). Based on TAILORx data, endocrine therapy alone recommended — chemotherapy not indicated. BRCA1/2: negative. Started tamoxifen 20mg daily (premenopausal/perimenopausal). Discussed side effects including hot flashes, VTE risk, endometrial changes. Radiation oncology referral for adjuvant RT.

Radiation therapy planning visit. Plan: whole breast irradiation, 40 Gy in 15 fractions (hypofractionated regimen) with 10 Gy boost to tumor bed. Treatment to begin next week, M-F for approximately 4 weeks. Discussed expected side effects: skin erythema, fatigue, breast edema. Tamoxifen well tolerated so far — mild hot flashes. Provided written instructions and skin care regimen. TSH checked: 3.4 — stable.

Radiation therapy completed. Tolerated well — mild skin erythema resolving, moderate fatigue. No grade 3+ toxicity. Post-RT mammogram in 6 months. Continue tamoxifen 20mg daily. Follow-up schedule: oncology q6 months for 2 years, then annually. Annual mammograms. Clinical breast exam at each visit. Patient coping well, attending breast cancer support group. Referred back to PCP for general health maintenance.

6-month post-treatment follow-up. No evidence of recurrence on clinical exam. Post-RT mammogram: expected post-surgical and post-radiation changes, no suspicious findings. BI-RADS 2. Tamoxifen continued — hot flashes manageable with lifestyle measures. No vaginal bleeding. PHQ-9: 8 (mild depression — increase from baseline). Discussed with patient — recommends discussing with PCP regarding bupropion dose adjustment. Cancer survivorship care plan provided.

Follow-up. Post breast cancer treatment — on tamoxifen. Depression slightly worsened per oncology. PHQ-9: 9. Increased bupropion to 300mg XL daily. TSH 3.3 — stable on levothyroxine 100mcg. Topiramate continued for migraines. Discussed exercise and psychosocial support for mood and cancer survivorship. DEXA ordered given tamoxifen use and perimenopausal status — T-scores normal. Follow-up 3 months.

Annual oncology visit. 2 years post-treatment. Clinical exam: no masses, no lymphadenopathy. Mammogram: BI-RADS 1 (negative). Tamoxifen continued — transitioning to anastrozole 1mg daily as patient now confirmed postmenopausal (FSH 68, amenorrheic >12 months). DEXA baseline before AI: T-score -1.2 lumbar, -1.0 hip (osteopenia). Calcium and vitamin D continued. Repeat DEXA in 2 years. Mood improved on bupropion 300mg — PHQ-9: 4.

3-year oncology follow-up. No evidence of recurrence. Mammogram BI-RADS 1. Tolerating anastrozole — reports mild arthralgias managed with stretching and acetaminophen. No fractures. TSH 3.0. BMI 26.4. Bupropion 300mg, levothyroxine 100mcg, anastrozole 1mg, topiramate 50mg. Continue AI for total 5 years (until 2025). Annual mammograms and clinical exams. Transitioning to annual oncology visits. Patient in good spirits, resumed full activities.

78-year-old female presenting for annual wellness visit. PMH significant for hypertension, osteoarthritis, and hyperlipidemia. BP 148/82, HR 72, BMI 26.1. Patient reports increased stiffness in bilateral knees, worse in the mornings. Currently on amlodipine 5mg daily and atorvastatin 20mg daily. Lipid panel ordered. Referred to Orthopaedics for knee evaluation.

Referral from Dr. Okafor for bilateral knee pain. X-rays demonstrate moderate tricompartmental OA, left worse than right. Crepitus noted on examination bilaterally. ROM: right knee 0-120°, left knee 5-110°. Recommended trial of physical therapy 2x/week for 6 weeks, acetaminophen 650mg TID PRN. Patient declines intra-articular injections at this time. Follow-up in 8 weeks.

Follow-up for bilateral knee OA after PT course. Patient reports moderate improvement in right knee but persistent pain and functional limitation in left knee. Now willing to consider corticosteroid injection. Performed left knee intra-articular injection with 40mg triamcinolone acetonide under sterile technique. Tolerated well. Continue home exercises. Return in 3 months or sooner if symptoms worsen.

Follow-up visit. BP 138/78 on amlodipine 5mg daily — still above target. Lipid panel from January: LDL 142, HDL 54, TG 168. Increased atorvastatin to 40mg daily. Adding hydrochlorothiazide 12.5mg daily for improved BP control. BMP ordered to monitor electrolytes in 2 weeks. Patient reports left knee improved after cortisone injection. Allergy to sulfa drugs noted — HCTZ is a sulfonamide derivative; discussed risk, patient has tolerated thiazides previously without issue.

Routine follow-up. BP 132/76, improved on current regimen. BMP: Na 139, K 3.8, Cr 0.94, eGFR 58. Mild CKD stage 3a noted — likely hypertensive nephropathy. LDL repeat: 98. Patient tolerating atorvastatin 40mg without myalgias. Continue current medications. Annual flu vaccine administered. Bone density screening ordered given age and gender.

Referred by PCP for evaluation of diffuse joint pain beyond bilateral knees. Patient reports new stiffness in hands and wrists, morning stiffness lasting >1 hour. Examination reveals MCP joint swelling bilaterally and positive squeeze test. RF 86 IU/mL (elevated), anti-CCP 124 U/mL (positive), ESR 42, CRP 2.8. Diagnosis: seropositive rheumatoid arthritis. Initiated methotrexate 10mg weekly with folic acid 1mg daily. Baseline LFTs and CBC obtained — within normal limits. Hepatitis B and C serologies pending.

Follow-up RA management. Patient reports 40% improvement in hand stiffness and swelling. Morning stiffness now approximately 30 minutes. Tolerating methotrexate without GI side effects. LFTs stable. Hep B and C negative. Increased methotrexate to 15mg weekly. DAS28 score improved from 4.8 to 3.6. Continue folic acid supplementation.

Annual wellness visit. BP 128/74. eGFR stable at 56. DEXA scan results: T-score lumbar spine -2.6, femoral neck -2.1 — consistent with osteoporosis. Started alendronate 70mg weekly with instructions for proper administration. Calcium 1200mg and vitamin D3 2000 IU daily recommended. Discussed fall prevention strategies given RA and osteoporosis. Comprehensive metabolic panel otherwise unremarkable.

Baseline ophthalmologic exam prior to consideration of hydroxychloroquine for RA per rheumatology. Visual acuity 20/30 OD, 20/25 OS with correction. IOP 16/17. Fundoscopic exam: early nuclear sclerotic cataracts bilaterally, no macular abnormalities. OCT macula: normal foveal contour, no thinning. Cleared for hydroxychloroquine use. Annual screening recommended.

RA follow-up. DAS28 score 2.9 — low disease activity. Methotrexate 15mg weekly continued. Added hydroxychloroquine 200mg BID per ophthalmology clearance for combination DMARD therapy. Discussed long-term monitoring plan. Patient concerned about medication burden — reassured regarding importance of disease control to prevent joint damage. Repeat labs in 8 weeks.

80-year-old female presenting with acute onset left wrist pain after mechanical fall at home. Denies LOC, head strike, or preceding dizziness. On examination: swelling and tenderness over distal left radius, limited ROM. Neurovascular status intact distally. X-ray: non-displaced distal radius fracture (Colles type). Placed in sugar-tong splint. Given acetaminophen 1000mg — avoiding NSAIDs given CKD. Orthopedics consulted for follow-up. Given fragility fracture, recommend reassessment of osteoporosis management with PCP.

Follow-up for non-displaced left distal radius fracture sustained from fall. Repeat films confirm stable alignment. Converted to short arm cast. Patient taking acetaminophen with adequate pain control. Discussed that alendronate compliance has been inconsistent — reinforced importance given fragility fracture. Return in 3 weeks for repeat imaging and potential cast removal.

Follow-up after fragility fracture. Fracture has healed well per orthopaedics. Reassessing osteoporosis management — patient unable to tolerate weekly alendronate (esophageal irritation). Transitioning to denosumab 60mg SC every 6 months. First injection administered today. BP 130/72. eGFR 54, stable. Reviewed fall risk: recommended grab bars in bathroom and removal of throw rugs. RA stable on combination DMARDs per rheumatology.

Second denosumab injection administered. BP 126/70 — well controlled. Annual labs: HbA1c 5.9% (prediabetes range), fasting glucose 108. Discussed lifestyle modifications for diabetes prevention. eGFR 52. LDL 88 on atorvastatin 40mg. Colonoscopy up to date. Age-appropriate cancer screenings reviewed. Influenza and updated COVID-19 vaccines administered.

RA follow-up. Patient reports new flare with increased swelling in MCPs and wrists over past 3 weeks. DAS28 score 4.2 — moderate disease activity. LFTs mildly elevated: ALT 52 (baseline 28). Holding methotrexate and rechecking LFTs in 2 weeks. If persistent elevation, will consider switching to leflunomide or biologic therapy. Prescribed short course of prednisone 10mg taper over 2 weeks for flare management.

34-year-old male presenting for new patient intake. Recently relocated. PMH: asthma (childhood, largely outgrown), seasonal allergies. No chronic medications. Socially: non-smoker, occasional alcohol, works as software engineer. FH: father with T2DM, mother with breast cancer at age 58. Vitals: BP 122/78, HR 68, BMI 28.4. Routine labs ordered including lipid panel, CMP, CBC, and HbA1c given family history.

Lab results review via phone encounter. CBC normal. CMP unremarkable. Lipid panel: LDL 128, HDL 42, TG 156. HbA1c 5.4%. Mildly dyslipidemic with low HDL. Discussed lifestyle modifications: increased aerobic exercise, Mediterranean-style diet, weight loss goal of 10-15 lbs. Will recheck in 6 months before considering statin therapy. Encouraged 150 min/week moderate-intensity exercise.

Follow-up lipid management. Patient has been exercising regularly, lost 8 lbs. BMI now 27.2. BP 118/74. Repeat lipid panel: LDL 112, HDL 48, TG 134. Improved but LDL still above optimal. Continue lifestyle measures. Patient prefers to avoid statin at this time. Will reassess at annual visit. Flu vaccine administered.

35-year-old male presenting with acute onset wheezing, dyspnea, and chest tightness over past 6 hours. Reports recent URI symptoms for 3 days. History of childhood asthma. No current rescue inhaler. O2 sat 94% on RA, HR 96, RR 22. Diffuse expiratory wheezes bilaterally. Administered albuterol 2.5mg via nebulizer x2 with improvement. O2 sat improved to 98%. Prescribed albuterol MDI 2 puffs Q4-6H PRN, prednisone 40mg x5 days. Recommended PFTs and pulmonology follow-up for possible adult-onset asthma recurrence.

Referral from ED for recurrent asthma evaluation. Patient reports wheezing episodes 2-3x/month, worse with exercise and upper respiratory infections. Using rescue inhaler 3x/week currently. PFTs performed today: FEV1 78% predicted, FEV1/FVC ratio 0.72, significant bronchodilator response (+14%). Consistent with moderate persistent asthma. Initiated fluticasone/salmeterol 250/50 1 puff BID. Provided asthma action plan. Allergy testing recommended. Follow-up in 6 weeks.

Asthma follow-up. Significant improvement — rescue inhaler use down to 1x/week. No nocturnal symptoms. Repeat spirometry: FEV1 improved to 88% predicted. Good inhaler technique demonstrated. Continue fluticasone/salmeterol 250/50 BID. Allergen skin testing positive for dust mites, grass pollen, and cat dander. Discussed environmental controls and consideration of allergen immunotherapy. Return in 3 months.

Annual physical. BMI 26.8, continued weight loss. BP 120/76. Asthma well-controlled on ICS/LABA per pulmonology. Lipids improved: LDL 105, HDL 52. HbA1c 5.3%. Discussed age-appropriate preventive care. Tdap booster administered. Patient reports increased work-related stress and difficulty sleeping. Discussed sleep hygiene measures. PHQ-9 score: 4 (minimal). Will monitor.

Self-referred for evaluation of changing mole on upper back. Patient reports the lesion has grown and darkened over past 3 months. Examination: 8mm irregularly bordered, variegated brown-black macule on right upper back. ABCDE criteria concerning. Shave biopsy performed and sent to pathology. Several other benign-appearing nevi noted. Full skin exam otherwise unremarkable. Results to follow in 7-10 days.

Biopsy results discussion. Pathology: moderately dysplastic compound nevus with positive margins. No melanoma identified. Recommend wide local excision with 5mm margins to ensure complete removal. Procedure scheduled for next week. Patient counseled on sun protection and monthly self-skin exams. Family history of maternal breast cancer noted — no additional melanoma risk factors identified.

Wide local excision of dysplastic nevus on right upper back performed under local anesthesia (1% lidocaine with epinephrine). Specimen sent to pathology for margin assessment. Wound closed in layered fashion. Post-op care instructions provided. Suture removal in 14 days. Final pathology to follow.

Self-referred for evaluation of persistent low mood, insomnia, and decreased concentration affecting work performance over past 2 months. PHQ-9 score: 14 (moderate depression). GAD-7 score: 10 (moderate anxiety). Reports significant work-related stressors and recent relationship difficulties. No SI/HI. Denies substance use beyond occasional alcohol. Diagnosis: major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate; generalized anxiety disorder. Initiated sertraline 50mg daily. Recommended weekly psychotherapy. Discussed potential side effects and 4-6 week onset of full therapeutic effect.

Follow-up MDD and GAD. Patient tolerating sertraline — mild initial nausea resolved. Sleep improving. PHQ-9: 10. GAD-7: 8. Engaging in weekly CBT sessions. Increased sertraline to 100mg daily for further symptom improvement. Continue psychotherapy. Encouraged regular exercise — discussed evidence for aerobic activity in depression management.

Ongoing psychiatric follow-up. PHQ-9: 5 (mild). GAD-7: 4 (minimal). Significant improvement on sertraline 100mg daily and ongoing CBT. Patient reports better coping strategies and improved work performance. Sleeping 7 hours nightly. Continue current regimen. Plan to reassess in 3 months regarding duration of pharmacotherapy — recommend minimum 9-12 months given first episode.

Annual visit. BMI 25.9. BP 116/72. Asthma remains well-controlled. Mood significantly improved on sertraline per psychiatry. Lipids at goal. HbA1c 5.5%. Dermatology follow-up skin exams current. No new concerns. Flu and updated COVID vaccine administered. Continue all current medications: fluticasone/salmeterol, sertraline 100mg, albuterol PRN.

Annual asthma review. Well-controlled on fluticasone/salmeterol 250/50 BID. Rescue inhaler use <1x/month. No exacerbations requiring ED visit or oral steroids in past year. PFTs: FEV1 92% predicted, FEV1/FVC 0.78. Discussed step-down trial to fluticasone monotherapy 250mcg BID given sustained control. Patient agreeable. Provided updated asthma action plan. Follow-up in 3 months to reassess after step-down.

60-year-old female presenting for routine physical. PMH: type 2 diabetes mellitus (diagnosed 2012), hypertension, GERD. Medications: metformin 1000mg BID, lisinopril 20mg daily, omeprazole 20mg daily. Allergies: penicillin (rash). BP 142/86, HR 76, BMI 31.2. HbA1c 7.8% — above target. Discussed intensification of glycemic management. Added glipizide 5mg daily. Renal function: Cr 0.88, eGFR 72. Microalbumin/creatinine ratio 45 (mildly elevated) — early diabetic nephropathy suspected. Ophthalmology referral for diabetic eye screening.

Diabetic eye screening. Visual acuity 20/25 OU with correction. Dilated fundus exam: mild non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy (NPDR) bilateral — scattered microaneurysms and dot-blot hemorrhages. No macular edema on OCT. Recommended tighter glycemic control and annual eye exams. No ophthalmic intervention needed at this time. Report sent to PCP.

DM follow-up. HbA1c improved to 7.2% on metformin + glipizide. Patient reports occasional hypoglycemic episodes (glucose 60s) in late afternoon. Reduced glipizide to 2.5mg daily. BP 136/82 — increased lisinopril to 40mg daily for both BP control and nephroprotective effect. Repeat microalbumin/Cr ratio 52 — stable. Reinforced dietary counseling and diabetic foot care. Monofilament exam: intact sensation bilaterally.

Referred by PCP for persistent epigastric pain and bloating despite omeprazole. Symptoms worsening over 3 months. H. pylori stool antigen positive. Follow-up right shoulder partial rotator cuff tear after 8 weeks PT. Patient reports 70% improvement in pain and function. Overhead strength improved. Can perform most work duties. Annual visit. Patient reports right shoulder fully recovered, back to full work duties. BP 130/82 — repeated: 128/80. BMI 25.2. Follow-up liver enzymes and alcohol use. Patient reduced to 4-5 drinks/week. Repeat labs: AST 32, ALT 38, GGT 45 — all improved. LDL 128. BMI 25.0. BP 124/78. 28-year-old male presenting with acute low back pain radiating to right posterior thigh after lifting heavy equipment at work. Onset 4 hours ago. Follow-up acute lumbar radiculopathy from January ED visit. Pain improved approximately 50% with conservative measures. Radicular symptoms less prominent. Follow-up low back pain. Completed 6 weeks PT with significant improvement. Radicular symptoms resolved. Able to return to modified duty. Lumbar MRI deferred as symptoms resolving. 49-year-old female presenting for evaluation of fatigue, weight gain (12 lbs over 6 months), and cold intolerance. PMH: migraines, anxiety (managed with buspirone 10mg BID). Hypothyroid follow-up. Anti-TPO antibodies strongly positive at 342 IU/mL — confirms Hashimoto thyroiditis. TSH improved to 6.8 on levothyroxine 50mcg. Still above target. Increased to 75mcg daily. Thyroid follow-up. TSH 3.2 on levothyroxine 75mcg — within target range. Patient feeling significantly better: energy improved, lost 4 lbs, no longer cold intolerant. Referred by PCP for increasing migraine frequency. Previously 2-3/month, now 6-8/month with aura (visual scotoma). Duration 8-12 hours. Medication review and coordination. Patient transitioning migraine prophylaxis from topiramate to propranolol per neurology. ECG: sinus bradycardia at 56 bpm, otherwise normal. Migraine follow-up. Propranolol 20mg BID — migraines reduced to 2/month. No cognitive side effects. HR 54, BP 108/66 — tolerating hemodynamically but at lower limit. Increased to 40mg BID cautiously. Annual gynecologic exam. LMP 2 weeks ago, regular cycles. No menopausal symptoms. Pap smear and HPV co-testing performed. Breast exam: no masses, tenderness, or discharge. Unscheduled visit for hot flashes, night sweats, and irregular menses over past 3 months. Last menstrual period 6 weeks ago. FSH 48 mIU/mL — perimenopause confirmed. Started low-dose estradiol patch 0.025mg/day with cyclic medroxyprogesterone 5mg for 12 days/month. TSH rechecked: 3.4 — stable. Discussed risks and benefits of HRT including cardiovascular and breast cancer considerations.

HRT follow-up. Hot flashes reduced by 80%. Sleeping better. Tolerating estradiol patch well, no breakthrough bleeding on cyclic progesterone. Discussed with neurology recommendation: switch from cyclic to continuous progesterone to minimize hormonal fluctuation. Changed to continuous combined estradiol 0.025mg/medroxyprogesterone 1.5mg daily patch. Monitor migraines.

Migraine follow-up in setting of perimenopause and HRT. Switch to continuous combined HRT improved hormonal migraine pattern — back to 2/month. Propranolol 40mg BID continued. Discussed that migraines may improve further after menopause is complete. Considering CGRP monoclonal antibody (erenumab) if frequency increases. Current management adequate. Follow-up in 6 months.

Annual visit. 53-year-old perimenopausal female. TSH 3.6. BP 112/70. BMI 27.2. Vasomotor symptoms well-controlled on HRT. Migraines stable per neurology. Anxiety managed. Comprehensive metabolic panel normal. LDL 112. HbA1c 5.6%. DEXA baseline ordered given perimenopause. Mammogram: BI-RADS 2, benign finding (small bilateral cysts). Follow-up visit. Last menstrual period >12 months ago — now postmenopausal. Vasomotor symptoms minimal on HRT. 66-year-old male referred by PCP for exertional chest pressure and dyspnea on exertion for 3 weeks. PMH: hypertension, hyperlipidemia, former smoker (30 pack-years, quit 10 years ago). Post-catheterization day 1. Radial access site clean, no hematoma. Chest pain resolved. Troponin peaked at 0.18 (type 4a periprocedural MI — expected). ECG: no new changes. Discharged on: aspirin 81mg daily, clopidogrel 75mg daily, rosuvastatin increased to 40mg daily, metoprolol succinate 25mg daily, amlodipine 10mg daily. Cardiac rehabilitation referral placed. Two-week post-PCI follow-up. No recurrent chest pain. Tolerating medications well. HR 62, BP 128/76. Radial access site healed. Enrolled in cardiac rehabilitation — starting next week. Six-month post-PCI follow-up. Completed 24 sessions of cardiac rehabilitation. Functional capacity significantly improved — now walking 3 miles daily without symptoms. BP 122/72, HR 58. LDL 62. 3-month post-AF ablation follow-up. Patient reports no palpitations since ablation. ECG: normal sinus rhythm, HR 64. 14-day Holter: sinus rhythm throughout, no AF recurrence, no significant arrhythmias. Excellent result. Continue apixaban for now — will reassess at 6 months.
