Plan to resume apixaban POD2 per hematology guidance.

Hospital day 5. Progressing well with PT — ambulating 50 feet with rolling walker. Apixaban resumed POD2 without bleeding complications. Wound clean and dry. Hgb stable at 10.2. Discharged to skilled nursing facility for continued rehabilitation. Estimated SNF stay 2-3 weeks. Fall prevention measures reinforced. Home rug removal recommended to daughter.

6-week post-op follow-up. Completed SNF rehab, now home. Ambulating with single-point cane. XR: prosthesis in good position, no periprosthetic fracture. ROM improving. Some residual thigh pain — expected, will resolve. PT continuing outpatient 2x/week. Discussed switching from alendronate to zoledronic acid IV annually given compliance concerns and GI intolerance risk in elderly. Coordinating with PCP.

Post-fracture follow-up. Recovering well from R hip hemiarthroplasty. Now ambulatory with cane. Switched from alendronate to zoledronic acid 5mg IV annually — first infusion today, tolerated well. Pre-treated with acetaminophen. Vitamin D 34 (improved on 2000 IU daily). TSH 2.8. Discussed polypharmacy review. Medication list reconciled. Cognitive screening (MMSE): 27/30 — mild deficits in recall. Will monitor annually.

81 y/o female referred for mild cognitive decline. Daughter reports word-finding difficulty, occasionally misplacing items, and repeating questions over past year. MMSE 26/30 (lost points: recall 1/3, orientation 1/5). MoCA 23/30. Neurological exam otherwise normal. MRI brain ordered. Labs: B12, folate, TSH, RPR to rule out reversible causes. Differential includes early Alzheimer's disease vs. age-related cognitive decline.

MRI brain: mild generalized cortical atrophy, moderate hippocampal volume loss bilateral (Scheltens grade 2). No acute infarcts, no significant white matter disease. Labs: B12 normal, folate normal, TSH euthyroid, RPR nonreactive. Diagnosis: mild cognitive impairment (MCI), amnestic type — likely prodromal Alzheimer's disease. Discussed diagnosis with pt and daughter. No pharmacotherapy indicated at MCI stage per current guidelines. Recommended cognitive stimulation, exercise, social engagement. Advance care planning discussed. Repeat cognitive testing in 12 months.

AF follow-up. Rate well controlled on metoprolol. HR 66 (irregular), BP 130/76. Echocardiogram: EF 58%, stable LA enlargement. No new symptoms — denies palpitations, dyspnea, or chest pain. Anticoagulation continued. Discussed fall risk with daughter given anticoagulation and recent hip fracture — benefits clearly outweigh risks at CHA2DS2-VASc 5. Continue current regimen.

Annual cognitive reassessment. Daughter reports gradual worsening — difficulty managing finances, occasional disorientation in familiar places. MMSE 23/30, MoCA 19/30 (decline from prior). Diagnosis updated: mild Alzheimer's disease. Started donepezil 5mg at bedtime, titrate to 10mg in 4-6 weeks if tolerated. Discussed prognosis, safety concerns (driving assessment recommended), legal/financial planning. Daughter appointed healthcare proxy.

Annual wellness visit. Accompanied by daughter (primary caregiver). Donepezil 10mg tolerated — daughter reports some stabilization of cognition. Weight 125 lbs (stable). BP 132/78. Labs: TSH 3.0, CMP normal, CBC normal. Zoledronic acid infusion #2 given. Reviewed all medications — 8 active prescriptions, no interactions identified. Flu and updated COVID vaccine administered. Home safety evaluation completed, grab bars installed.

Follow-up Alzheimer's disease. MMSE 21/30. Functional decline noted — needs assistance with medication management and meal preparation. Living with daughter. Added memantine 5mg daily, titrate to 10mg BID over 4 weeks (combination therapy with donepezil). Driving assessment completed — recommended cessation of driving, pt agreeable. Caregiver burnout screening: daughter reports mild stress, referred to support group. Goals of care discussion: pt wishes to avoid aggressive interventions and hospitalization if possible.

36 y/o female presenting with 6-week history of fatigue, unintentional weight loss (8 lbs), and intermittent low-grade fevers. Denies cough, night sweats, rash, or joint pain. PMHx: none significant. No regular medications. Allergies: NKDA. Social hx: non-smoker, occasional alcohol, works as graphic designer. BP 112/68, HR 88, Temp 99.8F. Exam: mild cervical lymphadenopathy bilateral, no hepatosplenomegaly. Labs ordered: CBC with diff, CMP, ESR, CRP, LDH, peripheral smear, monospot, HIV, TSH.

Lab results: WBC 14.2 with lymphocyte predominance (68%), Hgb 11.2, platelets 132. LDH 320 (elevated). ESR 42, CRP 1.8. Peripheral smear: atypical lymphocytes. Monospot negative. HIV negative. TSH normal. Given lymphadenopathy, cytopenias, elevated LDH, and atypical lymphocytes — concerning for lymphoproliferative disorder. Urgent referral to hematology/oncology. CT chest/abdomen/pelvis ordered.

Hematology consultation. CT C/A/P: bilateral cervical, axillary, and mediastinal lymphadenopathy. Largest node 3.2cm in left axilla. Spleen mildly enlarged at 14cm. No other masses. Reviewed peripheral smear — atypical lymphocytes with irregular nuclear contours. Flow cytometry on peripheral blood ordered. Excisional biopsy of left axillary node recommended for definitive diagnosis. Scheduled for next week.

Excisional biopsy of left axillary lymph node performed under local anesthesia with sedation. 3.5cm node excised intact, sent for pathology, flow cytometry, and cytogenetics. Procedure uncomplicated. Wound closed with subcuticular sutures. Follow-up with oncology for results.

Pathology: follicular lymphoma, grade 1-2. CD10+, BCL2+, BCL6+, t(14;18) positive by FISH. Flow cytometry confirms monoclonal B-cell population. PET/CT ordered for staging. Bone marrow biopsy scheduled. Discussed diagnosis with patient — she is understandably distressed but composed. Explained that follicular lymphoma is indolent and often treatable with good long-term outcomes.

Staging complete. PET/CT: FDG-avid bilateral cervical, axillary, and mediastinal nodes (SUVmax 8.2 in left axilla). Splenic involvement suspected. Bone marrow biopsy: 15% involvement by follicular lymphoma. Ann Arbor Stage IV. FLIPI score: 3 (high-intermediate risk). Given symptomatic disease (B symptoms, cytopenias), treatment indicated. Recommended bendamustine + rituximab (BR) x6 cycles. Discussed fertility preservation — referral to reproductive endocrinology placed given patient's age.

Fertility preservation consultation. 36 y/o female with newly diagnosed follicular lymphoma, planned BR chemotherapy. AMH 2.8 (age-appropriate). Discussed oocyte cryopreservation. Ovarian stimulation protocol initiated with gonadotropins. Timeline: ~2 weeks for egg retrieval before chemo can begin. Oncology informed and agrees with brief delay for preservation.

Oocyte retrieval: 14 mature oocytes collected via transvaginal ultrasound-guided aspiration. Cryopreserved via vitrification. No ovarian hyperstimulation. Procedure well tolerated. Cleared for chemotherapy initiation. Good preservation outcome for future family planning.

Cycle 1 of BR initiated. Bendamustine 90mg/m2 IV D1-2, rituximab 375mg/m2 IV D1. Pre-medications: acetaminophen, diphenhydramine, ondansetron. Rituximab infusion well tolerated, no reaction. Counseled on neutropenic precautions, signs of infection. Anti-emetics and prophylactic acyclovir prescribed. Labs in 1 week for nadir CBC.

Nadir labs: WBC 2.8, ANC 1.1 (mild neutropenia), Hgb 10.8, platelets 118. No fever or infection. Mild fatigue and nausea managed with ondansetron. Tolerating treatment. Will proceed with Cycle 2 on schedule in 1 week if counts recover.

Interim PET/CT after 4 cycles of BR: near-complete metabolic response. Residual mild FDG uptake in left axilla (SUVmax 2.1, down from 8.2). No new sites. Deauville score 3 — favorable. Continue BR for 2 more cycles to complete 6 total. Pt tolerating well, main side effect is fatigue days 3-7 post-treatment. ANC has required one dose of filgrastim.

Completed 6 cycles of BR. End-of-treatment PET/CT: complete metabolic response (CMR). No FDG-avid disease. Deauville score 1. Discussed rituximab maintenance: 375mg/m2 every 2 months x2 years — shown to prolong PFS in follicular lymphoma. Pt agrees. First maintenance dose scheduled. CBC recovering: WBC 4.8, Hgb 12.0, Plt 180. Tremendous response.

Rituximab maintenance visit #3. Tolerating well, no infusion reactions. CBC normal. IgG level 620 (low normal — monitoring for hypogammaglobulinemia, common with rituximab). No infections. Surveillance CT: continued complete remission. Discussed that follicular lymphoma can relapse but long remissions are common with this approach. Continue maintenance per protocol.

Annual wellness visit. Follicular lymphoma in complete remission, on rituximab maintenance. Weight recovered to pre-illness baseline. Energy levels back to normal. Labs: CBC normal, CMP normal, IgG 580 (slightly low). Discussed infection prevention, up to date on vaccines (given prior to rituximab). Shingrix completed. Mammogram and Pap scheduled. Mood stable. Pt grateful and optimistic.

Completed 2 years of rituximab maintenance. Final surveillance PET/CT: continued CMR. No evidence of disease. Transitioning to observation. Plan: clinical exam + labs every 3 months x2 years, then every 6 months. CT scans only if clinically indicated (moving away from routine surveillance imaging per updated guidelines). IgG 540 — will monitor, may need IVIG if recurrent infections. Pt doing well, back to full activities.

64 y/o male presenting with 2-month history of progressive bilateral hand tremor, worse at rest. Also reports difficulty initiating movement, stiffness, and shuffling gait. PMHx: GERD (on omeprazole 20mg), BPH (on tamsulosin). Allergies: NKDA. Family hx: unremarkable. BP 138/82, HR 72. Neuro exam: resting tremor bilateral (L>R), cogwheel rigidity bilateral upper extremities, bradykinesia, reduced arm swing. Gait: short stride, decreased arm swing. Clinical presentation concerning for Parkinson's disease. Referral to neurology placed.

65 y/o male referred for evaluation of parkinsonism. Detailed exam confirms asymmetric resting tremor (4-5 Hz, L>R), cogwheel rigidity, bradykinesia, and postural instability (positive pull test). No red flags for atypical parkinsonism (no early falls, autonomic failure, or cerebellar signs). DaTscan ordered to confirm. Clinical diagnosis: probable Parkinson's disease, Hoehn & Yahr stage 2. Starting carbidopa/levodopa 25/100mg TID. Discussed disease course, expectations, and support resources.

DaTscan results: reduced dopamine transporter uptake bilateral putamen, left worse than right — consistent with Parkinson's disease. Pt on carbidopa/levodopa x3 weeks, reports meaningful improvement in tremor and stiffness. Able to button shirt again. Mild nausea — taking with food, resolving. Continue current dose. PT referral for gait training and balance exercises. RTC 3 months.

3-month follow-up. Good motor response to carbidopa/levodopa. UPDRS motor score improved from 32 to 18. Gait improved with PT. Reports new symptom: REM sleep behavior disorder (acting out dreams, wife reports thrashing). This is common in PD. Added melatonin 3mg at bedtime as first-line treatment. Discussed sleep safety measures. Also screening for depression: PHQ-9 score 5 — mild, monitoring.

6-month follow-up. Motor function stable on carbidopa/levodopa 25/100 TID. RBD improved on melatonin. New concern: orthostatic hypotension — BP 138/82 sitting, 112/68 standing, symptomatic (dizziness on standing). Likely PD-related autonomic dysfunction. Advised increased fluid/salt intake, compression stockings. If persistent, will consider midodrine or fludrocortisone. PHQ-9: 7 — borderline, will monitor closely.

Annual exam. Reviewed PD management with Dr. Graves. Orthostatic hypotension ongoing — started midodrine 5mg TID per neuro recommendation. GERD stable on omeprazole. BPH symptoms controlled. BP 134/80 (sitting). Weight stable at 185 lbs. Labs: CMP normal, HbA1c 5.6%, lipids within normal limits. PSA 2.4. Age-appropriate screening current. Colonoscopy up to date. Flu vaccine given.

Follow-up PD. Motor symptoms progressing — reports wearing-off between doses (symptoms return ~3.5 hours after dose, before next dose due). UPDRS motor score 22 (worsened from 18). Added entacapone 200mg with each levodopa dose (switching to Stalevo). Discussed that motor fluctuations are expected with disease progression. If wearing-off persists, may add MAO-B inhibitor (rasagiline). PHQ-9: 9 — mild-moderate depression. Started sertraline 50mg daily.

On Stalevo (carbidopa/levodopa/entacapone 25/100/200) TID. Wearing-off improved — now 4.5 hours between doses. Added rasagiline 1mg daily for additional benefit. Depression improved on sertraline — PHQ-9: 4. New issue: constipation (common in PD). Started polyethylene glycol (MiraLAX) daily. Speech evaluation recommended — mild hypophonia noted. Referred to speech therapy (LSVT LOUD program).

67 y/o male, PD x2.5 years. Hoehn & Yahr stage 2.5. Motor fluctuations managed on current regimen. LSVT LOUD program completed — speech volume improved. New symptom: mild dyskinesias (choreiform movements) at peak dose — dose adjustment may be needed. Reduced individual levodopa dose to 75mg, increased frequency to QID. Orthostatic hypotension stable on midodrine. Discussed future consideration of deep brain stimulation if motor fluctuations worsen. Pt not ready to consider surgery at this time.

6-month follow-up. Dyskinesias improved with dose adjustment. Motor function fair — able to perform ADLs independently but notes increased difficulty with fine motor tasks (writing, buttoning). Freezing of gait episodes 1-2x/week. PT re-engaged for cueing strategies. UPDRS motor score 26. Cognition screened: MoCA 26/30 — within normal limits but will monitor for PD-related cognitive decline. Continue current regimen.

Referral for PD-related psychiatric symptoms. Reports increasing anxiety, particularly about disease progression. Also visual hallucinations — sees "shadow people" in peripheral vision, mainly in evening. Recognizes they are not real (insight preserved). PHQ-9: 6 (mild depression, improved on sertraline). GAD-7: 12 (moderate anxiety). Hallucinations likely PD-related — may consider pimavanserin if bothersome. For now, observation as insight is preserved. Added buspirone 5mg TID for anxiety. Avoid typical antipsychotics — contraindicated in PD.

Annual comprehensive PD review. H&Y stage 3. Motor fluctuations with 3-4 hours ON time per dose. Freezing episodes increasing. Dyskinesias mild. Visual hallucinations stable — non-bothersome, insight preserved. MoCA 24/30 (slight decline). Discussed DBS candidacy — pt now interested. Neuropsychological evaluation scheduled as part of DBS workup. Referred to movement disorder surgery team. Current medication burden is high (Stalevo QID + rasagiline + midodrine + sertraline + buspirone + melatonin + omeprazole + tamsulosin). Coordinating care across specialties.

24 y/o female presenting with 3-month history of intermittent bloody diarrhea (4-6 episodes/day), crampy abdominal pain, and urgency. Reports 6 lb weight loss. No recent travel or sick contacts. PMHx: asthma (albuterol PRN). Allergies: NKDA. Family hx: uncle with Crohn's disease. BP 108/66, HR 88, Temp 99.2F. Exam: diffuse abdominal tenderness, no peritoneal signs. Labs ordered: CBC, CMP, ESR, CRP, stool studies (C. diff, O&P, culture), fecal calprotectin. Urgent GI referral placed.

Labs reviewed: Hgb 10.8, MCV 78 (iron deficiency likely), ESR 48, CRP 4.2, fecal calprotectin 680 (markedly elevated). Stool studies negative for infection. Presentation highly suggestive of IBD. Flexible sigmoidoscopy scheduled for this week to expedite diagnosis. Iron studies ordered. Started iron supplementation.

Flexible sigmoidoscopy: continuous erythematous, edematous, friable mucosa from rectum to splenic flexure. Loss of vascular pattern. No skip lesions. Biopsies taken. Pathology: chronic active colitis with crypt distortion and cryptitis, consistent with ulcerative colitis. No granulomas (against Crohn's). No dysplasia. Full colonoscopy recommended once acute flare controlled for extent assessment. TPMT activity checked (normal) in anticipation of possible thiopurine use. Hepatitis B screening negative. TB QuantiFERON negative (preparing for possible biologic). Continue mesalamine, reassess in 4 weeks.

4-week follow-up. Stool frequency improved to 2-3/day but persistent blood and urgency. Partial Mayo score 5 (moderate). Mesalamine alone insufficient. Options discussed: steroids for induction vs. early biologic. Given moderate severity and desire to avoid steroids, starting vedolizumab (gut-selective, favorable safety profile in young woman). Induction: 300mg IV at weeks 0, 2, 6, then every 8 weeks. First infusion today, tolerated well.

Vedolizumab infusion #2 (week 2). Pt reports mild improvement — stool frequency down to 2/day, less blood. Urgency improving. CRP 2.1 (trending down). Iron studies: ferritin 12, iron saturation 14% — iron deficiency confirmed. Started IV iron sucrose infusion series (200mg x5) given poor oral absorption in active IBD. Continue mesalamine as adjunct.

Vedolizumab infusion #3 (week 6). Significant clinical improvement. Stool frequency 1-2/day, formed, no visible blood. No urgency. Partial Mayo score 1. CRP 0.6. Hgb 12.1 (improved post IV iron). Fecal calprotectin 85 (near normal). Excellent response. Continue maintenance vedolizumab every 8 weeks. Full colonoscopy scheduled in 3 months to confirm mucosal healing.

Surveillance colonoscopy: mucosa from rectum to splenic flexure shows complete mucosal healing — normal vascular pattern, no erythema, no friability. Proximal colon normal. Biopsies: quiescent colitis, no active inflammation. Deep remission achieved on vedolizumab + mesalamine. Outstanding outcome. Continue current regimen. Next colonoscopy in 1 year for surveillance.

Vedolizumab maintenance visit. Clinical remission sustained. No symptoms. Fecal calprotectin 42 (normal). Labs stable. Discussed long-term management — vedolizumab has favorable long-term safety. Contraception reviewed: combined OCP safe with UC (no increased VTE risk with vedolizumab, unlike some biologics). Flu vaccine administered (inactivated — safe on biologics). Avoid live vaccines.

Annual wellness visit. UC in remission on vedolizumab/mesalamine. Asthma well controlled, PRN albuterol use <2x/month. Weight recovered to baseline 132 lbs. BP 110/68. Labs all normal. Discussed mental health — adjusting well, no depression/anxiety symptoms. Updated vaccinations. Referred to dermatology for acne evaluation.

25 y/o female with moderate inflammatory acne on face and back. On vedolizumab for UC. Exam: comedonal and papulopustular acne, no cysts. Discussed treatment options — isotretinoin avoided given UC (potential GI risk, controversial). Started topical tretinoin 0.025% nightly + clindamycin/benzoyl peroxide gel AM. If inadequate, may consider oral spironolactone. RTC 8 weeks.

Acne follow-up. Moderate improvement on topical regimen. Tolerating tretinoin with minimal irritation. Inflammatory lesions reduced by ~50%. Added spironolactone 50mg daily for hormonal component. Discussed potential for menstrual irregularity. Continue topicals. RTC 3 months.

Annual UC surveillance colonoscopy. Complete mucosal healing maintained. No dysplasia on random biopsies. Fecal calprotectin 38. Deep remission sustained x2 years on vedolizumab. Discussed possibility of mesalamine discontinuation given biologic monotherapy may be sufficient — will continue for now given excellent tolerance. Next surveillance in 1-3 years per risk stratification.

Vedolizumab maintenance visit. Ongoing remission. No flares since initiation nearly 3 years ago. Vedolizumab trough level 18 mcg/mL (therapeutic). CRP <0.3. Discussed future family planning — vedolizumab considered low-risk in pregnancy per current data, but pre-conception planning with MFM recommended. Pt not planning pregnancy currently but wishes to be informed. Continue current regimen.

albuterol every 2-3 hours today. NKDA. Vitals: RR 24, HR 108, BP 118/74, SpO2
94% RA, Temp 37.3. Speaking in full sentences, widespread expiratory wheeze. PEF
245 L/min (58% of best 420). Tx: albuterol 5mg nebulized x3 (19:58, 20:15,
20:35) with ipratropium 0.5mg, prednisolone 40mg PO at 20:05. PEF 360 L/min
(86%) at 21:15 and 365 at 22:15, SpO2 97% RA, wheeze minimal. Dx: moderate acute
asthma exacerbation triggered by viral URI. Discharged home 22:40 (3 h 10 min in
ED) on prednisolone 40mg daily x5 days and new budesonide/formoterol 160/4.5 two
puffs BID; inhaler technique checked, written asthma action plan. Short steroid
course acceptable with UC; GI (Dr Okafor) informed. Follow-up: PCP (Dr Walsh)
within 48 h.

47 y/o male presenting for new patient visit. PMHx: gout (intermittent flares, on allopurinol 300mg), psoriasis (mild, topical clobetasol PRN), HLD (on pravastatin 40mg). Allergies: aspirin (bronchospasm — aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease). Social hx: non-smoker, social drinker 2-3 beers/week. BP 126/78, HR 70, BMI 29.8. Exam: few scattered psoriatic plaques on elbows and knees. No active gouty arthritis. Uric acid 6.2 (at goal on allopurinol). Lipids: LDL 112. Labs otherwise unremarkable. Advised weight reduction for gout and CVD risk.

48 y/o male presenting with acute onset severe R first MTP joint pain, swelling, and erythema overnight. Unable to bear weight. Reports dietary indiscretion (seafood dinner, 4 beers). On allopurinol 300mg — admits poor adherence recently. Exam: R first MTP exquisitely tender, erythematous, warm, swollen. Uric acid 9.8. WBC 12.4. Aspirate not performed (clinical diagnosis clear). NOTE: aspirin allergy (bronchospasm) — NO NSAIDs. Treated with colchicine 1.2mg then 0.6mg in 1 hour, followed by 0.6mg BID. Prednisone 40mg x5 day taper as adjunct. Counseled on allopurinol adherence. Follow-up with PCP.

Post-gout flare follow-up. Pain resolving on colchicine + prednisone taper. Discussed importance of allopurinol adherence — should NOT discontinue during flare. Uric acid target <6 mg/dL. Restarted consistent allopurinol. Counseled on trigger avoidance: alcohol, purine-rich foods, dehydration. Consider increasing allopurinol to 400mg if uric acid not controlled at next check. Colchicine 0.6mg daily as prophylaxis for 6 months.

Referral for recurrent gout despite allopurinol 300mg. Has had 3 flares in past year. Uric acid 7.4 (above target). Renal function normal (eGFR 92). Increased allopurinol to 400mg daily. Renal function and LFTs to be monitored. If target not achieved, will increase to 500-600mg (dose can go up to 800mg with monitoring). Discussed that aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease limits our anti-inflammatory options — colchicine and corticosteroids remain primary acute treatments. Continue colchicine prophylaxis.

Follow-up gout. Uric acid 5.8 on allopurinol 400mg — at goal. No flares since dose increase. Colchicine prophylaxis continuing. Joint exam: no synovitis. Dual-energy CT of feet ordered to assess for tophaceous deposits given recurrent disease. Continue current regimen. Plan to continue colchicine prophylaxis for total 6 months after achieving uric acid target.

DECT results: small monosodium urate deposits at R first MTP and L midfoot — subclinical tophaceous gout. No erosions on conventional CT. This reinforces need for long-term urate-lowering therapy. Target uric acid <5 mg/dL given tophaceous disease. Increased allopurinol to 500mg. Continue monitoring.

49 y/o male referred for worsening psoriasis. Previously mild plaque psoriasis on elbows/knees managed with topical clobetasol. Now new plaques on trunk, scalp, and gluteal cleft. BSA ~8% (moderate). PASI score 9.2. Discussed treatment escalation: phototherapy vs. systemic therapy. Given gout comorbidity (not a contraindication) and desire for convenient regimen, started apremilast 30mg BID (PDE4 inhibitor — oral, no immunosuppression). Titrated per protocol over first week. May benefit both psoriasis and potentially joint symptoms.

6-week follow-up on apremilast. GI side effects (nausea, diarrhea) in first 2 weeks, now resolved. Psoriasis improved — BSA ~5%, PASI 5.8. Scalp and trunk plaques thinning. Continue apremilast. If insufficient response at 16 weeks, may consider biologic (IL-17 or IL-23 inhibitor). Weight stable — apremilast can cause weight loss, monitoring.

16-week assessment of apremilast. PASI 4.2 (PASI-50 achieved but not PASI-75). BSA ~4%. Some residual plaques on elbows and scalp. Pt moderately satisfied. Given incomplete response, discussed escalation to biologic therapy. Recommended guselkumab (IL-23 inhibitor) — effective for moderate psoriasis, convenient dosing (every 8 weeks after induction). TB and hepatitis screening negative. Starting guselkumab 100mg SQ, loading doses at weeks 0 and 4, then every 8 weeks. Discontinuing apremilast.

Guselkumab 8-week assessment (received loading doses + first maintenance). Dramatic improvement — PASI 1.2, BSA <1%. Near-complete clearance. Pt very pleased. No injection site reactions. No infections. Continue guselkumab every 8 weeks. Discontinued clobetasol — no longer needed. Monitoring labs stable.

Annual exam. Gout controlled on allopurinol 500mg — uric acid 4.8, no flares x12 months. Colchicine prophylaxis discontinued. Psoriasis near-clear on guselkumab. HLD: LDL 108 on pravastatin — considering increase or switch given CVD risk factors (male, 50, BMI 29.5, HLD). Switched to rosuvastatin 10mg for greater LDL reduction. Weight 212 lbs — 5 lb loss since starting guselkumab (coincidental). BP 124/76. All other labs normal.

50 y/o male with aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease (AERD/Samter's triad) referred for evaluation of progressive nasal congestion and anosmia x6 months. Exam: bilateral nasal polyps grade 2-3, significantly obstructing airway. CT sinuses: bilateral pansinusitis with extensive polyposis. Discussed treatment: dupilumab (IL-4/IL-13 inhibitor) now FDA-approved for nasal polyps and would address AERD pathway. Alternatively, functional endoscopic sinus surgery (FESS). Given AERD, recommend dupilumab trial first — also coordinates with dermatology (potential benefit for residual psoriasis). Coordinating with allergist.

Started dupilumab 300mg SQ every 2 weeks (after 600mg loading dose). 8-week follow-up: significant improvement in nasal congestion and partial return of olfaction. Nasal endoscopy: polyps regressed to grade 1 bilateral. SNOT-22 score improved from 68 to 32. No injection site reactions. Continue dupilumab. Note: discussed with dermatology — may consider discontinuing guselkumab given dupilumab also has efficacy in psoriasis via IL-4/13 pathway, though primarily a Th2 agent. Will reassess.

Psoriasis check while on dupilumab for nasal polyps (guselkumab continued). Skin completely clear — PASI 0. Given excellent control and dupilumab's modest anti-psoriatic effect, trial of guselkumab discontinuation discussed. Will stop guselkumab and monitor — if psoriasis flares, will restart. Dupilumab continued for polyps. Close monitoring scheduled in 3 months.

3 months off guselkumab, on dupilumab only. Psoriasis remains clear — PASI 0. Dupilumab alone providing sufficient control, likely via Th2 modulation and downstream effects. Will continue monitoring. If any flare, restart guselkumab. Significant simplification of biologic regimen — one injection covering two indications (nasal polyps + psoriasis).

Annual exam. Complex multi-system management reviewed. Gout: well controlled, uric acid 4.6 on allopurinol 500mg, no flares x2 years. Psoriasis: clear on dupilumab alone. Nasal polyps: excellent response to dupilumab, olfaction restored. AERD stable. LDL 78 on rosuvastatin 10mg — at goal. BMI 28.8 (continued gradual weight loss). BP 122/74. All labs normal. Active meds: allopurinol 500mg, rosuvastatin 10mg, dupilumab 300mg q2wk, omeprazole 20mg, tamsulosin 0.4mg. Polypharmacy minimized where possible. Pt in best health in years.

76-year-old female presenting for annual wellness visit. PMH significant for hypertension (diagnosed 2005), osteoarthritis bilateral knees, and hyperlipidemia. Current medications: amlodipine 5mg daily, atorvastatin 20mg daily, acetaminophen PRN. BP 142/88, HR 72, BMI 26.1. Patient reports occasional knee pain limiting mobility. Lipid panel ordered. Will continue current regimen and reassess BP at next visit.

Follow-up for hypertension management. BP today 148/92 despite amlodipine 5mg daily. Patient admits to high sodium intake over holidays. LDL from January labs returned at 118 mg/dL, above target for her risk profile. Increasing amlodipine to 10mg daily and atorvastatin to 40mg daily. Dietary counseling provided. Recheck BP in 6 weeks. Family history notable for mother with stroke at age 72.

BP recheck visit. BP 134/82 on amlodipine 10mg, improved from prior. Patient reports mild ankle edema, likely medication-related. Kidney function stable with eGFR 62 mL/min. Will monitor edema; if worsening, consider switching to ACE inhibitor. Continue current medications. Return in 3 months.

Referred by Dr. Whitfield for routine diabetic screening, though patient is not diabetic. Comprehensive eye exam reveals early nuclear sclerotic cataracts OU, worse OS than OD. Visual acuity OD 20/30, OS 20/40. IOP 16/18 mmHg. No diabetic retinopathy. Recommend follow-up in 12 months; cataract surgery discussion when vision impairs daily function.

78-year-old female referred for worsening bilateral knee pain. X-rays demonstrate moderate-to-severe tricompartmental OA bilaterally, with joint space narrowing and osteophyte formation. Patient has failed conservative management with acetaminophen and physical therapy. Discussed options including corticosteroid injections, viscosupplementation, and eventual TKA. Patient elects trial of intra-articular corticosteroid injection right knee today. Allergy to sulfa drugs noted. Follow-up in 8 weeks.

Follow-up post right knee corticosteroid injection. Patient reports approximately 60% improvement in right knee pain lasting about 5 weeks, now gradually returning. Left knee remains symptomatic. Administered corticosteroid injection left knee today. Discussed timeline for potential bilateral TKA; patient prefers to delay surgery. Prescribed topical diclofenac gel for adjunctive relief.

Annual wellness visit. BP 138/84, well controlled. BMI 26.8, slight increase. Labs: LDL 96 mg/dL on atorvastatin 40mg, HbA1c 5.9% (prediabetic range, new finding). eGFR 58 mL/min, mild decline from prior. Discussed lifestyle modifications for prediabetes prevention: dietary changes, increased activity within limits of knee OA. Referred to nutritionist. Flu and pneumococcal vaccines administered.

79-year-old female presenting with acute onset dizziness and near-syncope at home. BP 98/60, HR 88, orthostatic positive. No chest pain, no focal neurological deficits. ECG: normal sinus rhythm, no acute ST changes. BMP: Na 134, K 3.2, Cr 1.4 (baseline ~1.2). Suspect dehydration and possible over-antihypertensive effect. Administered 1L NS IV. Held amlodipine. Admitted for observation. Potassium replacement initiated.

Post-discharge follow-up after 2-day admission for near-syncope and dehydration. BP today 128/78 off amlodipine. Potassium normalized at 4.1. Creatinine back to 1.2. Given improved BP control, will trial holding amlodipine and monitor. Continue atorvastatin 40mg. Recheck in 2 weeks. Patient counseled on hydration, especially in warmer months.

Routine follow-up. BP 144/86 without antihypertensive for 3 months, trending upward. HbA1c now 6.1%, progressing toward diabetes threshold. Weight stable. Restarting antihypertensive therapy with lisinopril 10mg daily (switching from amlodipine given prior edema and hypotension). Starting metformin 500mg daily for prediabetes/early diabetes prevention. Renal function acceptable for metformin use with eGFR 60.

6-month follow-up. BP 132/80 on lisinopril 10mg, well tolerated, no cough. HbA1c 5.8%, improved with metformin and dietary changes. Patient has been working with nutritionist. eGFR stable at 61. LDL 92. Knee pain managed with topical diclofenac. Overall stable. Continue current regimen. Annual labs in 6 months.

Annual eye exam follow-up. Cataract progression noted OS, visual acuity now 20/50. OD stable at 20/30. Patient reports difficulty reading and driving at night. IOP normal. Discussed cataract extraction with IOL implantation OS. Patient agrees to proceed. Pre-op workup ordered. Surgery scheduled for November.

Post-operative day 1 following uncomplicated phacoemulsification with posterior chamber IOL placement OS. Visual acuity OS 20/25 uncorrected, significant improvement. No signs of infection or elevated IOP. Prednisolone acetate 1% and moxifloxacin drops prescribed. Follow-up in 1 week, then 1 month.

Annual wellness exam. Patient is 81 years old, generally doing well. BP 130/78, HR 68, BMI 25.9. HbA1c 5.7%, excellent control maintained. eGFR 57, stable CKD stage 3a. LDL 88. Cataract surgery OS successful per ophthalmology notes, vision much improved. Knee pain chronic but manageable. Bone density scan ordered given age and gender. Continue lisinopril 10mg, atorvastatin 40mg, metformin 500mg. Shingrix vaccine series initiated.

Referred by Dr. Whitfield for evaluation of new-onset bilateral hand stiffness and swelling, worse in mornings, lasting >1 hour. Exam reveals MCP and PIP joint synovitis bilaterally. RF positive at 48 IU/mL, anti-CCP 62 U/mL, ESR 38, CRP 1.8. X-rays hands: periarticular osteopenia, no erosions yet. Diagnosis: seropositive rheumatoid arthritis. Starting hydroxychloroquine 200mg BID. Discussed disease course and importance of early treatment. Baseline eye exam for HCQ toxicity screening recommended. Follow-up in 8 weeks.

Follow-up for newly diagnosed RA on hydroxychloroquine 200mg BID for 10 weeks. Morning stiffness reduced from >60 min to ~20 min. Swelling improved but persistent in right 2nd and 3rd MCP joints. ESR 28, CRP 1.1, trending down. Tolerating HCQ well, no GI side effects. Will continue current therapy and reassess in 3 months. If inadequate response, will consider adding methotrexate (noting patient already on metformin, will monitor hepatic function closely).

33-year-old male presenting for new patient intake. Recently relocated. No significant PMH. Family history: father with type 2 DM, mother with breast cancer at age 58. No medications, NKDA. BP 122/78, HR 68, BMI 28.4. Routine labs ordered including CBC, CMP, lipid panel, HbA1c given family history. Patient is a non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Counseled on weight management.

Lab results review via phone visit. CBC normal. CMP unremarkable, fasting glucose 102 mg/dL. Lipid panel: TC 218, LDL 142, HDL 44, TG 160. HbA1c 5.6%. Borderline dyslipidemia and impaired fasting glucose. Given age and family history of DM, recommend lifestyle modification: Mediterranean diet, 150 min/week moderate exercise, weight loss goal of 10 lbs. Recheck in 6 months. Statin deferred for now.

6-month follow-up. Patient has lost 6 lbs, now BMI 27.5. Reports regular exercise 3x/week. Repeat fasting glucose 98, LDL 128, HDL 48, TG 138. Improvement noted. BP 118/74. Continue lifestyle modifications. Will recheck annually unless concerns arise.

34-year-old male self-referred for evaluation of changing mole on upper back, noticed by partner. Exam reveals 8mm asymmetric pigmented lesion with irregular borders at T4 level, right paravertebral. Dermatoscopic findings concerning for atypical melanocytic proliferation. Excisional biopsy performed today with 2mm margins. Specimen sent to pathology. Discussed importance of full skin exam. Three other benign-appearing nevi noted and documented. Follow-up upon pathology results.

Pathology results: severely dysplastic compound nevus with positive deep margin. No melanoma identified. Recommend re-excision with wider margins to ensure complete removal. Patient counseled on the benign but atypical nature of the lesion. Re-excision scheduled for next week. Advised monthly self-skin checks and annual dermatology follow-up given family history of cancer and atypical nevi.

Re-excision of atypical nevus upper back with 5mm margins performed under local anesthesia. Procedure well tolerated. Wound closed primarily. Pathology pending. Follow-up in 10 days for suture removal. Patient to avoid heavy lifting for 2 weeks.

Annual visit. Weight stable at BMI 27.2. BP 120/76, HR 72. Labs: fasting glucose 100, HbA1c 5.5%, LDL 124, HDL 50. Continued improvement in lipid profile with lifestyle changes alone. Dermatology follow-up up to date, re-excision margins clear per outside records. No new concerns. Tdap booster administered. Continue annual visits.

36-year-old male presenting with acute right lower quadrant pain x12 hours, associated with nausea and one episode of emesis. Temp 38.1°C, BP 130/82, HR 96. Exam: RLQ tenderness with rebound, positive McBurney point. WBC 14.2, CRP 4.8. CT abdomen/pelvis: inflamed appendix with periappendiceal fat stranding, no perforation. Diagnosis: acute uncomplicated appendicitis. General surgery consulted. Patient consented for laparoscopic appendectomy. NPO, IV fluids and cefoxitin initiated.

Post-op day 1 following uncomplicated laparoscopic appendectomy. Patient tolerated procedure well, operative time 42 minutes. Pathology: acute suppurative appendicitis, no perforation. Tolerating clear liquids, passing flatus. Pain controlled with oral acetaminophen and ibuprofen, avoiding opioids per patient preference. Ambulating independently. Discharge planned today with 1-week follow-up.

36-year-old male self-referred for evaluation of persistent low mood, poor concentration, and insomnia over the past 3 months following job loss. PHQ-9 score 14 (moderate depression). No suicidal ideation. No prior psychiatric history. Denies substance use. Sleep hygiene is poor with excessive screen time at night. Diagnosis: major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate. Initiating sertraline 50mg daily. Discussed side effect profile including initial GI upset and potential sexual dysfunction. Cognitive behavioral therapy referral provided. Follow-up in 4 weeks.

4-week follow-up on sertraline 50mg. Patient reports mild improvement in mood, sleep somewhat better. PHQ-9 score 11. Mild nausea first week that resolved. No sexual side effects. Has started CBT sessions weekly. Increasing sertraline to 100mg daily for further benefit. Continue CBT. Follow-up in 6 weeks.

Follow-up at 10 weeks of sertraline treatment, now 100mg daily for 6 weeks. Significant improvement. PHQ-9 score 5 (mild). Patient secured new employment, feeling more motivated. Sleep normalized. CBT ongoing, finding it helpful. Continue sertraline 100mg. Will plan taper discussion at 9-12 months if sustained remission. Follow-up in 3 months.

Annual visit. Patient doing well overall. Depression in remission on sertraline 100mg, psychiatry planning taper. BMI 27.0, BP 118/74. Labs: fasting glucose 104, HbA1c 5.7%, LDL 130, HDL 48. Slight uptick in glucose markers; reinforced dietary and exercise counseling. Discussed 10-year ASCVD risk calculation: 3.8%, low risk, statin not indicated at this time. Dermatology annual check scheduled. Continue monitoring metabolic parameters.

37-year-old male referred by PCP for persistent heartburn and epigastric discomfort x4 months, partially responsive to OTC omeprazole. No dysphagia, weight loss, or GI bleeding. No NSAID use. EGD performed today: LA Grade B erosive esophagitis, small hiatal hernia, negative for Barrett's. CLO test negative for H. pylori. Started on pantoprazole 40mg daily x8 weeks. Lifestyle modifications reviewed: elevate HOB, avoid late meals, limit caffeine and alcohol. Follow-up in 8 weeks. Repeat EGD in 8-12 weeks to confirm healing.

Annual visit. Age 38. GERD well controlled on pantoprazole, stepped down to 20mg daily successfully. Depression: completed sertraline taper, off medication since January, mood stable. BMI 26.8, BP 116/72. Labs: HbA1c 5.6%, LDL 122, fasting glucose 99. Metabolic parameters stable with continued lifestyle efforts. Skin exam clear per dermatology. No acute concerns. Return in 1 year.

59-year-old female presenting for routine annual exam. PMH: type 2 diabetes mellitus (diagnosed 2010), hypertension, obesity. Medications: metformin 1000mg BID, lisinopril 20mg daily. Allergies: penicillin (rash). BP 146/90, HR 78, BMI 34.2. HbA1c 7.8%, above target. Fasting glucose 168 mg/dL. Cr 0.9, eGFR 78. Urine microalbumin/creatinine ratio 45 mg/g (mildly elevated). LDL 148. Adding glipizide 5mg BID and atorvastatin 20mg. Discussed weight loss strategies and diabetic nephropathy prevention.

Follow-up for diabetes and hypertension management. HbA1c 7.3%, improved. Fasting glucose 142. Patient tolerating glipizide, no hypoglycemic episodes. BP 140/86 on lisinopril 20mg. Increasing lisinopril to 40mg. LDL 118 on atorvastatin. Weight down 3 lbs. Continue current diabetes regimen. Reinforced importance of annual eye and foot exams. Referral to diabetic educator.

60-year-old female with T2DM x9 years for annual diabetic retinopathy screening. Visual acuity OD 20/25, OS 20/25. IOP 14/15. Dilated fundoscopic exam: mild non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy (NPDR) OU with scattered microaneurysms. No macular edema on OCT. Recommend strict glycemic and BP control. Follow-up in 12 months; sooner if vision changes.

Follow-up. HbA1c 7.1%, gradual improvement but not at goal of <7%. BP 134/82 on lisinopril 40mg, improved. Weight stable. Foot exam: intact sensation to monofilament bilaterally, no ulcerations. Given suboptimal glycemic control despite metformin and glipizide, adding empagliflozin 10mg daily for additional glucose lowering, weight loss, and cardiovascular/renal benefit. Reviewed SGLT2 inhibitor precautions including genital mycotic infections and volume depletion.

Follow-up at 4 months on empagliflozin. HbA1c 6.7%, now at target. Fasting glucose 124. Patient has lost 5 lbs since starting SGLT2i. No UTI or yeast infections. BP 128/78. Urine microalbumin/creatinine ratio improved to 32 mg/g. Excellent response. Continue all current medications. Annual labs in 3 months.

61-year-old female with DM, HTN, and dyslipidemia referred for cardiovascular risk assessment. Stress echocardiography performed: achieved 7.2 METS, no wall motion abnormalities at peak stress, EF 60%. ECG: normal sinus rhythm, no ischemic changes. Coronary artery calcium score 82 Agatston units (moderate risk for her age). Recommend aggressive risk factor modification. Discussed aspirin 81mg daily given CAC score and multiple risk factors. Continue statin. Follow-up as needed.

Annual exam. Patient overall doing well. HbA1c 6.6%, well controlled on metformin, glipizide, and empagliflozin. BP 126/76. BMI 32.8, down from 34.2. LDL 98 on atorvastatin 20mg. eGFR 76, stable. Added ASA 81mg per cardiology recommendation. Diabetic retinopathy screening due. Mammogram and colonoscopy up to date. Flu vaccine given.

62-year-old female presenting with severe left great toe pain, erythema, and swelling x2 days. Unable to bear weight. Temp 37.6°C, BP 138/84. Exam: left 1st MTP joint erythematous, hot, exquisitely tender. No open wound. Joint aspiration performed: negatively birefringent needle-shaped crystals under polarized microscopy, consistent with gout. WBC 11.8, uric acid 9.2 mg/dL, Cr 1.0. Started colchicine 1.2mg followed by 0.6mg in 1 hour. NSAIDS avoided given renal considerations with her SGLT2i. Ice, elevation. PCP follow-up in 1 week for urate-lowering therapy discussion.

Follow-up post acute gout flare left 1st MTP. Symptoms resolved with colchicine. Uric acid 9.2 at time of flare. Given this is first episode, discussing risks and benefits of urate-lowering therapy. Patient had significant disability during flare. Starting allopurinol 100mg daily with plan to titrate to target uric acid <6 mg/dL. Continuing colchicine 0.6mg daily as prophylaxis during allopurinol initiation. Recheck uric acid in 4 weeks. Note: penicillin allergy documented (rash), no cross-reactivity concern with allopurinol.

Annual exam. Gout well controlled, no recurrent flares on allopurinol 200mg daily (titrated up), uric acid 5.4 mg/dL. Colchicine prophylaxis discontinued after 6 months. HbA1c 6.5%. BP 124/76. BMI 32.1. LDL 94. eGFR 74. Diabetic eye exam done: stable mild NPDR per ophthalmology. All preventive care up to date. Continue current medications. Patient interested in weight loss program; referred to bariatric medicine.

Follow-up. Patient enrolled in medically supervised weight loss program. Down 12 lbs over 6 months, BMI now 30.4. HbA1c 6.2%, best ever. Considering dose reduction of glipizide given improved control and weight loss. Reduced glipizide from 5mg BID to 5mg daily. Continue metformin and empagliflozin. BP 122/74. Recheck HbA1c in 3 months to ensure stable control with dose reduction.

Follow-up. HbA1c 6.3% after glipizide reduction, stable. Weight loss plateaued at BMI 30.0. BP 120/74. No hypoglycemia. Gout quiescent, uric acid 5.2. All markers stable. Discontinuing glipizide entirely as trial; patient will monitor fingerstick glucoses. Continue metformin 1000mg BID and empagliflozin 10mg. Recheck in 3 months.

Annual exam. HbA1c 6.4% off glipizide, acceptable. Successfully maintaining on dual therapy with metformin and empagliflozin. Weight stable, BMI 29.8, first time under 30 in years. BP 122/76. LDL 90. eGFR 72. Urine albumin/creatinine 28, improved. Diabetic eye exam: stable mild NPDR. No gout flares x2 years. Excellent disease management. Continue current regimen.

65-year-old female referred by PCP for episodic right-sided headaches with visual aura x3 months. Episodes occur 2-3x/month, preceded by scintillating scotoma lasting 20 minutes, followed by unilateral throbbing headache, nausea, and photophobia lasting 4-6 hours. No prior migraine history. Neurological exam normal. MRI brain ordered to exclude secondary causes given new-onset migraine in a patient over 50. Started sumatriptan 50mg PRN for acute episodes. Discussed migraine diary. If frequent, will consider prophylaxis.

Follow-up. MRI brain: no mass, no white matter lesions, no vascular abnormality. Reassuring. Patient has had 5 migraine episodes in past 6 weeks, meeting criteria for prophylactic therapy. Sumatriptan partially effective. Given her cardiovascular history, avoiding beta-blockers as first line (already on ACEi/statin). Starting topiramate 25mg nightly, titrating to 50mg in 2 weeks. Note: topiramate may aid weight management as added benefit. Follow-up in 8 weeks. Continue migraine diary.

48-year-old male referred for persistent cough x6 months and exertional dyspnea. 25 pack-year smoking history, quit 2 years ago. No hemoptysis, no weight loss. BP 128/80, HR 74, SpO2 96% on RA. Chest X-ray: hyperinflation, flattened diaphragms. Spirometry: FEV1 68% predicted, FEV1/FVC 0.62, positive bronchodilator response (12% improvement). Diagnosis: moderate COPD, GOLD stage II. Initiated tiotropium 18mcg inhaler daily. Smoking cessation reinforced. Flu and pneumococcal vaccines recommended. Follow-up in 3 months.

Follow-up for COPD. Patient reports improved dyspnea on tiotropium, able to walk 2 blocks without stopping. Cough less frequent. SpO2 97% on RA. No exacerbations. Reviewed inhaler technique, adequate. Added albuterol MDI PRN for breakthrough symptoms. Encouraged pulmonary rehabilitation enrollment. Repeat PFTs in 6 months. Continue tiotropium.

48-year-old male for annual exam. PMH: COPD (managed by pulmonology), former smoker, mild anxiety. Medications: tiotropium, albuterol PRN. No allergies. BP 132/84, HR 70, BMI 30.2. Labs: glucose 94, lipid panel normal (LDL 108, HDL 52), CBC normal. PSA not indicated at this age per guidelines. Discussed colon cancer screening; patient to schedule colonoscopy (age appropriate). Continue smoking abstinence.

6-month PFT follow-up. FEV1 70% predicted, stable. FEV1/FVC 0.63. SpO2 97%. Patient enrolled in pulmonary rehab, attending 2x/week, reports improved exercise tolerance. No COPD exacerbations since diagnosis. Continue current regimen. Annual CT low-dose lung cancer screening ordered given 25 pack-year history and age. Next PFT in 12 months.

49-year-old male presenting for screening colonoscopy. Prep adequate. Findings: two sessile polyps in sigmoid colon (6mm and 4mm), removed by snare polypectomy. One 3mm hyperplastic polyp in rectum, not removed. No other lesions to cecum. Pathology pending. If adenomatous, repeat colonoscopy in 5 years. Follow-up for pathology results.

Pathology results: 6mm sigmoid polyp = tubular adenoma with low-grade dysplasia; 4mm sigmoid polyp = hyperplastic. Given tubular adenoma, recommend surveillance colonoscopy in 5 years per guidelines. Continue high-fiber diet. Patient informed via phone and documentation updated.

49-year-old male with known COPD presenting with 3-day history of worsening dyspnea, increased sputum production (purulent), and low-grade fever 37.9°C. SpO2 91% on RA, HR 102, RR 22, BP 136/88. Bilateral expiratory wheezes, poor air entry. ABG: pH 7.38, PaCO2 44, PaO2 62. CXR: hyperinflated lungs, no consolidation. Dx: acute COPD exacerbation, likely infectious trigger. Started prednisone 40mg, azithromycin 500mg, nebulized albuterol/ipratropium q4h. Supplemental O2 2L NC. Admitted to medicine.

Inpatient pulmonology consult day 4 of admission for COPD exacerbation. Patient improving, SpO2 95% on RA, RR 16. Weaned off supplemental O2. Completing 5-day course of prednisone and azithromycin. Recommend stepping up maintenance therapy: adding budesonide/formoterol 160/4.5 BID to existing tiotropium (triple therapy indication given exacerbation history). Continue albuterol PRN. Discharge tomorrow with pulmonary rehab resumption in 2 weeks. Smoking status confirmed: still abstinent.

6-month post-exacerbation follow-up. Patient on triple therapy: tiotropium + budesonide/formoterol. No further exacerbations. Dyspnea at baseline. FEV1 66% predicted, slight decline from pre-exacerbation. SpO2 96%. LDCT lung screening: negative for nodules, emphysematous changes noted. Continue current regimen. Annual PFTs and LDCT. Influenza vaccine administered.

Annual exam. COPD stable on triple therapy, no exacerbations x1 year. BMI 29.4, down slightly. BP 130/82. Labs: glucose 96, HbA1c 5.4%, LDL 112, eGFR >90. Patient reports occasional anxiety about health since COPD diagnosis and hospitalization. PHQ-9 score 4, GAD-7 score 8 (mild anxiety). Discussed options; patient prefers non-pharmacological approach. Referred to counseling. Continue COPD management per pulmonology.

51-year-old male presenting with 3-month history of right shoulder pain, worse with overhead activities. No trauma. Exam: painful arc 60-120°, positive Neer and Hawkins signs, weakness in external rotation. MRI right shoulder: partial thickness supraspinatus tear, moderate subacromial bursitis. Recommend conservative management: physical therapy 2x/week x6 weeks, subacromial corticosteroid injection today. Avoid heavy lifting. Follow-up in 6 weeks. NSAIDs used cautiously given mild anxiety about medications.

Follow-up right shoulder. Significant improvement with PT and injection. Pain 3/10 from 7/10 at initial visit. ROM nearly full, strength improving. Continue PT for 4 more weeks then transition to home exercise program. No surgical intervention needed at this time. Return if symptoms recur.

Annual pulmonary follow-up. No COPD exacerbations in past 2 years on triple therapy. FEV1 65% predicted, stable. 6-minute walk test: 420 meters, adequate. SpO2 stable at 96%. LDCT screening: stable emphysema, no new nodules. CAT score 12, moderate impact. Continue triple therapy. Pulmonary rehab maintenance encouraged. Next visit in 12 months.

Annual exam. Age 53. COPD stable. Shoulder resolved. BMI 29.0, trending down with continued exercise from pulmonary rehab. BP 126/78. Labs: LDL 118, HbA1c 5.3%, all within normal limits. Anxiety improved with counseling, GAD-7 score 4. Colonoscopy surveillance due in 2024. Preventive care up to date. No acute issues.

Annual pulmonary visit. FEV1 64% predicted, stable decline consistent with treated COPD trajectory. No exacerbations. Patient remains active in pulmonary rehab maintenance program. LDCT: stable. SpO2 96%. Plan: continue triple therapy (tiotropium, budesonide/formoterol). Patient asks about newer therapies; discussed potential role of biologics if eosinophilic phenotype identified, but blood eosinophils 180 cells/μL, not elevated. Current regimen appropriate. Annual follow-up.

Annual pulmonary visit. 55 y/o male with moderate COPD (GOLD stage II) on triple therapy since March 2020: tiotropium 18mcg daily (LAMA) + budesonide/formoterol 160/4.5 2 puffs BID (ICS/LABA), albuterol PRN. Post-bronchodilator spirometry today (April 15, 2026): FEV1 62% predicted, FEV1/FVC 0.61. One moderate exacerbation in the past 12 months — December 9, 2025, treated as outpatient with prednisone 40mg x5 days, no antibiotics, no hospitalization. No other exacerbations; last hospitalization March 2020. No home O2 or NIV, SpO2 96% on RA. Former smoker, 25 pack-years, quit 2016. 12% bronchodilator response at diagnosis in 2018, but no clinical diagnosis of asthma. No bronchiectasis, ILD or lung cancer; LDCT January 2026: stable emphysema, no nodules. CBC today: WBC 6.8, eosinophils 310 cells/μL (0.31 x10^9/L), up from 180 in 2024. Continue triple therapy. Pulmonary rehab maintenance. Annual LDCT and PFTs. Follow-up 12 months.

24-year-old female presenting for annual well-woman exam. G0P0. LMP 2 weeks ago, regular 28-day cycles. On combined OCP (ethinyl estradiol/levonorgestrel) x3 years. No breakthrough bleeding. Pap smear performed, HPV co-testing. Breast exam normal. BP 110/68, BMI 22.4. No complaints. Discussed STI screening; chlamydia/gonorrhea NAAT obtained. Family history notable for maternal grandmother with ovarian cancer at age 68.
Results callback. Pap smear: NILM, HPV negative. STI screening negative. Continue current contraception. Routine screening in 3 years per guidelines given age and normal results.

25-year-old female presenting with 2-week history of fatigue, pallor, and heavy menstrual periods over the past 4 months. No prior anemia diagnosis. BP 108/64, HR 88, BMI 22.0. Exam: conjunctival pallor noted. Labs: Hgb 9.8 g/dL, MCV 72 fL, ferritin 8 ng/mL, TIBC elevated. Iron deficiency anemia secondary to menorrhagia. Started ferrous sulfate 325mg BID on empty stomach with vitamin C. Referred back to OB/GYN for menorrhagia evaluation. Recheck CBC in 8 weeks.

Follow-up for menorrhagia causing iron deficiency anemia. Patient reports periods lasting 8-9 days with heavy flow and clots. No intermenstrual bleeding. Pelvic ultrasound ordered: normal uterine size, no fibroids, no polyps, endometrial stripe 6mm. Labs: TSH 2.1, coagulation studies normal. Likely dysfunctional uterine bleeding. Discussed options: switching from OCP to levonorgestrel IUD for better menstrual control, or trial of tranexamic acid during menses. Patient opts for Mirena IUD. Insertion scheduled.

Levonorgestrel IUD (Mirena) inserted today without complication. Patient tolerated procedure well with minimal cramping. Proper placement confirmed on post-insertion ultrasound. Ibuprofen 400mg provided for cramping. Counseled on expected irregular spotting for 3-6 months followed by lighter or absent periods. String check in 6 weeks. Discontinue OCP.

Follow-up iron deficiency anemia. Patient reports lighter periods since Mirena placement. Repeat labs: Hgb 11.8 g/dL (up from 9.8), ferritin 22 ng/mL. Improving but ferritin still low. Continue iron supplementation for 3 more months to replete stores. Recheck ferritin when complete.
Recheck. Hgb 13.1 g/dL, ferritin 48 ng/mL, normalized. Periods now very light with Mirena. Discontinue iron supplementation. Patient feeling well, energy levels back to normal. Annual visit in fall.

26-year-old female self-referred for acne flare over past 3 months, predominantly chin and jawline. Reports worsening since stopping OCP and transitioning to IUD. Exam: moderate inflammatory papulopustular acne lower face and neck. No nodules or cysts. No hirsutism. Previous trials of benzoyl peroxide with partial response. Started tretinoin 0.025% cream nightly and doxycycline 100mg daily. Discussed sun protection. Avoid in pregnancy (unlikely with IUD). Follow-up in 8 weeks.

Acne follow-up. Moderate improvement on tretinoin and doxycycline 8 weeks. New lesions decreased by ~50%. Some dryness from tretinoin managed with moisturizer. Plan to continue doxycycline for 2 more months then transition to topical maintenance only. Increase tretinoin to 0.05% as tolerated. Spironolactone discussed as alternative if topicals insufficient long-term given hormonal pattern.

Annual well-woman exam. Mirena in place, strings visible, 20 months post-insertion. Periods essentially absent, patient very satisfied. No vaginal discharge or pelvic pain. Breast exam normal. Pap not due (last normal 2019, next due 2022). Performing Pap + HPV co-test today. Discussed genetic counseling given family history of ovarian cancer in grandmother; patient interested, referral placed.

Annual exam. Age 27. Iron studies normal, Hgb 13.4. BMI 22.2, BP 112/70. No acute complaints. Acne improving with topical regimen per dermatology. Pap/HPV results: NILM, HPV negative. Reviewed with patient. Genetic counseling appointment scheduled for next month. All routine screening up to date. Continue Mirena.

Patient presents with 5-day history of sore throat, low-grade fever (38.0°C), and cervical lymphadenopathy. No cough or rhinorrhea. Exam: erythematous posterior pharynx with tonsillar exudates bilaterally. Centor score 4. Rapid strep positive. Allergies: none known. Prescribed amoxicillin 500mg TID x10 days. Symptomatic care with ibuprofen and warm saltwater gargles. Return if worsening or no improvement in 48 hours.

28-year-old female presenting for preconception counseling. Patient and partner planning pregnancy in 6-12 months. Mirena removal discussed and planned for 3 months before intended conception. Prenatal vitamins with folic acid 800mcg started. Rubella immunity confirmed from prior vaccination. Varicella immune. Hgb 13.2, blood type A+, antibody screen negative. TSH 1.8. Genetic counseling completed: not a BRCA carrier, reassuring given family history. Discussed optimizing BMI and lifestyle prior to conception.

Mirena IUD removed without complication. Strings intact, device intact. Patient counseled that fertility typically returns within 1-3 months. May have adjustment bleeding. Continue prenatal vitamins. Tracking ovulation with LH kits. Follow-up when pregnant or in 6 months if not conceived. Discussed age-appropriate reassurance that intervention not typically indicated until 12 months of trying.

Patient presents with positive home pregnancy test, LMP approximately 5 weeks ago. Urine hCG positive in office. Quantitative beta-hCG 4,200 mIU/mL. Transvaginal ultrasound: intrauterine gestational sac, yolk sac visible, CRL not yet measurable. Estimated 5w2d. No ectopic features. Dating scan scheduled at 8 weeks. Reviewed first trimester precautions, nausea management, and prenatal visit schedule. Continue prenatal vitamins. Congratulations offered.

72-year-old male referred for evaluation of exertional chest tightness and dyspnea on exertion x3 months. PMH: hypertension x20 years, hyperlipidemia, former smoker (quit 1990). Medications: amlodipine 10mg, rosuvastatin 10mg. Allergy to ACE inhibitors (angioedema). BP 148/88, HR 72, BMI 27.8. ECG: NSR, LVH by voltage criteria. Stress echo: inducible anterior wall hypokinesis at peak stress, suggestive of LAD territory ischemia. EF 55%. Recommend cardiac catheterization. ASA 81mg added. Discussed risks/benefits.

Cardiac catheterization performed. Findings: 80% stenosis mid-LAD, 50% stenosis proximal LCx, RCA patent. LV function normal. Successful PCI with drug-eluting stent to mid-LAD. No complications. Post-procedure troponin flat. Started dual antiplatelet therapy: ASA 81mg + clopidogrel 75mg daily (minimum 12 months). Uptitrated rosuvastatin to 40mg. Added metoprolol succinate 25mg daily. ACE inhibitor contraindicated due to angioedema history; starting losartan 50mg (ARB safe alternative). Cardiac rehab referral.

6-week post-PCI follow-up. Patient doing well, no recurrent chest pain. Tolerating medications. BP 132/78 on amlodipine 10mg + losartan 50mg + metoprolol 25mg. HR 64. No bleeding on DAPT. Enrolled in cardiac rehab, attending 3x/week. LDL target reassessed: goal <70 mg/dL post-ACS. Labs: LDL 82 on rosuvastatin 40mg. Consider adding ezetimibe if not at goal on recheck. Continue all medications.

6-month post-PCI. No angina. Completed 12 weeks of cardiac rehab, continues independent exercise. BP 126/74. HR 60. LDL 68 mg/dL on rosuvastatin 40mg, at goal. Echo: EF 58%, no new wall motion abnormalities. Continue DAPT until at least March 2019. All medications well tolerated. Next visit in 6 months.

12 months post-PCI. Asymptomatic. Completing 12 months DAPT. Transitioning to ASA 81mg monotherapy, discontinuing clopidogrel. BP 124/72 on triple antihypertensive therapy, excellent control. LDL 64. Continue metoprolol, amlodipine, losartan, rosuvastatin, ASA. Annual follow-up unless symptoms.

74-year-old male referred for elevated PSA 5.8 ng/mL on routine screening (prior 3.2 two years ago). DRE: mildly enlarged prostate, no nodules, smooth. IPSS score 12 (moderate LUTS). Reports nocturia x2-3, weak stream, hesitancy. Labs: PSA free/total ratio 18% (borderline). Discussed options: mpMRI prostate for further risk stratification vs. biopsy. Patient elects mpMRI first. Also started tamsulosin 0.4mg nightly for LUTS.

mpMRI prostate results: PI-RADS 3 lesion (equivocal) in right peripheral zone, 12mm. Prostate volume 55cc. No extracapsular extension. Given equivocal MRI and rising PSA, recommend MRI-fusion targeted biopsy with systematic sampling. Discussed risks: bleeding, infection, urinary retention. Prescribed prophylactic ciprofloxacin (noting no drug interactions with current cardiac medications). Biopsy scheduled.

Transrectal MRI-fusion prostate biopsy performed: 4 targeted cores from PI-RADS 3 lesion + 12 systematic cores. Procedure tolerated well under local anesthesia. Mild hematuria expected. Holding ASA 3 days pre-procedure (discussed with cardiologist Dr. Cheng, deemed safe >12 months post-PCI). Resumed ASA today. Pathology pending. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

Biopsy results: targeted cores show Gleason 3+3=6 (Grade Group 1) adenocarcinoma in 2 of 4 cores, maximum 15% core involvement. Systematic cores: 1/12 positive with Gleason 3+3=6. Low-volume, low-grade prostate cancer. Discussed management options extensively: active surveillance vs. radical prostatectomy vs. radiation. Given low grade, low volume, and patient age 74, recommend active surveillance with PSA q6 months and repeat MRI/biopsy in 12 months. Patient agrees with AS protocol.

Annual cardiology visit. 2+ years post LAD stent. Asymptomatic, exercising regularly. BP 122/72. HR 58. ECG: NSR, unchanged LVH. LDL 62. Cardiac function stable. Discussed prostate cancer diagnosis and active surveillance plan, no contraindication from cardiac standpoint for any future intervention if needed. Continue current cardiac medications. Annual follow-up.

12-month active surveillance visit for Gleason 6 prostate cancer. PSA 6.1, stable. Repeat mpMRI: PI-RADS 3 lesion stable in size at 12mm, no new lesions. Confirmatory biopsy performed: Gleason 3+3=6, 1/4 targeted cores positive, 0/12 systematic cores positive. Stable low-grade disease. Continue active surveillance. Next PSA in 6 months, MRI/biopsy in 12-18 months. Tamsulosin helping LUTS, IPSS 8.

76-year-old male for annual wellness. PMH: CAD s/p LAD stent, HTN, HLD, prostate cancer on active surveillance, BPH. Multiple medications. BP 124/74. BMI 27.2. Labs: Cr 1.1, eGFR 68, HbA1c 5.5%, CBC normal, LDL 60. DEXA scan: T-score -1.8 lumbar spine (osteopenia). Started calcium 1200mg + vitamin D 2000 IU daily. Colonoscopy up to date. Flu vaccine administered. Depression screening negative.

Active surveillance update. PSA 6.4, minimally elevated from prior. mpMRI: stable PI-RADS 3 lesion, no progression. Given 2 stable biopsies and low-volume disease, extending biopsy interval to 2 years per updated AS protocols. Continue PSA q6 months. LUTS well managed on tamsulosin. Patient remains in good health overall.

77-year-old male presenting after mechanical fall at home, tripped on rug. Right hip pain, unable to bear weight. No head strike, no LOC. BP 140/82, HR 76. Right lower extremity externally rotated and shortened. X-ray: displaced right femoral neck fracture. Orthopedic surgery consulted. Pre-op labs and ECG obtained (ECG: NSR with old LVH, no acute changes). Troponin negative. Held ASA per ortho protocol. Pain managed with IV acetaminophen and low-dose morphine. Cardiology aware, cleared for surgery.

Right hip hemiarthroplasty performed for displaced femoral neck fracture. Cemented bipolar prosthesis via posterior approach. Operative time 68 minutes, EBL 250mL. Intra-op: stable hemodynamics. Post-op: weight bearing as tolerated with walker. DVT prophylaxis with enoxaparin 40mg SC daily (held ASA, will resume post-operatively). PT/OT evaluation ordered. Anticipated discharge to rehab facility in 3-5 days. Bone health optimization per PCP (known osteopenia).

6-week post-op follow-up right hip hemiarthroplasty. Patient completed 3 weeks inpatient rehab, now home with outpatient PT. Ambulating with single-point cane. Wound healed well, no signs of infection. X-ray: prosthesis well-positioned, no periprosthetic fracture. Hip precautions reviewed. Continue PT. Full recovery expected. Given osteopenia and fragility fracture, recommend discussion with PCP about bisphosphonate therapy. Resume ASA as prior.

Follow-up post hip fracture recovery. Patient ambulating with cane, improving. Discussed osteoporosis management: repeat DEXA shows T-score -2.2 lumbar spine, worsened and now meets osteoporosis threshold especially given fragility fracture. Starting alendronate 70mg weekly. Reviewed proper administration: take with full glass of water, remain upright 30 min, take on empty stomach. Ensure adequate calcium and vitamin D intake. Fall prevention strategies reviewed. BP 126/76. All other chronic conditions stable.

Annual cardiology follow-up. 6 years post LAD stent. Patient recovered well from hip fracture. No cardiac symptoms. BP 128/76. HR 60. ECG: NSR, LVH stable. LDL 58, well controlled. Echo: EF 55%, mild diastolic dysfunction grade I (new, age-appropriate). Continue all cardiac medications unchanged. Discussed importance of continued exercise within physical limitations. Next annual visit or sooner if symptoms.

40-year-old female presenting for new patient visit. PMH: generalized anxiety disorder managed with escitalopram 10mg, seasonal allergic rhinitis. Allergy to codeine (nausea/vomiting). Family history: father with colon cancer at age 62. BP 118/72, HR 76, BMI 24.8. General exam unremarkable. Labs ordered: CBC, CMP, lipid panel, TSH. Due for early colonoscopy at age 40 given first-degree relative with CRC before 65. Referral placed.

40-year-old female with family history of paternal colon cancer at 62 presenting for screening colonoscopy. Prep excellent. Findings: normal mucosa throughout, no polyps identified to cecum. Recommend repeat in 5 years given family history. Patient tolerated procedure well.

Follow-up. Labs from May reviewed: all normal including TSH 2.4, LDL 98. Patient presents today with complaints of intermittent bilateral hand and wrist pain x2 months, worse in mornings, stiffness lasting ~15 minutes. No swelling. Exam: no joint effusion, mild tenderness over bilateral wrist extensors. Suspect repetitive strain/early tendinopathy (patient works extensively at computer). Prescribed wrist splints for nighttime use and ergonomic workstation assessment. NSAIDs PRN. If not improving in 6 weeks, will investigate further.

Annual visit. Hand/wrist pain resolved with ergonomic modifications. BP 120/74, BMI 24.5. Anxiety well controlled on escitalopram 10mg, no panic attacks. PHQ-9 score 2, GAD-7 score 6. Labs: glucose 88, LDL 102, HbA1c 5.2%. All normal. Flu vaccine administered. Continue current medications.

42-year-old female referred by PCP for recurrent sinusitis, 4 episodes in past 12 months requiring antibiotics. Current symptoms: facial pressure, purulent nasal discharge, post-nasal drip x10 days. CT sinuses: mucosal thickening bilateral maxillary and anterior ethmoid sinuses, no polyps. Treating acute episode with amoxicillin-clavulanate 875mg BID x10 days (codeine allergy noted, not relevant). Initiated fluticasone nasal spray daily and nasal saline irrigation. If recurrence continues, may discuss functional endoscopic sinus surgery. Follow-up in 6 weeks.

Follow-up recurrent sinusitis. Acute episode resolved. Patient using fluticasone nasal spray and saline irrigation daily as prescribed. No further sinusitis episodes in past 6 weeks. Will continue preventive regimen through allergy season. Allergy testing recommended to identify triggers and consider immunotherapy if appropriate. Follow-up in 3 months or sooner if recurrence.

Annual exam. No sinusitis recurrence since starting nasal steroids and irrigation. Allergy testing revealed sensitivity to dust mites and grass pollen. Considering sublingual immunotherapy. BP 116/70, BMI 24.2. Anxiety stable. Labs normal. Patient asks about discontinuing escitalopram after 5+ years. Discussed risks of recurrence; agreed to very gradual taper starting in spring when seasonal anxiety is lower, with close monitoring.

Escitalopram taper visit. Reduced from 10mg to 5mg x4 weeks ago. Patient reports mild increase in baseline anxiety, occasional restlessness, but manageable. No panic attacks. GAD-7 score 9 (mild-moderate, up from 6). Sleep slightly disrupted. Continue 5mg for 4 more weeks before further taper. Discussed reinstatement at 10mg if symptoms worsen. Supportive measures: regular exercise, sleep hygiene, mindfulness. Follow-up in 4 weeks.

Taper follow-up. Anxiety symptoms worsened at 5mg: GAD-7 score 14, difficulty concentrating at work, muscle tension, poor sleep. Patient wishes to return to 10mg. Reinstated escitalopram 10mg daily. Discussed that long-term maintenance may be appropriate given her history. Referred for CBT to develop additional coping strategies alongside medication. Follow-up in 6 weeks.

Annual visit. Back on escitalopram 10mg x5 months, anxiety well controlled, GAD-7 score 5. Started CBT, finding it helpful. BP 118/72. BMI 24.0. Labs normal. Sinuses well controlled on fluticasone. No recurrent infections in past year. Colonoscopy surveillance due in 2024. Continue current plan.

44-year-old female presenting with irregular menstrual cycles over past 6 months: cycle length varying 21-38 days, occasional heavy flow, intermittent hot flashes. LMP 3 weeks ago. Exam: normal. FSH 18 mIU/mL, estradiol 42 pg/mL, consistent with perimenopause. TSH 2.2, normal. Discussed perimenopausal transition, expected symptom trajectory. Hot flashes mild, not requiring treatment currently. Continue contraception as ovulation can still occur. Escitalopram may help with vasomotor symptoms as secondary benefit. Follow-up in 6 months or if symptoms worsen.

Follow-up. Perimenopausal symptoms mildly increased: hot flashes 2-3x/day, night sweats disrupting sleep. Cycles irregular, last period 6 weeks ago. Mood stable on escitalopram. BP 120/76. BMI 24.1. Discussed HRT options: given her age, symptom burden, and no contraindications, trial of low-dose transdermal estradiol 0.025mg patch + oral micronized progesterone 100mg nightly is appropriate. Patient agrees. Labs: lipid panel stable, mammogram up to date and normal. Follow-up in 3 months.

HRT follow-up at 3 months. Significant improvement: hot flashes reduced to 2-3x/week, sleep improved, mood stable. No vaginal bleeding. BP 118/74. Tolerating estradiol patch and progesterone well. Continue current doses. Colonoscopy surveillance due this year; referral placed. Mammogram annual. Will reassess HRT in 12 months with plan to use lowest effective dose for shortest duration.

66-year-old male presenting for annual exam. PMH: type 2 diabetes x15 years on insulin (glargine 24 units nightly + lispro sliding scale), hypertension, diabetic neuropathy bilateral feet, stage 3a CKD (eGFR 52). Allergy: sulfonamides (Stevens-Johnson syndrome - documented severe). BP 142/86 on losartan 100mg + amlodipine 5mg. HbA1c 8.2%, above target. Weight 210 lbs, BMI 31.4. Foot exam: diminished monofilament sensation bilaterally, no ulcers. Adjusting glargine to 28 units nightly. Adding semaglutide 0.25mg SQ weekly for glycemic control and weight management. CKD monitoring: Cr 1.4, eGFR 52, urine protein/creatinine 380 mg/g (elevated). Nephrology referral.

66-year-old male with T2DM, HTN, and CKD stage 3a referred for proteinuric CKD management. eGFR 52, UPCR 380. Already on losartan 100mg (appropriate for proteinuria reduction). BP 138/84. Recommend uptitrating BP target to <130/80 per KDIGO. Added chlorthalidone 12.5mg daily (avoiding sulfonamide antibiotics per allergy, but thiazide-like diuretics generally safe; discussed with patient, will monitor closely for any reaction). Checking renal panel and UPCR in 6 weeks. Discussed dietary protein moderation, sodium restriction. Consider adding finerenone if proteinuria persists despite optimization.

Follow-up diabetes and CKD. HbA1c 7.4%, improved on semaglutide (now titrated to 1mg weekly) and glargine 28 units. Weight 202 lbs, down 8 lbs. Tolerating semaglutide with mild nausea initially that resolved. BP 128/78 on losartan + amlodipine + chlorthalidone, at target. No hypoglycemia. eGFR 54 (stable), UPCR 290 (improving). Nephrology recommends continuing current renal protective strategy. Continue current regimen. Diabetic eye exam due.

66-year-old male with T2DM x15 years for diabetic retinopathy screening. VA OD 20/30, OS 20/25. Dilated exam: moderate NPDR OU with multiple microaneurysms and scattered dot-blot hemorrhages. No macular edema on OCT. No neovascularization. Strict glycemic and BP control essential. Follow-up in 6 months given moderate NPDR. If progression to severe NPDR or macular edema, will initiate treatment.

67-year-old male referred for painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy bilateral feet, not adequately controlled with gabapentin 300mg TID (started by PCP 2 years ago). Reports burning, tingling, and lancinating pain worse at night, VAS 6/10. EMG/NCS: axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy, moderate severity. Increasing gabapentin to 600mg TID with monitoring for sedation given CKD (renally dosed). If inadequate, will add duloxetine or consider pregabalin. Foot care reinforced. Capsaicin cream 0.075% offered for topical relief.

Follow-up neuropathic pain. Gabapentin 600mg TID providing moderate relief, VAS 4/10. Some drowsiness initially that improved. Given residual symptoms, adding duloxetine 30mg daily, titrating to 60mg in 2 weeks. Duloxetine may also benefit mood (patient reports mild depressive symptoms since chronic pain onset). Monitor renal function with this combination. Follow-up in 8 weeks.

Annual exam. HbA1c 7.1%, best control in years. Weight 196 lbs, BMI 29.3 (from 31.4). Semaglutide 1mg weekly well tolerated. Glargine reduced to 22 units nightly given improved control (risk of hypoglycemia). Neuropathic pain better managed on gabapentin + duloxetine per neurology. BP 126/76. eGFR 50, mildly declined. UPCR 260. Potassium 4.8, monitoring given losartan + CKD. Chlorthalidone continues. Finerenone discussed with nephrology; patient to follow up. Foot exam: intact skin, diminished sensation unchanged.

6-month follow-up for moderate NPDR. Visual acuity stable. Dilated exam: progression to severe NPDR OD with multiple cotton wool spots and venous beading. OS remains moderate NPDR. OCT: early diabetic macular edema OD, central subfield thickness 340 microns. Initiating anti-VEGF therapy with intravitreal aflibercept OD. First injection today, well tolerated. Monthly injections planned x3 then reassess. OS monitoring closely. Emphasized urgent need for continued glycemic optimization.

Post 3 monthly aflibercept injections OD. DME improving: central subfield thickness now 290 microns, down from 340. Visual acuity OD stable at 20/30. Continuing injections extending to q8 weeks using treat-and-extend protocol. OS: moderate NPDR stable, no macular edema. Continue close monitoring.

Follow-up CKD. eGFR 48 (from 52 at initial visit, gradual decline). UPCR 240, improved with maximal losartan and semaglutide. K 4.9. BP 128/76. Starting finerenone 10mg daily given persistent albuminuria with T2DM and CKD per FIDELIO-DKD data. Monitor potassium closely at 1 and 4 weeks; hold if K >5.5. Dietary potassium counseling reinforced. Continue all other medications. Goal: slow CKD progression.

Annual exam. HbA1c 7.0%. Weight stable at 194 lbs. eGFR 47, K 5.1 on finerenone (within acceptable range). UPCR 180, significant improvement. BP 124/74. Neuropathic pain VAS 3/10, well managed. DME treatment ongoing per ophthalmology, responding well. No hypoglycemia on reduced glargine 20 units. Review of systems: patient reports occasional left calf cramping when walking, relieved by rest. Concerning for peripheral arterial disease given DM, HTN, former smoker history (20 pack-years, quit 2000). ABI ordered.

ABI results: right 1.04 (normal), left 0.72 (abnormal, consistent with PAD). Confirming mild intermittent claudication left lower extremity. Starting cilostazol 100mg BID (contraindication check: no heart failure). Supervised exercise therapy recommended. Smoking cessation already achieved. Vascular surgery referral if symptoms worsen or fail conservative management. Continue ASA 81mg (already on it).

Follow-up. Claudication mildly improved with cilostazol and walking program, now able to walk 2 blocks before symptoms. HbA1c 7.2%, slight rise. Weight stable. Adjusting glargine back to 22 units. eGFR 45, slow progression. K 5.0. UPCR 165, continued improvement on finerenone. Eyes: aflibercept extended to q12 weeks, DME resolved OD. Comprehensive management ongoing. Follow-up in 6 months.

Annual exam. Age 70. HbA1c 7.1%. eGFR 43 (CKD stage 3b). UPCR 150. BP 122/74. Weight 192. Neuropathy stable. Claudication stable. Eyes: aflibercept q12 weeks, no active DME. Comprehensive medication reconciliation: losartan 100mg, amlodipine 5mg, chlorthalidone 12.5mg, finerenone 10mg, glargine 22u, semaglutide 1mg, gabapentin 600mg TID, duloxetine 60mg, cilostazol 100mg BID, ASA 81mg, rosuvastatin 20mg, capsaicin cream. 12 medications total. Polypharmacy review completed; all indicated. Fall risk assessment performed: Timed Up and Go 14 seconds (borderline). Home safety evaluation recommended.

71-year-old male presenting with left foot non-healing ulcer x2 weeks, worsening erythema and purulent drainage x3 days. T 38.3°C, BP 134/82, HR 88. Exam: 2cm ulcer plantar left foot over 1st metatarsal head, surrounding cellulitis, no crepitus, probe-to-bone negative. WBC 15.2, Cr 1.6 (above baseline 1.4), glucose 268. X-ray: no osteomyelitis. Wound culture obtained. Started empiric IV piperacillin-tazobactam (avoiding sulfonamides per documented SJS allergy). Blood glucose managed with insulin drip. Podiatry and vascular surgery consulted. Admitted to medicine.
