Follow-up T2DM and CKD. 73-year-old male, T2DM x ~23 years (diagnosed 2003) on insulin glargine 22 units nightly + semaglutide 1mg weekly. Empagliflozin 10mg daily added March 2024 after the foot-infection admission. Losartan 100mg daily (long-standing, since before 2018), amlodipine 5mg, chlorthalidone 12.5mg. Finerenone stopped Aug 2025 for K 5.8 — no MRA since. Left plantar ulcer healed, no recurrence. BP 126/74. Labs Apr 1: Cr 1.85, eGFR 38, K 5.2, HbA1c 7.6%. Urine albumin/creatinine ratio 486 mg/g (UACR now replacing UPCR for monitoring). Assessment: diabetic kidney disease, CKD stage 3b A3, with hyperkalemia on ARB. Low-potassium dietary counseling; recheck K in 2 weeks, start patiromer 8.4g daily if K remains above 5.0. Continue losartan 100mg. Sulfonamide allergy (SJS). Eyes stable on aflibercept q12 weeks. RTC 3 months.

28-year-old female presenting for new patient intake. No significant PMH. Takes only OTC multivitamin. NKDA. Non-smoker, occasional alcohol. BP 108/66, HR 62, BMI 21.8. Exam unremarkable. Discussed age-appropriate screening. Labs: CBC, CMP, TSH all normal. Active lifestyle, runs 20 miles/week. No complaints.

29-year-old female runner presenting with 6-week history of right anterior knee pain, worse with running, stairs, and prolonged sitting. No trauma, no locking or giving way. Exam: positive patellar grind test, tenderness lateral patellar facet, no effusion, stable ligaments. Diagnosis: patellofemoral pain syndrome. Prescribed physical therapy focusing on VMO strengthening, hip stabilization, and ITB flexibility. Activity modification: reduce running mileage by 50% for 4 weeks. Ibuprofen PRN. Follow-up in 6 weeks.

Follow-up PFPS right knee. Completed 6 weeks of PT, symptoms improved significantly. Pain 2/10 from 6/10 at initial visit. Running resumed at lower mileage without recurrence. Continue home exercise program focusing on quad and hip strengthening. Gradual return to full mileage over 4 weeks. No further orthopaedic follow-up needed unless recurrence.

Annual visit. Knee resolved. Patient training for marathon. BP 106/64, HR 56 (athletic bradycardia). BMI 21.5. No complaints. Labs unremarkable. Discussed sports nutrition, especially iron status in female runners: ferritin 28 ng/mL (low-normal). Recommend iron-rich foods and monitoring. No supplementation at this level but recheck if symptomatic. Flu vaccine given.

30-year-old female presenting with 3-month history of intermittent abdominal pain, bloating, and alternating constipation/diarrhea. No weight loss, no blood in stool, no nocturnal symptoms. Diet log shows no clear trigger. BP 110/68. Abdomen: mild diffuse tenderness, no masses, no organomegaly. Labs: CBC normal, CRP <0.5, celiac panel (TTG-IgA) negative, stool calprotectin 18 (normal). Meets Rome IV criteria for IBS, mixed type. Discussed dietary modifications: low FODMAP trial x6 weeks. Psyllium fiber supplement daily. Consider peppermint oil capsules for cramping. Follow-up in 6 weeks.

IBS follow-up. Low FODMAP diet x6 weeks with moderate improvement. Identified high-fructose fruits and lactose as likely triggers. Bloating reduced by ~50%, bowel habits more regular. Transitioning to FODMAP reintroduction phase with guidance from dietitian. Continue psyllium. Peppermint oil helpful for cramping. If symptoms plateau, will consider referral to GI for further evaluation.

Annual exam. IBS well managed with dietary modifications, avoidance of identified triggers. Occasional symptoms during stress. BP 108/66. BMI 21.3. Running consistently, completed half-marathon last month. Ferritin 24 ng/mL, borderline low in context of athletic activity. Starting ferrous gluconate 325mg every other day (better absorbed, fewer GI side effects - important given IBS). Recheck ferritin in 3 months. Vitamin D 28 ng/mL (insufficient), supplement with D3 2000 IU daily.

Ferritin recheck: 38 ng/mL, improved. Vitamin D 42 ng/mL, replete. Continue supplementation. Patient reports new symptom: intermittent palpitations x2 months, occurring at rest and during running, lasting seconds. No syncope, no chest pain. Exam: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur. ECG: NSR, rate 58, normal intervals. Given symptoms, ordering Holter monitor 48-hour study and checking TSH, electrolytes. Follow-up for results.

Results review. Holter monitor: sinus rhythm throughout, HR 48-142, frequent premature atrial contractions (PACs), 3.2% burden. No sustained arrhythmias. Correlates with patient's symptom diary (palpitations during PAC clusters). TSH 2.0, electrolytes normal. Mg 1.8 (low-normal). Frequent PACs, benign in structurally normal heart. Reassurance provided. Recommend reducing caffeine, supplementing magnesium glycinate 400mg daily. If symptomatic burden worsens, consider cardiology referral for possible echo. No treatment needed at this time.

Annual visit. PACs improved with caffeine reduction and magnesium. Palpitations now rare. IBS managed well. Running 25 miles/week. BP 108/64, HR 54, BMI 21.0. Labs stable, ferritin 42, vitamin D 40. All well. Continue supplements. Age-appropriate screening up to date. No concerns.

32-year-old female presenting for annual well-woman exam. G0P0. On combined OCP x8 years. Pap smear + HPV co-testing performed. Breast exam normal. Patient not planning pregnancy currently. Discussed long-term contraceptive options given age; patient satisfied with current OCP regimen. No menstrual irregularities. Family history updated: mother recently diagnosed with breast cancer at age 60. Discussed implications: now qualifies for earlier breast cancer screening. Referral for genetic counseling and risk assessment.

Follow-up regarding maternal breast cancer diagnosis. Genetic counseling completed: patient tested negative for BRCA1/2 and other high-penetrance mutations. Lifetime breast cancer risk calculated at approximately 20% by Tyrer-Cuzick model (borderline for enhanced screening). Discussed with patient: annual mammography starting at age 30 (10 years before mother's diagnosis) plus consideration of breast MRI. First mammogram and breast MRI ordered. Continue routine care otherwise.

Results review. Mammogram: BI-RADS 1, negative. Breast MRI: BI-RADS 1, no suspicious enhancement. Reassuring. Plan: annual mammogram + MRI given elevated lifetime risk. Patient relieved. IBS stable, palpitations resolved, running well. Iron and vitamin D maintained. Annual visit due in fall.

33-year-old female runner presenting with 4-week history of left shin pain, worse during and after running. Exam: focal tenderness over distal left tibia medially. Hop test positive for pain. XR: no fracture line visible. Given high clinical suspicion, ordered MRI left tibia: findings show stress reaction with periosteal edema and bone marrow edema consistent with tibial stress fracture. Non-weight-bearing boot x6 weeks. No running for 8 weeks minimum. Calcium and vitamin D supplementation confirmed. Refer to sports dietitian to ensure adequate caloric intake relative to training volume. RED-S screening questionnaire administered - borderline concerning.

56-year-old male presenting for executive health screening. PMH: gout (intermittent, allopurinol PRN), mild GERD. Medications: omeprazole 20mg daily. NKDA. 10 pack-year smoking history, quit 2008. Moderate alcohol (2-3 drinks/week). BP 138/88, HR 76, BMI 29.0. Labs: uric acid 7.8, glucose 108, HbA1c 5.8%, LDL 152, HDL 42, TG 198. eGFR 82. Borderline metabolic parameters. Starting allopurinol 100mg daily for gout prophylaxis. Recommend lifestyle modifications for metabolic risk. Statin discussion initiated; patient defers pending lifestyle trial. Follow-up in 6 months.

6-month follow-up. Lifestyle changes attempted but limited. BP 140/90. LDL 148, TG 182, HbA1c 5.9%. Weight unchanged. Uric acid 6.4 on allopurinol 100mg, no gout flares. Given persistent borderline hypertension and dyslipidemia with family history (father MI at age 63), ASCVD risk 8.2%, starting atorvastatin 20mg and hydrochlorothiazide 25mg daily. Strongly encouraged dietary changes and exercise program.

Follow-up. BP 128/82 on HCTZ 25mg, improved. LDL 98 on atorvastatin 20mg, at goal. TG 142. HbA1c 5.7%. Uric acid 5.8. Patient joined gym, exercising 2-3x/week. Weight down 5 lbs, BMI 28.3. All parameters improving. Continue current medications. Annual screening in 6 months.

Annual exam. Stable on current regimen. BP 126/80. LDL 94. HbA1c 5.6%. Weight stable. Prostate screening discussed: PSA 2.1, DRE normal. Colonoscopy screening: up to date (normal in 2017). Flu vaccine given. No acute concerns. Continue medications.

58-year-old male referred for persistent GERD symptoms despite omeprazole 20mg daily x3 years. Reports breakthrough heartburn 3-4x/week, occasional regurgitation. No dysphagia, no weight loss. EGD: LA Grade A esophagitis, small Schatzki ring, no Barrett's. H. pylori negative. Increasing omeprazole to 40mg daily. Lifestyle modifications reinforced: weight loss, avoid late meals, elevate HOB. If refractory, consider pH impedance study. Follow-up in 8 weeks.

GERD follow-up. Symptoms improved on omeprazole 40mg, breakthrough heartburn now 1x/week. Patient has elevated HOB and reduced evening meals. Plan: continue omeprazole 40mg, attempt step-down to 20mg in 3 months. Long-term PPI use monitored: DEXA baseline recommended given duration of use, and periodic magnesium levels. Follow-up PRN.

Annual exam. Age 59. All chronic conditions stable. BP 124/78. LDL 90. HbA1c 5.5%. Weight: BMI 27.8, continued gradual loss. GERD managed on omeprazole 40mg, stepping down attempted but symptoms recurred at 20mg, back to 40mg. Uric acid 5.6, no gout flares x2 years. DEXA ordered per GI recommendation given long-term PPI use: T-score -0.8 (normal). Magnesium 1.9 (normal). Continue all medications. PSA 2.3, stable.

59-year-old male presenting with 2-month history of progressive right shoulder pain and stiffness. Pain with reaching overhead and behind back. No trauma. Exam: significantly restricted ROM right shoulder - forward flexion 100°, external rotation 20°, internal rotation to buttock. Painful arc absent (too stiff). Diagnosis: adhesive capsulitis (frozen shoulder). X-ray: no arthritis, no calcification. Corticosteroid injection glenohumeral joint performed under ultrasound guidance. Prescribed intensive physical therapy 3x/week. Patient counseled this is a self-limiting condition typically resolving over 12-18 months.

Frozen shoulder follow-up at 3 months. ROM improving: forward flexion 130°, external rotation 35°. Pain 4/10, down from 7/10. Responding to PT. Second injection not needed at this time. Continue PT, home stretching program. Reassess in 3 months. If plateau, consider hydrodilatation or manipulation under anesthesia, though prognosis good.

60th birthday screening visit. Shoulder improving. BP 122/76. BMI 27.5. LDL 88. HbA1c 5.6%. Glucose 102. TG 134. All improved from baseline 4 years ago. Colonoscopy surveillance due (5 years since last, age appropriate). PSA 2.4, stable. LDCT lung cancer screening discussed: eligible given 10 pack-year history but quit >15 years ago, and only 10 pack-years so below USPSTF threshold. Not indicated. Continue preventive care.

60-year-old male presenting for surveillance colonoscopy. Prep good. Findings: 8mm sessile polyp ascending colon, removed by cold snare. 5mm pedunculated polyp sigmoid, removed by snare polypectomy. No other lesions. Pathology: ascending = tubulovillous adenoma with low-grade dysplasia; sigmoid = tubular adenoma. Given tubulovillous histology, recommend surveillance in 3 years per guidelines. Patient informed.

60-year-old male referred by PCP for borderline glucose and HbA1c trending up over 5 years despite lifestyle efforts. Latest HbA1c 6.0%, fasting glucose 112. BMI 27.5. Family history: father T2DM. Oral glucose tolerance test performed: fasting 110, 2-hour 162 mg/dL (impaired glucose tolerance). Fasting insulin 18 (elevated, suggesting insulin resistance). Diagnosis: prediabetes with insulin resistance. Metformin 500mg daily initiated given IGT + family history + multiple metabolic risk factors. Continue lifestyle modifications. Recheck HbA1c in 3 months.

3-month follow-up on metformin 500mg. Tolerating well, mild GI adjustment first 2 weeks. HbA1c 5.7%, improved. Fasting glucose 100. Weight down 3 lbs. No hypoglycemia. Continue metformin 500mg daily. Recheck in 6 months. Goal: prevent progression to overt diabetes. Diet and exercise counseling reinforced.

Annual exam. Comprehensive review. Age 61. Prediabetes managed with metformin, HbA1c 5.7%. BP 120/76 on HCTZ. LDL 86 on atorvastatin. Uric acid 5.4, gout quiescent on allopurinol. GERD managed on omeprazole 40mg. BMI 27.0, lowest in years. Shoulder fully recovered. PSA 2.5, stable. Colonoscopy surveillance in 2025. Reviewed all medications: omeprazole 40mg, HCTZ 25mg, atorvastatin 20mg, allopurinol 100mg, metformin 500mg. All indicated. Patient in good overall health. Continue current management.

62-year-old male referred for evaluation after reporting exertional palpitations during exercise. PMH as above. ECG: NSR with occasional PVCs. Exercise stress test: achieved 10.2 METS, peak HR 148 (94% predicted). Rare PVCs at rest, suppressed with exercise (benign pattern). No ischemic ECG changes. No chest pain. Echo: normal LV size and function, EF 60%, no valvular disease. Reassuring evaluation. PVCs likely benign, possibly related to caffeine or stress. No cardiac medication needed. Cleared for unrestricted exercise. Follow-up with PCP.

Follow-up. Palpitations resolved after reducing coffee from 4 cups to 1 daily. Cardiology workup reassuring. HbA1c 5.6% on metformin, excellent. BP 118/74. LDL 84. BMI 26.8. All chronic conditions well controlled. Flu and updated COVID vaccines administered. Patient asks about discontinuing HCTZ given improved BP and weight loss. Agreed to trial off HCTZ with home BP monitoring x4 weeks; if BP remains <130/80, will discontinue permanently. Follow-up in 6 weeks.

62 y/o female presenting for annual wellness exam. PMHx significant for HTN, hyperlipidaemia, and osteoarthritis. BP 142/88, HR 72, BMI 27.3. Currently on lisinopril 10mg daily and atorvastatin 20mg daily. Lipid panel ordered. Encouraged dietary modifications and regular exercise. RTC 6 months.

Patient referred for diabetic screening eye exam. Fundoscopic exam reveals early non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy R eye. L eye within normal limits. Visual acuity 20/25 bilaterally. Recommend follow-up in 6 months and optimisation of glycaemic control. Discussed findings with patient.

Follow-up visit. BP improved at 134/82 on current regimen. HbA1c 7.2% — previously undiagnosed T2DM. Fasting glucose 148 mg/dL. Started metformin 500mg BID. Discussed diabetic diet, SMBG, and referral to diabetes educator. Lipids improved: LDL 112. Continue atorvastatin. Ophthalmology notes early NPDR R eye.

Referral from PCP for newly diagnosed T2DM. HbA1c 7.2% on metformin 500mg BID x3 months. Tolerating medication well, no GI side effects. Reviewed SMBG log — fasting BG averaging 135. Increased metformin to 1000mg BID. Reinforced carb counting, set HbA1c target <7%. Recheck in 3 months.

Follow-up T2DM management. HbA1c now 6.8%, fasting BG 118. Patient adhering well to metformin 1000mg BID. Weight down 3 lbs. Renal function stable, eGFR 72. Continue current regimen. Annual microalbumin ordered. Next visit 6 months.

63 y/o female with worsening bilateral knee pain, R > L, over past 2 years. X-ray shows moderate tricompartmental OA R knee, mild-moderate L knee. Crepitus on exam bilaterally. ROM limited R knee flexion to 110 degrees. Trial of meloxicam 15mg daily, PT referral. Advised weight loss. Avoid NSAIDs if renal function declines given DM. Follow-up 8 weeks.

Follow-up bilateral knee OA. Patient reports 40% improvement with meloxicam and PT. Completing exercises at home. R knee still symptomatic with prolonged walking. Discussed cortisone injection vs continued conservative management. Patient opts for R knee intra-articular corticosteroid injection today — 40mg triamcinolone with 3mL lidocaine 1%. Tolerated well. Continue PT.

Annual follow-up. BP 130/78. HbA1c 6.7%, well controlled on metformin 1000mg BID. eGFR 68, stable. Microalbumin/Cr ratio 42 — mildly elevated. Started low-dose lisinopril increased to 20mg for renal protection. Atorvastatin continued. Knee OA managed by orthopaedics. Colonoscopy due — referred to GI. Flu vaccine administered.

Screening colonoscopy. Prep adequate. Scope advanced to caecum. Two sessile polyps found in sigmoid colon, 4mm and 6mm, removed via cold snare polypectomy. No complications. Path pending. Recommend repeat colonoscopy in 3 years given polyp findings. Patient tolerated procedure well, discharged in stable condition.

Path results from colonoscopy: tubular adenomas x2, low-grade dysplasia, margins clear. Discussed findings with patient — benign but pre-malignant. Surveillance colonoscopy recommended in 3 years. No GI symptoms currently. Continue high-fibre diet.

Routine follow-up. Patient reports intermittent palpitations over past month, no syncope or chest pain. BP 128/76, HR 78 irregular. ECG in office shows atrial fibrillation with controlled ventricular rate. Started on apixaban 5mg BID given CHA2DS2-VASc score of 4. Referred to cardiology urgently. Metformin, lisinopril 20mg, atorvastatin continued.

New diagnosis paroxysmal AF. Echo: EF 55%, mild LVH, no valvular disease. TSH normal. Started metoprolol succinate 25mg daily for rate control in addition to apixaban. Holter monitor ordered. Discussed rhythm vs rate control strategy. Patient prefers conservative approach. Avoid flecainide given structural changes. Follow-up post-Holter.

Holter results: paroxysmal AF with longest run 4 hours, average ventricular rate 82 bpm, no pauses >2.5s. Patient reports reduced palpitations on metoprolol. Increased metoprolol to 50mg daily. Continue apixaban. Recheck in 3 months. Discussed signs requiring ED visit.

65 y/o female presenting with acute onset SOB and rapid palpitations x2 hours. Hx of paroxysmal AF. HR 134 irregular, BP 108/70, SpO2 94% RA. ECG confirms AF with RVR. Troponin negative. CXR mild pulmonary congestion. IV diltiazem 20mg bolus administered with improvement to HR 96. Admitted to telemetry. Cardiology consulted.

Inpatient consult — AF with RVR, now rate-controlled on diltiazem drip transitioned to PO. Metoprolol discontinued, switched to diltiazem ER 180mg daily. Apixaban continued. BNP 380, mild volume overload — furosemide 20mg PO daily added. Echo unchanged from prior. Recommend cardioversion if AF persists. Discharge planned tomorrow.

Post-discharge follow-up. Patient in sinus rhythm today, HR 68. Tolerating diltiazem ER 180mg well. No recurrent AF symptoms. Discontinued furosemide — no peripheral oedema, weight stable. Continue apixaban 5mg BID. Repeat echo in 6 months. PCP managing DM and HTN.

Annual comprehensive visit. BP 126/74. HbA1c 6.9%, eGFR 65. Microalbumin stable at 38. AF in remission per cardiology. Meds reconciled: metformin 1000mg BID, lisinopril 20mg, atorvastatin 20mg, diltiazem ER 180mg, apixaban 5mg BID. DEXA scan ordered — postmenopausal female with risk factors. Shingrix vaccine #1 given.

30 y/o male new patient visit. No significant PMHx. Allergies: penicillin (rash). BP 118/74, HR 66, BMI 24.1. FHx notable for father with MI at age 52, mother with T2DM. Baseline labs ordered. Patient exercises regularly, non-smoker, social EtOH. Counselled on cardiovascular risk given FHx. RTC PRN.

Patient presents with pruritic erythematous plaques on bilateral elbows and knees x6 months. Well-demarcated, silvery scale. Clinical diagnosis: plaque psoriasis, mild-moderate. Started triamcinolone 0.1% cream BID to affected areas. Discussed chronic nature of disease, triggers. Vitamin D analogue calcipotriene added. Follow-up 6 weeks.

Follow-up psoriasis. Good response to topical steroids and calcipotriene. Plaques thinning, less erythematous. PASI score improved from 8 to 4. Continue current regimen, taper triamcinolone to daily. Moisturise liberally. Discussed phototherapy if flare. RTC 3 months.

31 y/o male presenting with acute R lower quadrant abdominal pain x12 hours, nausea, low-grade fever 38.1C. Tenderness at McBurney's point, positive Rovsing's sign. WBC 14.2, CRP 68. CT abdomen: acute uncomplicated appendicitis. General surgery consulted for appendectomy. NPO, IV fluids and ceftriaxone/metronidazole started. Allergy to penicillin noted — no cross-reactivity concern.

Consult for acute appendicitis. Examined patient — classic presentation. CT confirms non-perforated appendicitis. Proceeded with laparoscopic appendectomy under GA. Procedure uncomplicated, operative time 45 minutes. EBL minimal. Appendix sent to path. Post-op plan: clear liquids tonight, advance diet as tolerated, discharge anticipated POD1.

POD2 follow-up. Patient tolerating regular diet, ambulating independently. Afebrile, wound sites clean and dry. Pain controlled with paracetamol. Path: acute appendicitis, no perforation, no neoplasm. Discharged home with instructions. Lifting restrictions x2 weeks. Follow-up clinic 2 weeks.

Routine visit. Fully recovered from appendectomy. Psoriasis well-controlled on topicals. BP 120/76. Lipid panel: TC 218, LDL 142, HDL 48, TG 140. Given FHx of premature CAD, discussed lifestyle modifications for LDL reduction. Not meeting statin threshold by guidelines but will reassess. Advised Mediterranean diet.

Self-referred for symptoms of anxiety and low mood x4 months following relationship breakdown. PHQ-9 score 14 (moderate depression), GAD-7 score 12 (moderate anxiety). Sleep disrupted, appetite poor, difficulty concentrating at work. No SI/HI. Started sertraline 50mg daily. Discussed CBT referral. Safety plan reviewed. Follow-up 2 weeks.

Two-week check on sertraline. Mild nausea first week, now resolved. Sleep slightly improved. PHQ-9 score 12. No adverse effects. Dose adequate for now. CBT intake appointment scheduled. Continue sertraline 50mg. Follow-up 4 weeks.

8-week follow-up. PHQ-9 improved to 8 (mild), GAD-7 down to 7. Engaging well with CBT. Sleep normalised, appetite improved. Concentration better at work. Continue sertraline 50mg. Plan to reassess in 3 months with view to taper if sustained improvement.

PHQ-9 score 4, GAD-7 score 3 — both in minimal range. Patient feels back to baseline. Completed 12 sessions of CBT. Discussed tapering sertraline. Will reduce to 25mg daily x4 weeks then discontinue. Patient aware of relapse signs. Door open for re-referral.

Psoriasis flare — new plaques on trunk and scalp following period of stress. PASI score 10. Topicals insufficient for current extent. Discussed systemic options. Started apremilast 30mg BID after titration. Baseline LFTs and CBC normal. Continue calcipotriene for scalp. Follow-up 12 weeks.

Follow-up on apremilast. Significant improvement — trunk plaques nearly resolved, scalp improved. PASI score 3. Tolerating medication well, mild initial diarrhoea resolved. Continue apremilast. Monitoring labs stable. Reassess in 6 months with consideration of biologic if needed.

Annual visit. BP 122/78. BMI 24.8. Psoriasis managed on apremilast. Depression resolved, off sertraline. Repeat lipids: LDL 138 despite dietary changes. Given 10-year ASCVD risk and strong FHx, initiated rosuvastatin 10mg daily. Penicillin allergy confirmed in chart. Hepatitis B immunity confirmed. Up to date on preventive care.

73 y/o female with PMHx of COPD (GOLD stage II), HTN, and osteoporosis presenting for routine follow-up. BP 138/84, HR 78, SpO2 94% RA. Currently on tiotropium 18mcg inhaler daily, amlodipine 5mg, alendronate 70mg weekly, calcium/vitamin D. Spirometry: FEV1 62% predicted, FEV1/FVC 0.64. Stable from prior. Continue current regimen. Flu and pneumococcal vaccines due.

Referral for COPD optimisation. Patient reports increased dyspnoea on exertion over past 3 months, using rescue albuterol 3-4x/week. No exacerbations in past year. SpO2 93% RA. PFTs confirm moderate obstruction. Added LABA — formoterol/budesonide combination inhaler. Reviewed inhaler technique. Pulmonary rehabilitation recommended. Smoking cessation confirmed — quit 8 years ago.

Follow-up COPD. Patient reports improved exercise tolerance since starting combination inhaler and pulm rehab. Rescue inhaler use down to 1x/week. SpO2 95% RA at rest. FEV1 stable. Continue current regimen. Annual CT chest for lung cancer screening discussed — meets criteria. Ordered LDCT.

LDCT chest results: no lung nodules, mild emphysematous changes upper lobes bilaterally consistent with known COPD. No masses or lymphadenopathy. Continue annual screening. Results discussed with patient.

74 y/o female with COPD presenting with 3-day hx of worsening dyspnoea, productive cough with yellow-green sputum, fevers to 38.4C. SpO2 88% RA, RR 24, HR 102. CXR: R lower lobe infiltrate. WBC 15.8, CRP 124. Dx: community-acquired pneumonia with acute COPD exacerbation. Started levofloxacin 750mg IV, nebulised salbutamol/ipratropium, prednisone 40mg PO. O2 via NC at 2L/min. Admitted to medicine.

Inpatient day 4. Clinically improving — afebrile x48h, SpO2 93% RA, cough improving. WBC trending down to 10.2. Transitioned to PO levofloxacin to complete 7-day course. Prednisone taper over 10 days. Resumed home inhalers. Discharge tomorrow with close pulmonology follow-up. Discussed action plan for future exacerbations.

Post-exacerbation follow-up. Patient recovered well. SpO2 94% RA. PFTs show mild decline — FEV1 now 55% predicted. Given exacerbation history, added roflumilast 500mcg daily to reduce future exacerbation risk. Discussed importance of prompt treatment of future infections. Annual flu vaccine given.

Referral for evaluation of joint pain. Patient reports progressive bilateral hand pain and stiffness, worse in mornings x3 months. Exam: MCP and PIP joint swelling bilaterally, reduced grip strength. RF positive, anti-CCP 86 (high). ESR 42, CRP 28. X-ray hands: periarticular osteopaenia, early erosions R 2nd MCP. Diagnosis: seropositive rheumatoid arthritis. Started methotrexate 15mg weekly with folic acid. Baseline LFTs, CBC normal. Hepatitis B/C screen negative.

Follow-up RA — 12 weeks on methotrexate 15mg weekly. Morning stiffness reduced from 90 to 30 minutes. DAS28 improved from 5.1 to 3.8. LFTs normal, CBC stable. Still some residual swelling L 3rd MCP. Increased methotrexate to 20mg weekly. Added short course prednisone 5mg taper. Recheck 8 weeks.

RA follow-up. DAS28 now 2.9 — low disease activity. Tolerating methotrexate 20mg weekly. No hepatotoxicity on monitoring. Hand function much improved. DEXA scan results reviewed: T-score lumbar spine -2.8, femoral neck -2.4. Osteoporosis worsening concern — discussed with PCP re: bisphosphonate continuation and RA-related bone loss.

Comprehensive annual visit. Multiple active problems: COPD (stable on triple inhaler + roflumilast), RA (controlled on MTX), osteoporosis (alendronate continued), HTN. BP today 144/86 — amlodipine increased to 10mg. DEXA shows progressive bone loss despite alendronate — rheumatology and I agree to switch to denosumab 60mg SC q6months. First dose given today. HbA1c 5.8% — prediabetic range. Lifestyle counselling provided.

Referral for declining renal function. Cr 1.4 (baseline 0.9 two years ago), eGFR 38. Urinalysis: trace protein, no haematuria. Renal US: bilateral kidneys normal size, no hydronephrosis. Likely CKD stage 3b — multifactorial (age, HTN, NSAID use for RA, alendronate). Advised strict avoidance of NSAIDs. Reviewed meds — no nephrotoxins to discontinue. ACE/ARB not on board due to amlodipine preference; consider adding low-dose losartan for renal protection. Discussed with PCP.

Follow-up CKD and med reconciliation. Added losartan 25mg per nephrology recommendation, reduced amlodipine to 5mg. BP 132/78 on new regimen. Cr stable at 1.3, eGFR 40. Methotrexate dose reviewed with rheumatology — continue with close monitoring given CKD. Denosumab second dose administered. COPD stable.

Annual COPD review. FEV1 52% predicted — gradual decline. No exacerbations since 2020 hospitalisation. SpO2 92% RA at rest, desats to 87% on 6MWT. Qualifies for supplemental O2 with exertion. Prescribed portable O2 at 2L/min PRN activity. Continued all inhalers. LDCT chest: stable emphysema, no nodules.

RA stable on methotrexate 20mg weekly. DAS28 2.6 — remission. However, patient reports new methotrexate-related nausea despite folic acid. LFTs mildly elevated: ALT 52. Reduced MTX to 15mg weekly, added ondansetron PRN. If inadequate control, will consider switch to leflunomide or biologic. Recheck LFTs 4 weeks.

78 y/o comprehensive review. CKD stable — eGFR 39. BP 128/76 on losartan/amlodipine. HbA1c 6.0%. RA well-controlled on reduced MTX. COPD managed with O2 PRN, no recent exacerbations. Denosumab on schedule. Falls risk assessment performed — Timed Up and Go 14 seconds, moderate risk. PT referral for balance training. Advance care planning discussed, patient wishes documented.

78 y/o female brought in by EMS after mechanical fall at home. Tripped on rug, landed on L hip. Unable to bear weight. L leg shortened and externally rotated. X-ray: displaced intracapsular fracture L neck of femur. Pre-op workup initiated — ECG sinus rhythm, Hb 11.2, Cr 1.5, INR 1.0. Orthopaedics consulted. NPO for surgery.

L hip hemiarthroplasty performed under spinal anaesthesia. Displaced subcapital NOF fracture. Cemented Thompson prosthesis. Procedure uncomplicated, EBL 250mL. Post-op: LMWH DVT prophylaxis, weight bearing as tolerated. Physiotherapy from POD1. Denosumab on schedule — osteoporosis management critical. Target discharge POD 4-5 to rehab facility.

Post-op review 10 weeks. Patient progressing well in rehab, now mobilising with single stick. L hip ROM satisfactory, wound healed. X-ray: prosthesis well-positioned, no loosening. Continue PT. Denosumab injection given. Discussed falls prevention strategies. Gradual return to independent living anticipated.

COPD review after a recent exacerbation. 80 y/o female with COPD (GOLD stage II), seropositive RA on methotrexate 15mg weekly, CKD stage 3b, osteoporosis on denosumab, s/p L hip hemiarthroplasty January 2024. Exacerbations in the past 12 months, both outpatient, no hospitalization: November 24, 2025 (prednisolone 30mg x5 days + doxycycline) and June 10, 2026 (prednisolone 30mg x5 days + doxycycline 100mg x7 days, started by her GP) — now improving, cough settling, not yet fully back to baseline. Last hospitalization for COPD June 2020. Inhaled therapy: triple since August 2019 — tiotropium 18mcg daily (LAMA) + budesonide/formoterol (ICS/LABA); roflumilast 500mcg daily since July 2020. Post-bronchodilator spirometry April 8, 2026: FEV1 50% predicted, FEV1/FVC 0.57. Portable O2 2L/min PRN activity only (under 2 h/day), no continuous O2, no NIV; SpO2 92% RA today. Former smoker, 30 pack-years, quit 2011. No asthma, bronchiectasis, ILD or lung cancer (LDCT 2022: stable emphysema, no nodules). Bloods April 8, 2026: eosinophils 410 cells/μL (0.41 x10^9/L), Cr 1.35, eGFR 38. Plan: complete recovery, continue triple therapy and roflumilast, pulmonary rehab once recovered, review in 3 months.

42 y/o male presenting for new patient evaluation. PMHx: GERD, seasonal allergies. Meds: omeprazole 20mg daily, cetirizine PRN. Allergies: NKDA. BP 128/82, HR 70, BMI 31.2. FHx: mother with breast cancer at 58, father alive with HTN. Smoker 10 pack-years, motivated to quit. Discussed smoking cessation — started nicotine patch 21mg. Labs ordered including lipid panel and fasting glucose.

Follow-up. Labs: TC 234, LDL 158, HDL 42, TG 170. Fasting glucose 108. HbA1c 5.9% — prediabetic. BMI still 31.2. Patient has reduced smoking to 3 cigs/day on nicotine patch. Counselled on metabolic syndrome risks. Not yet meeting statin criteria by pooled cohort equation but borderline. Lifestyle modifications emphasised — weight loss target 10%. Repeat labs 6 months.

Referral for GERD not adequately controlled on omeprazole 20mg daily. Patient reports persistent heartburn and regurgitation despite PPI. EGD performed: LA Grade B erosive oesophagitis, small hiatal hernia. No Barrett's. CLO test negative for H. pylori. Increased omeprazole to 40mg daily, added famotidine 20mg at bedtime. Dietary counselling: avoid late meals, elevate HOB. Repeat EGD in 8 weeks to confirm healing.

Repeat EGD: oesophagitis healed, LA Grade A residual. Hiatal hernia unchanged. No dysplasia on biopsy. Maintain omeprazole 40mg daily. Can trial step-down to 20mg in 6 months if asymptomatic. Long-term PPI risks discussed — bone density, magnesium, B12. Monitoring plan in place.

Follow-up. Successfully quit smoking 3 months ago. Weight down 4 lbs. BP 124/80. Repeat labs: LDL 148, HbA1c 5.8%. GERD controlled on omeprazole 40mg. Started structured exercise programme — gym 3x/week. Continue weight loss efforts. Congratulated on smoking cessation. LDCT lung cancer screening not yet indicated — under 20 pack-year threshold. RTC 6 months.

43 y/o male presenting with acute L shoulder pain after gym injury 1 week ago — felt pop during overhead press. Limited ROM — cannot abduct past 80 degrees. Positive empty can test, painful arc. MRI: partial thickness supraspinatus tear, mild subacromial bursitis. Conservative management: sling PRN, PT referral, naproxen 500mg BID x2 weeks. Avoid overhead activity. Follow-up 6 weeks.

L shoulder follow-up. Improved ROM — abduction now to 130 degrees. Pain reduced with PT. Progressing through rotator cuff strengthening protocol. Continue PT 2x/week. Avoid heavy lifting x6 more weeks. Naproxen discontinued. Patient anxious to return to gym — cleared for lower body and light cardio only.

Annual exam. BMI 29.8 — down from 31.2, good progress. BP 122/76. Non-smoker x1 year. L shoulder fully recovered. LDL 140, HbA1c 5.7% — improved. GERD: stepped down omeprazole to 20mg, tolerating well. Overall trending in right direction. Continue lifestyle modifications. Colonoscopy screening at 45 per updated guidelines — scheduled.

Screening colonoscopy — age 44, average risk. Prep excellent. Scope to caecum. One 3mm hyperplastic polyp in rectum, removed. No adenomas. No other findings. Path: hyperplastic polyp — benign, no follow-up needed. Routine screening in 10 years. GERD well controlled on omeprazole 20mg.

Patient referred for persistent nasal congestion and facial pressure x6 months, not responding to cetirizine or nasal saline. Anterior rhinoscopy: oedematous inferior turbinates bilaterally, mucopurulent discharge L middle meatus. CT sinuses: mucosal thickening L maxillary and ethmoid sinuses consistent with chronic rhinosinusitis. Started fluticasone nasal spray 2 puffs each nostril BID and saline irrigations. Augmentin 875mg BID x14 days. Follow-up 4 weeks.

Follow-up chronic sinusitis. Symptoms improved 60% on antibiotics and nasal steroids. Residual L-sided congestion. Endoscopy: L middle meatus still oedematous but improved drainage. Continue fluticasone. If recurrence, will consider FESS. Allergy testing recommended — may have underlying allergic component driving chronic inflammation.

Annual visit. BP 120/74, BMI 28.6. Continued weight loss, now down 18 lbs total. Non-smoker. LDL 128, HbA1c 5.6% — out of prediabetic range. Excellent lifestyle changes. GERD well managed. Chronic sinusitis being managed by ENT. Meds: omeprazole 20mg daily, fluticasone nasal spray. Preventive care up to date. Well done.

45 y/o male referred for recurrent episodes of gross haematuria x2 months. No dysuria, no flank pain. Non-smoker x3 years. Urinalysis: RBC >50/hpf, no WBC, no casts. Cytology: atypical cells, cannot exclude malignancy. CT urogram: 2cm papillary lesion L bladder wall, no upper tract disease. Cystoscopy scheduled. PSA 0.8 — normal.

Cystoscopy and TURBT performed under spinal anaesthesia. 2.2cm papillary tumour L lateral bladder wall resected completely. Base cauterised. No perforation. Muscle present in specimen. Path pending. Post-op: continuous bladder irrigation overnight, Foley removal POD1. Mitomycin C single intravesical instillation given post-operatively per protocol.

Pathology: non-muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma, low grade, pTa. Muscularis propria present in specimen — no invasion. Good prognostic category. Plan: surveillance cystoscopy q3 months for 2 years, then q6 months. No BCG required for low-grade Ta disease. CT urogram annually. Smoking history counselled as risk factor — patient quit 3 years ago. Discussed prognosis — excellent for this stage.

First surveillance cystoscopy 3 months post-TURBT. No recurrence. Bladder mucosa healthy, prior resection site well healed. Cytology negative. Patient relieved. Continue q3-month surveillance. Next cystoscopy October.

25 y/o female new patient. Generally healthy. PMHx: iron deficiency anaemia (childhood), mild intermittent asthma. Meds: salbutamol PRN, ferrous sulphate 325mg daily. Allergies: sulfonamides (anaphylaxis). BP 110/68, HR 72, BMI 22.4. Labs: Hb 12.1, ferritin 28 (low-normal), TSH 2.4. Continue iron supplementation. Asthma well controlled — uses rescue inhaler <1x/month. Up to date on immunisations.

Patient presents for routine annual gynaecological exam. LMP 2 weeks ago, regular 28-day cycles. On combined OCP x4 years. Pap smear performed — results pending. Breast exam normal. Discussed HPV vaccination — completed series. No dysmenorrhoea on OCP. Continue current regimen.
Pap smear result: ASCUS with positive high-risk HPV. Colposcopy recommended. Discussed findings — likely low-grade changes given age. Patient anxious but reassured. Colposcopy scheduled in 2 weeks.

Colposcopy performed. Acetowhite area noted at 6 o'clock on cervix. Punch biopsy taken. No concerning vascular patterns. ECC not performed given age and low suspicion. Path pending. Patient tolerated procedure well.

Biopsy result: CIN 1 (low-grade cervical dysplasia). HPV-mediated changes likely to regress. Plan: observation with repeat co-testing in 12 months per ASCCP guidelines. No treatment indicated at this time. Patient counselled on natural history and excellent prognosis.

25 y/o female presenting with acute onset R flank pain radiating to groin x6 hours, nausea, and haematuria. Pain 9/10. Temp 37.2C, HR 92, BP 132/84. CVA tenderness R side. Urinalysis: RBC+++, WBC 5, nitrite negative. CT KUB: 5mm calculus at R ureterovesical junction with mild hydroureter. No hydronephrosis. IV ketorolac 30mg and ondansetron with significant pain relief. Urology consulted.

ED consult for R ureteric calculus 5mm at UVJ. Patient now comfortable post-analgesia. Given stone size and location, high likelihood of spontaneous passage. MET: tamsulosin 0.4mg daily x4 weeks. Strain urine for stone analysis. Increase fluid intake to >2.5L/day. If persistent pain, fever, or no passage in 4 weeks, will proceed with ureteroscopy. SULFA ALLERGY noted — avoid sulfonamide antibiotics if infection develops.

Follow-up renal calculus. Patient passed stone spontaneously day 10 — recovered and sent for analysis. Result: calcium oxalate monohydrate. 24-hour urine collection: hypercalciuria (320 mg/day), normal oxalate and citrate. Advised dietary modifications — reduce sodium, moderate calcium intake, increase citrate-rich foods. Adequate hydration crucial. No thiazide at this time. Recheck 24-hour urine in 6 months.

Annual visit. Kidney stone resolved, ferritin improving to 42 on iron supplementation. Hb 12.8. Asthma well controlled. Discussed discontinuing OCP as patient considering pregnancy in next 1-2 years. Transitioned to prenatal vitamins with folate 800mcg. Pre-conception counselling provided. Rubella immune, varicella immune. Sulfa allergy documented prominently.

12-month follow-up colposcopy and co-testing for CIN 1. Pap: negative for intraepithelial lesion. HPV: negative. CIN 1 has regressed as expected. Return to routine screening per age-appropriate guidelines. Patient relieved. Discussed fertility plans — OCP discontinued, cycles regular.

Patient presents with positive home pregnancy test. LMP 6 weeks ago. Urine hCG positive in office. Transvaginal US: intrauterine pregnancy, CRL consistent with 6w2d, fetal cardiac activity present. EDD: 7 December 2023. Prenatal labs ordered: CBC, blood type, antibody screen, rubella, hepatitis B, HIV, syphilis, urinalysis. Initiated prenatal care. Discussed first trimester screening options.

14-week prenatal visit. NT scan normal, combined first trimester screen low risk (1:8500 for T21). Prenatal labs all normal — blood type O positive, rubella immune, Hb 11.8, platelets 210. Asthma stable — continued salbutamol PRN, no controller needed. BP 108/66. FHR 156 bpm on doppler. Weight gain appropriate. Iron supplementation continued given Hx of IDA.

24-week visit. Anatomy scan at 20 weeks was normal. GDM screening today — 1-hour glucose challenge 142 mg/dL (elevated). Proceeding to 3-hour GTT. BP 112/70, no proteinuria. Fundal height 24cm. FHR 148. Patient feeling well, good fetal movements. Hb 11.2 — borderline, increased ferrous sulphate to BID.

3-hour GTT results: fasting 88, 1hr 196, 2hr 168, 3hr 132. Two abnormal values — diagnostic for gestational diabetes. Referred to diabetes educator and dietitian. Started SMBG QID. Dietary management first line. If fasting BG >95 or 2hr postprandial >120 despite diet x2 weeks, will initiate insulin. Metformin considered but patient prefers insulin if needed.

Referral for GDM management at 30 weeks. Patient on dietary management x6 weeks. SMBG log: fasting consistently 92-98, postprandial values mostly at target except occasional spikes to 130-140 after dinner. HbA1c 5.4%. Initiated bedtime NPH insulin 10 units to address fasting values. Continue diet for postprandial control. Growth scan ordered — no macrosomia on prior US. Close monitoring until delivery.

36-week visit. GDM well controlled on NPH insulin 14 units at bedtime, fasting BG 82-90. Growth scan: EFW 2.8kg, 55th percentile, normal AFI, normal doppler. Vertex presentation. BP 118/74. GBS swab taken. Discussed delivery plan — induction at 39 weeks if GDM remains insulin-requiring. Antenatal corticosteroids not indicated given gestational age.

Induction of labour at 39+1 weeks for insulin-requiring GDM. Cervix 2cm/50%/-2 — Foley bulb placed followed by oxytocin augmentation. Progressed to complete dilation over 14 hours. Normal vaginal delivery of live male infant, 3.35kg, Apgar 9/9. No perinatal complications. EBL 350mL. Neonatal BG monitoring — initial glucose 52, stable. Insulin discontinued post-delivery. SMBG to continue 48 hours post-partum. 6-week post-partum GTT planned.

6-week post-partum visit. Recovering well, breastfeeding established. GTT results: fasting 84, 2-hour 118 — normal glucose tolerance. GDM resolved. Counselled on 50% lifetime risk of T2DM — annual HbA1c screening recommended. Mood screening: Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale 4/30 — normal range. Discussed contraception — started POP (norethisterone) given breastfeeding. Perineum healed well.

67 y/o male with PMHx of T2DM x15 years, HTN, peripheral neuropathy, and CKD stage 3a (eGFR 52). Current meds: insulin glargine 28 units at bedtime, metformin 1000mg BID (recently held per nephrology), lisinopril 40mg, amlodipine 10mg, gabapentin 300mg TID. Allergies: ACE inhibitor cough — tolerating lisinopril well currently. BP 140/86, HR 74. HbA1c 8.1% — suboptimal. Discussed adding GLP-1 RA given renal and cardiovascular benefit.

Referral for T2DM optimisation with CKD. HbA1c 8.1% on glargine 28u + metformin (held). eGFR 52. Initiated semaglutide 0.25mg SC weekly, titrating to 0.5mg at 4 weeks. Continued glargine — may reduce dose once semaglutide titrated. Discussed GI side effects. Target HbA1c <7.5% given comorbidities. Metformin: can restart at 500mg BID if eGFR remains >45.

Follow-up. On semaglutide 0.5mg weekly x3 months. HbA1c improved to 7.4%. Weight down 4kg. Mild nausea initially, resolved. Glargine reduced to 22 units. Restarted metformin 500mg BID — eGFR stable at 50. SMBG: fasting BG 110-130. Titrate semaglutide to 1mg weekly. Renal function monitoring ongoing.

Annual nephrology review. CKD 3a — eGFR 48, Cr 1.5. UACR 180 mg/g — moderate albuminuria, worsened from 120 last year. On max dose lisinopril. Added dapagliflozin 10mg daily for renal protection — also synergistic with DM management. Discussed expected initial dip in eGFR. Avoid NSAIDs. Monitoring Cr and K+ in 2 weeks.

2-week labs post-dapagliflozin initiation. Cr 1.6 (from 1.5), eGFR 45. Expected haemodynamic dip. K+ 4.8 — acceptable. Continue dapagliflozin. Recheck in 3 months. Patient reports mild increase in urinary frequency — expected with SGLT2i.

Annual comprehensive. BP 134/80 on lisinopril/amlodipine. HbA1c 7.1% — well improved on semaglutide 1mg + glargine 20u + metformin 500mg BID + dapagliflozin 10mg. Weight down 7kg total. eGFR 47, UACR 140 — improved. Peripheral neuropathy stable on gabapentin 300mg TID — monofilament exam shows decreased sensation bilateral feet. Foot care education reinforced. Annual dilated eye exam due.

Annual diabetic eye exam. Known moderate NPDR bilaterally, stable from last year. No macular oedema on OCT. Visual acuity 20/30 R, 20/25 L. IOP 18/19 — normal. Recommend continued glycaemic and BP optimisation. Follow-up 6 months given NPDR severity.

69 y/o male referred for pre-operative cardiac assessment — considering elective R inguinal hernia repair. PMHx: T2DM, HTN, CKD 3. ECG: LVH, no ischaemic changes. Echo: EF 50%, mild concentric LVH, grade 1 diastolic dysfunction. No regional wall motion abnormalities. Stress test not indicated — functional capacity >4 METs. Cleared for surgery with moderate cardiac risk. Optimise BP pre-op.

Elective laparoscopic R inguinal hernia repair. Reducible indirect hernia confirmed. Mesh repair (Lichtenstein modified laparoscopic). Procedure uncomplicated, 50 minutes. Discharged same day. Metformin held morning of surgery, resume tomorrow. Insulin glargine given at half dose pre-op. Post-op: paracetamol and tramadol PRN. Lifting restriction 6 weeks.

Referral for worsening peripheral neuropathy despite gabapentin 300mg TID. EMG/NCS: moderate sensorimotor axonal polyneuropathy, length-dependent. Consistent with diabetic neuropathy. B12 level normal. Gabapentin increased to 600mg TID with slow titration. Discussed duloxetine as alternative/adjunct if gabapentin insufficient. Capsaicin cream for localised pain. Fall risk counselled.

Follow-up multiple chronic conditions. HbA1c 7.0% — at target. eGFR 44, UACR 125 — albuminuria improving on dapagliflozin. BP 130/78. Neuropathy somewhat improved on gabapentin 600mg TID — pain 4/10 from 7/10. Hernia repair site healed. Weight stable. Comprehensive metabolic panel reviewed. Continue all current medications. Shingrix #2 given.

6-month diabetic eye exam. NPDR stable bilaterally, no progression to proliferative disease. No clinically significant macular oedema. OCT: mild central foveal thickening R eye — 290 microns, borderline. Will monitor closely. Visual acuity stable. Continue current management, return 6 months.

CKD progressing — eGFR now 38 (stage 3b). Cr 1.8. UACR 160, slight uptick. K+ 5.1 on lisinopril + dapagliflozin. Metformin discontinued — eGFR below threshold for continued use. Continue dapagliflozin and lisinopril but monitor K+ closely. Discussed CKD trajectory, renal diet counselling referral. If eGFR <30, will discuss AV fistula planning.

Diabetes management update. Metformin stopped per nephrology. HbA1c drifted to 7.6%. Currently on semaglutide 1mg weekly + glargine 20u + dapagliflozin. Increased glargine to 26 units. Added insulin aspart 4 units with largest meal — initiating basal-bolus transition. SMBG log reviewed. Hypoglycaemia awareness intact. Recheck HbA1c 3 months.

71 y/o annual review. Complex medication regimen. HbA1c 7.3% on basal-bolus insulin + semaglutide + dapagliflozin. CKD 3b stable — eGFR 36. BP 132/76. Neuropathy pain managed. NPDR stable. Discussed advance care planning given progressive CKD. Geriatric pharmacist review arranged for polypharmacy optimisation. Flu and COVID vaccines administered.

eGFR declining — now 30. Cr 2.1. Entering CKD stage 4. K+ 5.3 — started patiromer 8.4g daily. Discussed long-term renal replacement therapy options. Patient prefers peritoneal dialysis if needed. Referred for PD catheter evaluation when eGFR approaches 15-20. Dapagliflozin continued for residual benefit. Erythropoietin assessment: Hb 10.2, ferritin 180, TSAT 22% — started epoetin alfa 4000 units SC weekly.

CKD 4 follow-up. 73 y/o male, T2DM x ~22 years (diagnosed 2004) on insulin glargine 26 units + aspart 4 units with largest meal and semaglutide 1mg weekly; metformin stopped Jan 2023. Dapagliflozin 10mg continued (since Mar 2020). Lisinopril 40mg daily, long-term (since before 2019); amlodipine 10mg. No MRA. Patiromer 8.4g daily since May 2024. Epoetin alfa 4000 units weekly. BP 134/78. Labs 16 Feb: Cr 2.8, eGFR 23 (30 in May 2024), K 4.7, HbA1c 7.2%, Hb 10.8. UACR 212 mg/g. Assessment: diabetic kidney disease, CKD stage 4 A2, progressing ~3.5 mL/min/yr. Not on dialysis. Modality education completed — patient still prefers peritoneal dialysis; PD catheter surgical assessment booked. Continue dapagliflozin and lisinopril while tolerated. Renal diet reinforced. Recheck bloods in 3 months.

34 y/o female presenting with fatigue and weight gain x6 months. PMHx: depression (on escitalopram 10mg). BP 118/72, HR 58, BMI 26.8. Exam: dry skin, mild periorbital puffiness, delayed relaxation phase of ankle reflexes bilaterally. Clinical suspicion for hypothyroidism. Labs ordered: TSH, free T4, CBC, CMP, lipid panel.

Lab results: TSH 42 mIU/L (markedly elevated), free T4 0.4 ng/dL (low). Anti-TPO antibodies strongly positive at 480 IU/mL. Diagnosis: Hashimoto's thyroiditis with overt hypothyroidism. Started levothyroxine 75mcg daily on empty stomach, 30 min before breakfast. Recheck TSH in 6 weeks. Lipids: LDL 168 — likely secondary to hypothyroidism, recheck after euthyroid.

6-week thyroid recheck. TSH 12.4 — improving but still elevated. Free T4 0.8. Patient reports some improvement in energy but still fatigued. Increased levothyroxine to 100mcg daily. Discussed medication interactions — take separately from calcium, iron, and coffee. Recheck 6 weeks.

TSH now 4.8, free T4 1.1 — approaching target. Energy significantly improved, skin less dry, weight down 3 lbs. Continue levothyroxine 100mcg. Repeat lipids: LDL 132 — improved with thyroid normalisation. Will recheck TSH in 3 months to confirm stability. Depression also improved — escitalopram continued.

TSH 2.8 — euthyroid on levothyroxine 100mcg. Patient feeling well, energy back to baseline. Weight stable. LDL 124. Discussed long-term nature of levothyroxine therapy. Annual TSH monitoring sufficient now that stable. Escitalopram — discussed taper with patient; prefers to continue for now. RTC 1 year.

Patient referred for evaluation of multiple pigmented lesions. FHx: sister with melanoma at age 40. Total body skin exam performed. >50 naevi noted, mostly typical. One atypical lesion on L upper back — 7mm, asymmetric, irregular border, colour variegation. Excisional biopsy performed. Remaining naevi photographed for baseline digital dermoscopy. Annual surveillance recommended given FHx.

Biopsy result L upper back: moderately dysplastic compound naevus with clear margins. No melanoma. Reassuring result but given degree of atypia and FHx, re-excision with 5mm margins recommended as precaution. Scheduled for minor procedure next week. Continue annual total body skin checks.

Annual visit. TSH 3.1 on levothyroxine 100mcg — stable. Feeling well. BMI 25.4 — improved. Escitalopram 10mg continued. Naevus re-excision healed well per dermatology. BP 116/70. Routine labs normal. Discussed smoking status — never smoker. Alcohol: social. Preventive care: Pap smear due, referred to gynae.

36 y/o female referred for recurrent headaches x1 year. Unilateral throbbing, L temporal, with photophobia, nausea, occasionally preceded by visual aura (scintillating scotoma x20 min). 3-4 episodes/month, lasting 8-24 hours. Triggers: stress, menstruation, wine. Exam: neuro exam normal. Dx: migraine with aura. Started sumatriptan 50mg PRN for acute attacks. Given frequency, discussed prophylaxis — started propranolol 40mg BID. Contraindicated for triptans + ergotamines simultaneously.

Migraine follow-up. Propranolol 40mg BID x3 months. Frequency reduced from 4 to 1.5 episodes/month. Sumatriptan effective for acute attacks. No aura in past 6 weeks. BP on propranolol 108/66, HR 56 — tolerating well. MRI brain ordered given new-onset migraines with aura to exclude secondary cause — anticipate normal. Continue current regimen.

MRI brain with and without contrast: normal. No structural abnormality, no white matter lesions, no AVM. Reassuring. Continue migraine prophylaxis with propranolol. Discussed combined OCP contraindication with migraine with aura — patient currently not on OCP, but important for future reference. Follow-up 6 months or PRN.

Annual visit. Hypothyroidism stable — TSH 2.9 on levothyroxine 100mcg. Migraines well controlled on propranolol. Escitalopram tapered and discontinued 2 months ago — mood stable. Dermatology: annual skin check normal, no new atypical naevi. BP 110/68. All preventive care up to date. Well-managed patient.

38 y/o female presenting for pre-conception counselling. PMHx: Hashimoto's on levothyroxine, migraine with aura on propranolol, Hx of depression. Wishes to conceive in next 6 months. Plan: check TSH — may need levothyroxine dose increase in pregnancy. Propranolol: compatible with pregnancy but switch from sumatriptan to paracetamol for acute migraine — triptans category C. Folic acid 400mcg started. Discussed age-related fertility considerations.

Pre-conception check. TSH 3.4 on levothyroxine 100mcg — increased to 112mcg given increased requirement in early pregnancy. Will recheck TSH q4 weeks once pregnant. Propranolol continued. Folic acid ongoing. Labs: rubella immune, varicella immune, Hb 13.2, ferritin 48. Blood type A negative — anti-D prophylaxis will be needed. Cleared for conception.

58 y/o male presenting for executive health check. PMHx: gout (2 episodes), mild obesity. Meds: allopurinol 300mg daily. Allergies: NKDA. BP 148/92, HR 76, BMI 32.4. FHx: father died MI age 62, brother with T2DM. Labs: fasting glucose 112, HbA1c 6.1%, TC 248, LDL 162, HDL 38, TG 240, uric acid 7.2, Cr 1.1, eGFR 78. Significant cardiovascular risk profile. Started atorvastatin 40mg. Discussed HTN — lifestyle trial 3 months before pharmacotherapy. Weight loss critical.

3-month follow-up. BP 144/88 despite lifestyle changes — minimal weight loss (1kg). Started hydrochlorothiazide 25mg daily. Discussed HCTZ and gout risk — monitor uric acid, continue allopurinol. LDL on atorvastatin: 108 — improved. HbA1c 6.0%. Advised calorie-restricted diet, referred to dietitian. Structured exercise prescription: 150 min/week moderate intensity.

Follow-up. BP 136/84 on HCTZ 25mg. Weight down 3kg. Uric acid 6.8 — stable on allopurinol. No gout flares. Fasting glucose 108, HbA1c 5.9%. LDL 102. Improving but BP not yet at target. Added lisinopril 10mg. Continue atorvastatin 40mg. Patient engaging with dietitian. Encouraged continued progress.

Referral for cardiovascular risk assessment. Strong FHx and multiple risk factors. ASCVD 10-year risk 18%. Exercise stress test: achieved 10 METs, no ischaemic ST changes, appropriate hemodynamic response. Coronary artery calcium score: 185 (moderate). Recommend aggressive risk factor management. Aspirin 81mg daily added. Continue statin. BP target <130/80.

Annual review. BP 128/78 on lisinopril 10mg + HCTZ 25mg — at target. Weight down 5kg total, BMI 30.2. LDL 98, TG 180 — improved. HbA1c 5.8%. Gout stable. CAC score discussed — motivating for patient. Continue aspirin, atorvastatin, allopurinol, antihypertensives. Colorectal cancer screening due — colonoscopy ordered.

Screening colonoscopy for 60 y/o male. Prep good. Scope to caecum. Three polyps: 8mm sessile polyp ascending colon, 5mm pedunculated polyp sigmoid, 3mm polyp rectum. All removed — ascending by EMR, others by cold snare. No complications. Path pending. Anticipate 3-year surveillance given multiple polyps.

Pathology results: ascending colon — tubulovillous adenoma with low-grade dysplasia. Sigmoid — tubular adenoma. Rectum — hyperplastic polyp. Given advanced adenoma (tubulovillous), recommend surveillance colonoscopy in 3 years. No high-grade dysplasia. Discussed importance of adherence to surveillance schedule.

61 y/o male with acute R great toe pain, swelling, erythema x2 days. Known gout history. Exam: R 1st MTP joint erythematous, exquisitely tender, warm. Joint aspirate: negatively birefringent monosodium urate crystals, WBC 42000. No organisms on gram stain. Acute gout flare despite allopurinol. Treated with colchicine 1.2mg then 0.6mg one hour later. Short course prednisone 30mg taper over 5 days given NSAID relative contraindication with HTN. Allopurinol continued — do not stop during flare.

Post-gout flare follow-up. Flare resolved. Uric acid 6.4 — still above target of <6. HCTZ may be contributing. Discussed switching HCTZ to losartan (uricosuric properties) — lisinopril switched to losartan 50mg, HCTZ discontinued. Allopurinol increased to 400mg daily. BP will need monitoring on new regimen. Recheck uric acid and BP in 6 weeks.

Recheck. BP 132/82 on losartan 50mg alone — slightly above target. Uric acid 5.4 — at goal on allopurinol 400mg + losartan. Added amlodipine 5mg for BP optimisation. LDL 94 on atorvastatin 40mg. Weight stable. Patient reports improved dietary compliance. Continue current regimen.

Annual visit. BP 126/76 on losartan 50mg + amlodipine 5mg — at target. BMI 29.1, weight down 8kg total. LDL 90. HbA1c 5.7%. Uric acid 5.2, no gout flares x10 months. All metrics improving. Aspirin, atorvastatin, allopurinol, losartan, amlodipine — tolerating all well. PSA 2.1 — normal for age. Preventive care current.

62 y/o male referred for evaluation of progressive exertional dyspnoea x4 months. Non-smoker. No wheeze or cough. PFTs: FVC 72% predicted, FEV1 74% predicted, FEV1/FVC 0.82 — restrictive pattern. DLCO reduced at 58% predicted. HRCT chest: bilateral basilar reticular opacities, traction bronchiectasis, early honeycombing. Pattern highly suspicious for usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP). Autoimmune workup ordered. Pulmonary function to be monitored closely.

Autoimmune serologies all negative — ANA, RF, anti-CCP, anti-Scl-70, anti-Jo-1. Diagnosis: idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis based on UIP pattern on HRCT and exclusion of secondary causes. Discussed prognosis honestly with patient. Started nintedanib 150mg BID — antifibrotic to slow progression. Warned of diarrhoea as common side effect. Hepatic monitoring baseline LFTs normal. Pulmonary rehab referral. Supplemental O2 if desaturation on exertion.

3-month follow-up IPF on nintedanib. PFTs: FVC 70% — stable. Mild diarrhoea managed with loperamide PRN. LFTs normal. 6MWT: 380 metres, SpO2 nadir 89% — prescribed ambulatory O2 2L/min with exertion. Patient coping well emotionally. Discussed lung transplant evaluation if progressive decline — patient willing to consider. Referred to transplant centre for preliminary assessment.

6-month follow-up. FVC 67% — gradual decline despite nintedanib. DLCO 50%. Increasing O2 requirement — now using 2L at rest during activity, 3L with exertion. Transplant workup in progress — cardiology, nephrology, and psychosocial evaluations completed. BMI 28.5 — needs to be <30 for listing. Encouraged continued weight loss. GAD-7 score 8 — mild anxiety, referred to psycho-oncology/chronic illness support.

Comprehensive review. IPF progressing — FVC 65%, on nintedanib and O2. Transplant listing pending. CV risk well managed: BP 124/74, LDL 88, HbA1c 5.6%. Gout quiescent x2 years. BMI 28.2 — approaching transplant threshold. Medication reconciliation: 8 scheduled medications. Discussed palliative care involvement for symptom management alongside curative intent. Patient agrees. Colonoscopy surveillance due — scheduling with GI.

49 y/o female presenting with worsening bilateral hand joint stiffness and pain x4 months, predominantly in mornings lasting >1 hour. PMHx: migraines, seasonal allergies. Meds: sumatriptan PRN. Allergies: codeine (nausea). BP 122/74, HR 68, BMI 24.6. Exam: synovitis MCP joints 2-4 bilaterally, PIP joints 2-3 R hand. ESR 38, CRP 24. RF and anti-CCP ordered along with hand X-rays.

Urgent referral for suspected inflammatory arthritis. Labs: RF 86 (positive), anti-CCP 124 (strongly positive). X-rays: periarticular soft tissue swelling, no erosions yet. DAS28-CRP: 4.6 (moderate disease activity). Diagnosis: seropositive rheumatoid arthritis. Baseline labs for DMARD initiation: LFTs, CBC, hepatitis B/C, CXR — all normal. Started methotrexate 15mg PO weekly with folic acid 5mg the next day. Bridging prednisone 10mg daily taper over 6 weeks.

12-week follow-up RA on methotrexate 15mg weekly. Morning stiffness reduced to 20 minutes. DAS28-CRP 3.4 — improved but not in remission. Prednisone tapered off. LFTs and CBC normal. Tolerating MTX well — mild fatigue day after dosing. Increased MTX to 20mg weekly. Target: DAS28 <2.6. Recheck 8 weeks.

RA follow-up on MTX 20mg weekly. DAS28-CRP 2.4 — remission achieved. Excellent response. Minimal residual synovitis. Grip strength improved bilaterally. LFTs stable. Continue MTX 20mg weekly. Introduced hydroxychloroquine 200mg BID as combination DMARD therapy for sustained remission. Ophthalmology baseline exam for HCQ toxicity screening ordered.

Baseline eye exam prior to hydroxychloroquine therapy. Visual acuity 20/20 bilaterally. Slit lamp: anterior segments normal. Fundoscopy: normal maculae, no retinal changes. OCT macular thickness within normal limits. Humphrey 10-2 visual fields: full. Clear baseline. Recommend annual screening after 5 years of HCQ use, or earlier if risk factors develop.

Annual visit. RA in remission on MTX 20mg + HCQ 200mg BID. Reports new symptoms: hot flushes, irregular menses, mood lability x3 months. Last menstrual period 6 weeks ago. FSH 48 mIU/mL — menopausal range. Diagnosis: perimenopause. Discussed HRT risks and benefits given age 50. Patient interested in trial of low-dose transdermal oestradiol. No contraindications identified — no Hx of VTE, breast cancer. Started 25mcg oestradiol patch + micronised progesterone 100mg cyclical.

Follow-up perimenopause on HRT. Hot flushes reduced by 80%. Sleep improved. Mood more stable. No vaginal bleeding. BP 120/72. Breast exam normal. Continue HRT. Annual mammogram scheduled. RA stable on DMARDs. Migraine frequency unchanged at 1-2/month.

Annual RA review. DAS28-CRP 2.2 — sustained remission x18 months. No joint swelling, minimal morning stiffness. X-rays hands: no new erosions, stable from baseline. LFTs normal, CBC stable. Discussed potential MTX dose reduction — patient prefers to maintain current dose given excellent control. Continue MTX 20mg + HCQ 200mg BID.

diarrhoea and vomiting (several family members affected), and reduced urine
output for 2 days. He continued his losartan and metformin and took
over-the-counter ibuprofen 400 mg three times daily for 3 days for abdominal
cramps and headache. PMH (followed by his internist, Dr Liu): hypertension, type
2 diabetes (HbA1c 6.0% in 2023), gout (no flares since 2019), hyperlipidaemia,
previous right shoulder impingement. Baseline creatinine about 95 µmol/L.

Allergies: codeine (nausea).

O/E 10:30: temp 37.4°C, HR 104, BP 98/58, RR 18, SpO2 97% on air. Dry mucous
membranes, capillary refill 3 s. Abdomen soft, mildly tender, active bowel
sounds. Pain NRS 3/10 (abdominal cramps).

Bloods 10:40: creatinine 398 µmol/L (eGFR 14), urea 31.2 mmol/L, potassium 5.9,
sodium 133, bicarbonate 17, lactate 2.1, glucose 7.4, CRP 18, Hb 15.9. Urine
sodium 14 mmol/L; dipstick trace protein only. ECG 10:50: sinus tachycardia 104,
no hyperkalaemic changes.

Impression: AKI stage 3 (creatinine > 3x baseline), prerenal from volume
depletion with viral gastroenteritis, aggravated by angiotensin-receptor blocker
and NSAID; hyperkalaemia without ECG changes.

Plan: 0.9% sodium chloride 1 L over 1 h, then 1 L 4-hourly with review of volume
status; urine output monitoring (urinal, target > 0.5 mL/kg/h); stool sample for
viral PCR; side room with contact precautions. Losartan, ibuprofen and metformin
withheld; amlodipine held (BP 98/58); allopurinol held for now. Repeat potassium
at 20:00. Renal ultrasound and nephrology review.

VTE risk assessment 13:30: increased risk (acute illness, reduced mobility);
eGFR 14 — unfractionated heparin 5,000 units subcutaneously 12-hourly rather
than enoxaparin.

Medication reconciliation 13:40 by Dr Vermeersch with clinical pharmacist M.
Hendrickx, using the patient, his wife and the community pharmacy record:
losartan 100 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, metformin 1,000 mg daily,
atorvastatin 20 mg daily, allopurinol 400 mg daily, famotidine 20 mg as needed,
plus ibuprofen 400 mg three times daily (over the counter, 3 days).

Admitted to Ward 12 (Acute Medical Unit) under Dr Menon at 15:00.

Pressure-injury risk: Braden score 20 — not at risk; skin intact.

Pain NRS 3/10 (abdominal cramps).

Strict fluid balance: 4 loose stools and 1 vomit today before admission to the

RADIOLOGY REPORT — Renal tract ultrasound

Date: 02/09/2025, 09:30. Clinical details: AKI stage 3 after gastroenteritis, on
ARB and NSAID.

Findings: Right kidney 11.2 cm, left kidney 11.0 cm, normal cortical thickness
and corticomedullary differentiation. No hydronephrosis, calculus or mass.
Bladder partially filled, smooth wall; prostate mildly enlarged (32 mL).

Impression: Normal-sized unobstructed kidneys. No evidence of chronic kidney

CONSULTATION — Nephrology

64-year-old man with AKI stage 3 (creatinine 398 µmol/L on 01/09, baseline about
95) after 4 days of diarrhoea and vomiting while taking losartan and
over-the-counter ibuprofen. Stool PCR positive for norovirus GII.

Today: clinically euvolaemic after 5 L of IV fluid, BP 122/74, urine output 1.1
mL/kg/h overnight. Creatinine 352, potassium 5.1, bicarbonate 19. Urine sodium
14 mmol/L on admission, bland urine dipstick, normal renal ultrasound.

Impression: Prerenal AKI from volume depletion, compounded by haemodynamic
effects of the ARB and NSAID; already recovering. No indication for renal
replacement therapy (no refractory hyperkalaemia, acidosis or fluid overload).

Advice: continue IV fluids guided by volume status, reduce as oral intake
improves. Keep losartan and all NSAIDs off; restart losartan only once
creatinine is within 20% of baseline. Metformin can restart when eating and eGFR
> 30 (maximum 1,000 mg/day while eGFR 30-45). Allopurinol at a reduced dose of
100 mg daily while eGFR < 30, then increase. Daily U&E. Sick-day rules (pause
metformin, ARB and diuretics during vomiting or diarrhoea) to be taught before
discharge. No nephrology follow-up needed if creatinine returns to baseline.

DISCHARGE LETTER

Patient: James Okafor (64M)
Admitted: 01/09/2025   Discharged: 07/09/2025   Ward 12 (Acute Medical Unit), 6 bed-days.
Admission route: Emergency Department
Discharge destination: Home

Reason for admission: Acute kidney injury stage 3 with hyperkalaemia after
gastroenteritis.

Hospital course: Four days of diarrhoea and vomiting (norovirus GII on stool
PCR) while continuing losartan and taking over-the-counter ibuprofen. On arrival
he was hypotensive and dry, with creatinine 398 µmol/L (baseline about 95, eGFR
14), urea 31.2 mmol/L and potassium 5.9 mmol/L without ECG changes. Losartan,
ibuprofen, metformin, amlodipine and allopurinol were withheld and he received
IV fluids. Renal ultrasound was normal and the nephrology team (Dr Yusuf)
confirmed prerenal AKI with no need for dialysis. Diarrhoea settled by 03/09.
Creatinine fell steadily: 352 (02/09), 281 (03/09), 214 (04/09), 168 (05/09) and
132 µmol/L (eGFR 52) on 07/09; potassium normalised to 4.4-4.6 mmol/L.
Amlodipine was restarted on 04/09 (BP 136/80), allopurinol at 100 mg on 05/09
and metformin on 06/09 once eating normally. No gout flare. Sick-day rules were
explained to him and his wife.

Discharge diagnoses: Acute kidney injury stage 3, prerenal, due to volume
depletion from norovirus gastroenteritis with angiotensin-receptor blocker
(losartan) and NSAID (ibuprofen) use — recovering; hyperkalaemia (resolved);
norovirus gastroenteritis; hypertension; type 2 diabetes mellitus; gout;
hyperlipidaemia.

Discharge medications: Amlodipine 5 mg daily; metformin 1,000 mg daily;
atorvastatin 20 mg daily; allopurinol 100 mg daily (reduced from 400 mg — to be
increased as renal function recovers); famotidine 20 mg as needed. Withheld:
losartan until creatinine is within 20% of baseline. Stopped: ibuprofen — avoid
all NSAIDs.

Follow-up: Dr Liu (internal medicine) in 1 week with U&E, to restart losartan
and re-titrate allopurinol towards 400 mg when creatinine is back near 95
µmol/L. Pause metformin and losartan during future vomiting or diarrhoea.

CHF follow-up. 80 y/o female with HFpEF. NYHA class II, stable. Echo: LVEF 55%, grade II diastolic dysfunction, moderate LA enlargement. BNP 310. No recent hospitalizations. K recheck: 4.9, improved with lisinopril dose reduction. Continue spironolactone 12.5mg with close monitoring. Cr 1.7, stable. BP 132/70, acceptable given CKD. Continue current regimen. Monthly K and Cr monitoring.

6-month visit. 80 y/o female, multiple comorbidities. Weight 156, up 2 lbs. Mild edema recurring. BNP 340. K 5.0. eGFR 30. HbA1c 7.0% on sitagliptin. TSH 2.8. Increase furosemide to 80mg daily. Continue spironolactone. Discussed advance care planning; patient has healthcare proxy but no living will. Encouraged completion. Flu vaccine given.

81 y/o female presenting with worsening dyspnea x 3 days, orthopnea, and 6 lb weight gain over 1 week. Hx HFpEF, CKD. BP 158/88, HR 92, SpO2 90% RA, RR 26. Exam: JVD, bilateral crackles to mid-lung fields, 3+ pedal edema. BNP 1240. CXR: bilateral pleural effusions, pulmonary edema. Cr 2.1 (baseline 1.7). K 5.4. Troponin <0.01. ECG: sinus tach, LVH. Inpatient CHF management, day 3. Aggressive diuresis with IV furosemide drip, net negative 4L. Weight down to 152 from 162 on admission. SpO2 96% RA. Crackles clearing. Edema improved to 1+. Cr peaked at 2.3 (cardiorenal syndrome), now 2.0. K 4.7 after correction. BNP 680, trending down. Transitioned to oral furosemide 80mg BID. Hold spironolactone given AKI. CKD follow-up post-CHF exacerbation. eGFR 28, declined from 30 pre-hospitalization. Cr 1.9. Hgb 9.8, CKD anemia progressing. Ferritin 55, TSAT 16%. Start IV iron sucrose 200mg x 5 doses. 82 y/o female. Telehealth visit. Weight 150, stable. No CHF symptoms. Taking furosemide 80mg BID faithfully. Cr 2.0, eGFR 26 (CKD stage 4). Hgb 10.2 after IV iron course. HbA1c 7.3%, rising. 84 y/o female, annual review. CKD stage 4-5 (eGFR 18), conservative management chosen. CHF stable. T2DM controlled. Palliative care team involved. Hgb 9.8. BNP 380. New patient. 27 y/o male presenting with persistent low back pain x 4 months, morning stiffness lasting >1 hour, improving with activity. No trauma. PMH: unremarkable. No medications. NKDA. Family hx: father with psoriasis. Nonsmoker. BP 120/72, HR 68, BMI 24.0. Exam: limited lumbar flexion, bilateral sacroiliac tenderness. Schober test 3cm (reduced). Neurological exam intact. Suspect inflammatory back pain. Labs: ESR 28, CRP 1.8, HLA-B27 ordered. X-ray lumbar spine and SI joints ordered.

Results review. HLA-B27 positive. X-ray SI joints: bilateral sacroiliitis grade 2. Lumbar spine: mild squaring of vertebral bodies. Consistent with ankylosing spondylitis. Start naproxen 500mg BID with food. Refer to rheumatology for confirmation and management. PT referral for spinal mobility program.

Referral for suspected ankylosing spondylitis. 27 y/o HLA-B27+ male with inflammatory back pain, bilateral sacroiliitis on X-ray, morning stiffness >1 hour. Meets modified NY criteria. MRI SI joints ordered to assess active inflammation. BASDAI score 6.2 (high). Continue naproxen. If NSAID response inadequate at 4 weeks, will consider TNF inhibitor. Baseline labs: CBC normal, CMP normal, hepatitis B/C negative, TB QuantiFERON negative. Discussed disease course, importance of exercise and posture.

MRI SI joints: bilateral active sacroiliitis with bone marrow edema. Confirms axial spondyloarthritis with active inflammation. Naproxen partially effective, BASDAI 4.8, still moderate. Given young age and active disease, initiate adalimumab 40mg SC every 2 weeks. Prior authorization submitted. TB and hepatitis screening negative. Continue naproxen until biologic takes effect. RTC 12 weeks.

12-week follow-up on adalimumab. Dramatic improvement. Morning stiffness reduced to 15 minutes. BASDAI 2.1. CRP 0.4 (normalized). Pain significantly reduced, able to exercise regularly. Tolerating injections well, no injection site reactions. Discontinued naproxen. Continue adalimumab. PT going well, improved spinal mobility. RTC 4 months.

Routine AS follow-up. Continued improvement on adalimumab. BASDAI 1.8. No extra-articular manifestations (no uveitis, no IBD symptoms, no psoriasis). CRP 0.3. Exercising 4x/week with swimming and yoga. Fully functional at work as software engineer. Continue adalimumab. Annual ophthalmology screening for uveitis. RTC 6 months.

Annual screening for uveitis in setting of ankylosing spondylitis. Patient asymptomatic. VA 20/20 OU. Slit lamp: quiet anterior chambers bilaterally, no cells or flare. IOP normal. Fundoscopy unremarkable. No evidence of uveitis. Continue annual monitoring. Educate on symptoms: red eye, pain, photophobia, blurred vision - present urgently if these develop.

Urgent ophthalmology follow-up tomorrow. Contacted rheumatology.

Urgent follow-up acute anterior uveitis OD. On prednisolone q1h and cyclopentolate. Cells reduced to 1+. VA 20/25 OD. Continue current drops. Taper prednisolone: q2h x 3 days, then QID x 1 week, then BID x 1 week, then daily x 1 week, then stop. IOP monitoring throughout. First episode of uveitis in known AS. Discussed with rheumatology re: adalimumab dose optimization. RTC 3 days.

Uveitis follow-up 3 weeks. Anterior chamber quiet, no cells. VA 20/20 OD recovered. Completing prednisolone taper. No posterior segment involvement. Episode resolved without complications. Monitor closely for recurrence. Coordinate with rheumatology.

Post-uveitis flare discussion. First episode of AAU despite adalimumab. AS otherwise well controlled, BASDAI 2.0. Literature supports adalimumab for uveitis prevention, but breakthrough can occur. Continue adalimumab at current dose. If recurrent uveitis (>2 episodes/year), consider switching to infliximab which may have superior uveitis prevention. Monitor closely. Continue regular eye exams every 6 months.
6-month AS follow-up. No recurrence of uveitis. BASDAI 1.5. CRP 0.2. Spinal mobility maintained. No new symptoms. Continue adalimumab. Flu and COVID vaccines given (safe on biologic). RTC 6 months.

Routine follow-up. AS well controlled. BASDAI 1.6. No uveitis recurrence. Patient inquiring about long-term prognosis and family planning (partner is pregnant). Discussed: AS has genetic component (HLA-B27), ~10-20% risk of offspring developing SpA. No need for genetic testing of offspring. Disease well managed with current therapy. Continue adalimumab. RTC 6 months.

Referred by rheumatology. 30 y/o male with AS on adalimumab now developing scaly plaques on elbows and scalp x 2 months. Adalimumab should also help psoriasis. RTC 6 weeks.

Psoriasis follow-up. Elbows improved significantly with clobetasol. Scalp clearing with calcipotriene/betamethasone foam. BSA <1%. Reduce to maintenance: clobetasol BID weekends only to elbows, scalp foam twice weekly. Moisturize liberally. Adalimumab providing systemic benefit. Satisfied with results. RTC 3 months or PRN.

Annual comprehensive AS review. 31 y/o male on adalimumab x 3.5 years. BASDAI 1.4, low disease activity. CRP 0.2. No uveitis recurrence. Psoriasis well controlled with topical + biologic. Spinal X-ray: no progression, no syndesmophytes. Excellent functional status, exercising regularly. Continue adalimumab. Transition to annual visits if stable. Comprehensive labs normal. No hepatotoxicity or cytopenias on biologic.
